class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup></td>\n<td>11,562</td>\n<td>10%\n</td></tr></tbody></table>\n</td></tr></tbody></table>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Health">Health</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Hispanic_and_Latino_Americans&amp;action=edit&amp;section=19" title="Edit section: Health"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Longevity">Longevity</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Hispanic_and_Latino_Americans&amp;action=edit&amp;section=20" title="Edit section: Longevity"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-right" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Sobrato_Pavilion_at_the_Valley_Medical_Center_1643_(cropped).jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/ac/Sobrato_Pavilion_at_the_Valley_Medical_Center_1643_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-Sobrato_Pavilion_at_the_Valley_Medical_Center_1643_%28cropped%29.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="114" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/ac/Sobrato_Pavilion_at_the_Valley_Medical_Center_1643_%28cropped%29.jpg/500px-Sobrato_Pavilion_at_the_Valley_Medical_Center_1643_%28cropped%29.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="4032" data-file-height="1836" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Santa_Clara_Valley_Medical_Center" title="Santa Clara Valley Medical Center">Santa Clara Valley Medical Center</a> in San Jose, California.</figcaption></figure>\n<p>As of 2016, life expectancy for Hispanic Americans is 81.8 years, which is higher than the life expectancy for White Americans (78.6 years).<sup id="cite&#95;ref-131" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-131"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>129<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Research on the "<a href="/wiki/Hispanic_paradox" title="Hispanic paradox">Hispanic paradox</a>"—the well-established apparent mortality advantage of Hispanic Americans compared to White Americans, despite the latter\'s more advantaged socioeconomic status—has been principally explained by "(1) health-related migration to and from the US; and (2) social and cultural protection mechanisms, such as maintenance of healthy lifestyles and behaviors adopted in the countries of origin, and availability of extensive social networks in the US."<sup id="cite&#95;ref-Goldman&#95;132-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Goldman-132"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>130<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> The "salmon bias" hypothesis, which suggests that the Hispanic health advantage is attributable to higher rates of <a href="/wiki/Repatriation" title="Repatriation">return migration</a> among less-healthy migrants, has received some support in the scholarly literature.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-133" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-133"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>131<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> A 2019 study, examining the comparatively better health of foreign-born American Hispanics, challenged the hypothesis that a stronger orientation toward the family (<a href="/wiki/Familism" class="mw-redirect" title="Familism">familism</a>) contributed to this advantage.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-134" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-134"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>132<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Some scholars have suggested that the Hispanic mortality advantage is likely to disappear due to the higher rates of <a href="/wiki/Obesity" title="Obesity">obesity</a> and <a href="/wiki/Diabetes" title="Diabetes">diabetes</a> among Hispanics relative to White people, although lower rates of smoking (and thus <a href="/wiki/Health_effects_of_tobacco" title="Health effects of tobacco">smoking-attributable mortality</a>) among Hispanics may counteract this to some extent.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-Goldman&#95;132-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Goldman-132"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>130<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>As the <a href="/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_the_United_States" title="COVID-19 pandemic in the United States">COVID-19 coronavirus</a> spread throughout the United States, disproportionate numbers of cases have been observed among <a href="/wiki/Black_people" title="Black people">Black</a> and <a href="/wiki/Hispanic" title="Hispanic">Hispanic</a> populations.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-135" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-135"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>133<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-136" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-136"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>134<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-137" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-137"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>135<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Healthcare">Healthcare</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Hispanic_and_Latino_Americans&amp;action=edit&amp;section=21" title="Edit section: Healthcare"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-left" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Memorial-hermann-hospital.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8c/Memorial-hermann-hospital.jpg/250px-Memorial-hermann-hospital.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="188" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8c/Memorial-hermann-hospital.jpg/500px-Memorial-hermann-hospital.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="1024" data-file-height="768" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Memorial_Hermann%E2%80%93Texas_Medical_Center" title="Memorial Hermann–Texas Medical Center">Memorial Hermann–Texas Medical Center</a> in Houston, Texas.</figcaption></figure>\n<p>As of 2017, about 19% of Hispanic Americans <a href="/wiki/Health_insurance_coverage_in_the_United_States" title="Health insurance coverage in the United States">lack health insurance coverage</a>, which is the highest of all ethnic groups except for Indigenous Americans and Alaska Natives.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-KFFCoverage&#95;138-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-KFFCoverage-138"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>136<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> In terms of extending health coverage, Hispanics benefited the most among US ethnic groups from the <a href="/wiki/Affordable_Care_Act" title="Affordable Care Act">Affordable Care Act</a> (ACA); among non-elderly Hispanics, the uninsured rate declined from 26.7% in 2013 to 14.2% in 2017.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-KFFCoverage&#95;138-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-KFFCoverage-138"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>136<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Among the population of non-elderly uninsured Hispanic population in 2017, about 53% were non-citizens, about 39% were US-born citizens, and about 9% were naturalized citizens.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-KFFCoverage&#95;138-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-KFFCoverage-138"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>136<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> (The ACA does not help undocumented immigrants or legal immigrants with less than five years\' residence in the United States gain coverage).<sup id="cite&#95;ref-KFFCoverage&#95;138-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-KFFCoverage-138"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>136<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>According to a 2013 study, Mexican women have the highest uninsured rate (54.6%) as compared to other immigrants (26.2%), Black (22.5%) and White (13.9%).<sup id="cite&#95;ref-deLeonSiantz&#95;139-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-deLeonSiantz-139"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>137<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> According to the study, Mexican women are the largest female immigrant group in the United States, and are also the most at risk for developing preventable health conditions.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-deLeonSiantz&#95;139-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-deLeonSiantz-139"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>137<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Multiple factors such as limited access to health care, legal status and income increase the risk of developing preventable health conditions because many undocumented immigrants postpone routine visits to the doctor until they become seriously ill.\n</p>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Effects_of_family_separation">Effects of family separation</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Hispanic_and_Latino_Americans&amp;action=edit&amp;section=22" title="Edit section: Effects of family separation"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-right" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Ursula_(detention_center)_1.png" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/64/Ursula_%28detention_center%29_1.png/250px-Ursula_%28detention_center%29_1.png" decoding="async" width="250" height="141" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/64/Ursula_%28detention_center%29_1.png/500px-Ursula_%28detention_center%29_1.png 1.5x" data-file-width="2500" data-file-height="1406" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Ursula_(detention_center)" title="Ursula (detention center)">Ursula detention center</a> in <a href="/wiki/McAllen,_Texas" title="McAllen, Texas">McAllen, Texas</a> is the largest <a href="/wiki/U.S._Customs_and_Border_Protection" class="mw-redirect" title="U.S. Customs and Border Protection">U.S. Customs and Border Protection</a> facility for processing <a href="/wiki/Undocumented_immigrants" class="mw-redirect" title="Undocumented immigrants">undocumented immigrants</a>.</figcaption></figure>\n<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Families_Belong_Together_(42627153945).jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e7/Families_Belong_Together_%2842627153945%29.jpg/250px-Families_Belong_Together_%2842627153945%29.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="250" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e7/Families_Belong_Together_%2842627153945%29.jpg/500px-Families_Belong_Together_%2842627153945%29.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="3024" data-file-height="3024" /></a><figcaption>Rally to end the <a href="/wiki/Trump_administration_family_separation_policy" title="Trump administration family separation policy">Trump administration family separation policy</a> in <a href="/wiki/San_Francisco" title="San Francisco">San Francisco</a>.</figcaption></figure>\n<p>The <a href="/wiki/American_Academy_of_Pediatrics" title="American Academy of Pediatrics">American Academy of Pediatrics</a>, the <a href="/wiki/Canadian_Paediatric_Society" title="Canadian Paediatric Society">Canadian Paediatric Society</a>, the <a href="/wiki/American_Medical_Association" title="American Medical Association">American Medical Association</a>, the <a href="/wiki/Canadian_Medical_Association" title="Canadian Medical Association">Canadian Medical Association</a> and the International Society for Social Pediatrics and Child Health strongly condemn the systematic splitting of immigrant families. During the summer 2018, over 2300 immigrant children, reportedly including preverbal and breastfed infants were relocated to separate shelters across the USA pending their parent’s case.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-140" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-140"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>138<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> By 2025, at least 5,600 migrant children had been separated from their parents, hundreds of which have never been reunited, while families continue to be separated.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-141" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-141"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>139<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> In 2025, more than 100 US citizen infants and children were separated from their parents.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-142" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-142"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>140<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>Immigration policies for arriving Mexican and Central American immigrants are linked to mental health issues among documented and undocumented immigrant families and youth. The effects are often long-term and the impact extends to the community level. Children may experience emotional traumas and long-term changes in behaviors. Additionally, when parents are forcefully removed, children often develop feelings of abandonment and they might blame themselves for what has happened to their family. Some children believe in the possibility of never seeing their parents again. These effects can cause negative parent-child attachment. Reunification may be difficult because of immigration laws and re-entry restrictions which further affect the mental health of children and parents.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-Torres-Richards&#95;143-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Torres-Richards-143"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>141<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Parents who leave their home country also experience negative mental health experiences. According to a study published in 2013 on Mexican migrant men, 46% of those who participated in the study reported elevated levels of depressive symptoms, associated with structural stressors (family separation, sending remittances to Mexico) and situational stressors (fearfulness, worry about police confrontation, treatment by non-Latinos, and lack of support).<sup id="cite&#95;ref-Letiecq-Eudave&#95;144-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Letiecq-Eudave-144"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>142<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Vulnerabilities">Vulnerabilities</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Hispanic_and_Latino_Americans&amp;action=edit&amp;section=23" title="Edit section: Vulnerabilities"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-left" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Alligator_Alcatraz_-_54627249257.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0f/Alligator_Alcatraz_-_54627249257.jpg/250px-Alligator_Alcatraz_-_54627249257.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="167" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0f/Alligator_Alcatraz_-_54627249257.jpg/500px-Alligator_Alcatraz_-_54627249257.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="7000" data-file-height="4667" /></a><figcaption>President <a href="/wiki/Donald_Trump" title="Donald Trump">Donald Trump</a> visiting the newly-built <a href="/wiki/Alligator_Alcatraz" title="Alligator Alcatraz">Alligator Alcatraz</a> immigrant detention facility in Florida.</figcaption></figure><p> President <a href="/wiki/Donald_Trump" title="Donald Trump">Donald Trump</a> and his administration have pursued a <a href="/wiki/Deportation_and_removal_from_the_United_States" class="mw-redirect" title="Deportation and removal from the United States">deportation policy</a> characterized as "<a href="/wiki/Hardline" title="Hardline">hardline</a>" <sup id="cite&#95;ref-145" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-145"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>143<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> with "huge camps" for immigrant detention.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-Graziosi&#95;146-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Graziosi-146"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>144<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> According to a mid-July list of the population detainted at the immigration detention center in the Everglades dubbed "<a href="/wiki/Alligator_Alcatraz" title="Alligator Alcatraz">Alligator Alcatraz</a>", more than 95% of the detainees originated from Latin American countries, with approximately 20% from Guatemala, ~20% from Mexico, and another ~10% from Cuba.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-147" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-147"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>145<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> On July 16, 2025, the <a href="/wiki/American_Civil_Liberties_Union" title="American Civil Liberties Union">American Civil Liberties Union</a>, the ACLU of Florida, and Americans for Immigrant Justice filed a <a href="/wiki/Class_action" title="Class action">class action</a> suit claiming the <a href="/wiki/Second_presidency_of_Donald_Trump" title="Second presidency of Donald Trump">Trump administration</a> violates the <a href="/wiki/First_Amendment" class="mw-redirect" title="First Amendment">First Amendment</a> and <a href="/wiki/Fifth_Amendment_to_the_United_States_Constitution" title="Fifth Amendment to the United States Constitution">Fifth Amendment</a> rights of people being detained, as well as the First Amendment rights of legal service organizations and law firms with clients held at the facility.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-148" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-148"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>146<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>Many immigrant families cannot enjoy doing everyday activities without exercising caution because they fear encountering immigration officers, which limits their involvement in community events. Undocumented families also may not trust government institutions and services. Because of their fear of encountering immigration officers, immigrants may feel ostracized and isolated which can lead to the development of mental health issues such as depression and anxiety.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-Torres-Richards&#95;143-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Torres-Richards-143"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>141<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> The harmful effects of being ostracized from the rest of society are not limited to just that of undocumented immigrants but it affects the entire family even if some of the members are of legal status. Children often reported having been victims of bullying in school by classmates because their parents are undocumented.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-HinojosB&#95;149-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-HinojosB-149"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>147<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> This can cause them to feel isolated and develop a sense of inferiority which can negatively impact their academic performance.\n</p>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Stress">Stress</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Hispanic_and_Latino_Americans&amp;action=edit&amp;section=24" title="Edit section: Stress"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-right" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Little_Havana_Dominos_Park.JPG" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f3/Little_Havana_Dominos_Park.JPG/250px-Little_Havana_Dominos_Park.JPG" decoding="async" width="250" height="188" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f3/Little_Havana_Dominos_Park.JPG/500px-Little_Havana_Dominos_Park.JPG 1.5x" data-file-width="4000" data-file-height="3000" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Little_Havana" title="Little Havana">Little Havana</a> is a hub for the Cuban community of <a href="/wiki/Miami" title="Miami">Miami</a>, Florida.</figcaption></figure>\n<p>Despite the struggles Hispanic families encounter, they have found ways to keep motivated. Many immigrants use religion as a source of motivation. Mexican immigrants believed that the difficulties they face are a part of God\'s bigger plan and believe their life will get better in the end. They kept their faith strong and pray every day, hoping that God will keep their families safe.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-HinojosB&#95;149-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-HinojosB-149"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>147<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Immigrants participate in church services and bond with other immigrants that share the same experiences.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-Torres-Richards&#95;143-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Torres-Richards-143"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>141<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Undocumented Hispanics also find support from friends, family and the community that serve as coping mechanisms. Some Hispanics state that their children are the reason they have the strength to keep on going. They want their children to have a future and give them things they are not able to have themselves.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-HinojosB&#95;149-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-HinojosB-149"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>147<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> The community is able to provide certain resources that immigrant families need such as tutoring for their children, financial assistance and counseling services.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-Torres-Richards&#95;143-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Torres-Richards-143"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>141<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Some identified that maintaining a positive mental attitude helped them cope with the stresses they experience. Many immigrants refuse to live their life in constant fear which leads to depression in order to enjoy life in the United States.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-HinojosB&#95;149-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-HinojosB-149"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>147<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Since many immigrants have unstable sources of income, many plan ahead in order to prevent future financial stress. They put money aside and find ways to save money instead of spend it such as learning to fix appliances themselves.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-HinojosB&#95;149-4" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-HinojosB-149"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>147<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Poverty_and_mental_health">Poverty and mental health</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Hispanic_and_Latino_Americans&amp;action=edit&amp;section=25" title="Edit section: Poverty and mental health"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-right" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Ch%C3%A1vez_Ravine_forcible_eviction.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c7/Ch%C3%A1vez_Ravine_forcible_eviction.jpg/250px-Ch%C3%A1vez_Ravine_forcible_eviction.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="198" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c7/Ch%C3%A1vez_Ravine_forcible_eviction.jpg/500px-Ch%C3%A1vez_Ravine_forcible_eviction.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="700" data-file-height="554" /></a><figcaption>In 1958, <a href="/wiki/Los_Angeles_County_Sheriff" class="mw-redirect" title="Los Angeles County Sheriff">Los Angeles County Sheriffs</a> forcibly evicted the Mexican/Chicano community of <a href="/wiki/Chavez_Ravine" title="Chavez Ravine">Chavez Ravine</a> for the construction of <a href="/wiki/Dodger_Stadium" title="Dodger Stadium">Dodger Stadium</a>, in a dispute known as the "<a href="/wiki/Battle_of_Chavez_Ravine" title="Battle of Chavez Ravine">Battle of Chavez Ravine</a>".</figcaption></figure>\n<p>Many Hispanic families migrate to find better economic opportunities in order to send remittances back home. Being undocumented limits the possibilities of jobs that immigrants undertake and many struggle to find a stable job. Many Hispanics report that companies turned them down because they do not have a <a href="/wiki/Social_Security_(United_States)" title="Social Security (United States)">Social Security</a> number. If they are able to obtain a job, immigrants risk losing it if their employer finds out they are unable to provide proof of residency or citizenship. Many look towards agencies that do not ask for identification, but those jobs are often unreliable. In order to prevent themselves from being detained and deported, many have to work under exploitation. In a study, a participant reported "If someone knows that you don\'t have the papers&#160;... that person is a danger. Many people will con them&#160;... if they know you don\'t have the papers, with everything they say \'hey I\'m going to call immigration on you.<span style="padding-right:.15em;">\'</span>"<sup id="cite&#95;ref-HinojosB&#95;149-5" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-HinojosB-149"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>147<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> These conditions lower the income that Hispanic families bring to their household and some find living each day very difficult. When an undocumented parent is deported or detained, income will be lowered significantly if the other parent also supports the family financially. The parent who is left has to look after the family and might find working difficult to manage along with other responsibilities. Even if families are not separated, Hispanics are constantly living in fear that they will lose their economic footing.\n</p><p>Living in poverty has been linked to depression, low self-esteem, loneliness, crime activities and frequent drug use among youth.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-Torres-Richards&#95;143-4" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Torres-Richards-143"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>141<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Families with low incomes are unable to afford adequate housing and some of them are evicted. The environment in which the children of undocumented immigrants grow up in is often composed of poor air quality, noise, and toxins which prevent healthy development.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-Torres-Richards&#95;143-5" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Torres-Richards-143"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>141<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Furthermore, these neighborhoods are prone to violence and <a href="/wiki/Gangs_in_the_United_States" title="Gangs in the United States">gang activities</a>, forcing the families to live in constant fear which can contribute to the development of PTSD, aggression and depression.\n</p>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Economic_outlook">Economic outlook</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Hispanic_and_Latino_Americans&amp;action=edit&amp;section=26" title="Edit section: Economic outlook"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-right" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Income_by_Race_and_Ethnicity_and_Hispanic_origins_2023.png" class="mw-file-description"><img alt="Income by Race and Ethnicity and Hispanic / Latino origins 2023" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/92/Income_by_Race_and_Ethnicity_and_Hispanic_origins_2023.png/250px-Income_by_Race_and_Ethnicity_and_Hispanic_origins_2023.png" decoding="async" width="250" height="252" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/92/Income_by_Race_and_Ethnicity_and_Hispanic_origins_2023.png/500px-Income_by_Race_and_Ethnicity_and_Hispanic_origins_2023.png 1.5x" data-file-width="864" data-file-height="870" /></a><figcaption><b>Income by Race and Ethnicity and Hispanic / Latino origins 2023 shows the economic status of different ethnic groups</b><sup id="cite&#95;ref-150" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-150"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>148<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup></figcaption></figure>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Median_income">Median income</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Hispanic_and_Latino_Americans&amp;action=edit&amp;section=27" title="Edit section: Median income"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<p>In 2017, the <a href="/wiki/US_census" class="mw-redirect" title="US census">US census</a> reported the median household incomes of Hispanic Americans to be $50,486. This is the third consecutive annual increase in median household income for Hispanic-origin households.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-census.gov&#95;94-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-census.gov-94"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>94<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Poverty">Poverty</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Hispanic_and_Latino_Americans&amp;action=edit&amp;section=28" title="Edit section: Poverty"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<p>According to the US census, the <a href="/wiki/Poverty_threshold" title="Poverty threshold">poverty rate</a> Hispanics was 18.3 percent in 2017, down from 19.4 percent in 2016. Hispanics accounted for 10.8 million individuals in poverty.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-census.gov&#95;94-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-census.gov-94"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>94<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> In comparison, the average poverty rates in 2017 for non-Hispanic White Americans was 8.7 percent with 17 million individuals in poverty, Asian Americans was 10.0 percent with 2 million individuals in poverty, and African Americans was 21.2 percent with 9 million individuals in poverty.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-census.gov&#95;94-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-census.gov-94"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>94<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p>\n<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-left" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Dolores_Huerta.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c6/Dolores_Huerta.jpg/250px-Dolores_Huerta.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="198" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c6/Dolores_Huerta.jpg/500px-Dolores_Huerta.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="2100" data-file-height="1666" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Dolores_Huerta" title="Dolores Huerta">Dolores Huerta</a> is an activist for workers\', immigrants\' and women\'s rights. She was the first Hispanic inducted into the <a href="/wiki/National_Women%27s_Hall_of_Fame" title="National Women&#39;s Hall of Fame">National Women\'s Hall of Fame</a>, in 1993.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-makers&#95;hof&#95;151-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-makers_hof-151"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>149<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-adelante&#95;152-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-adelante-152"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>150<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup></figcaption></figure>\n<p>Among the largest Hispanic groups during 2015 was: Honduran Americans &amp; Dominican Americans (27%), Guatemalan Americans (26%), Puerto Ricans (24%), Mexican Americans (23%), Salvadoran Americans (20%), Cuban Americans and Venezuelan Americans (17%), Ecuadorian Americans (15%), Nicaraguan Americans (14%), Colombian Americans (13%), Argentinian Americans (11%), and Peruvian Americans (10%).<sup id="cite&#95;ref-153" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-153"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>151<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>Poverty affects many underrepresented students as racial/ethnic minorities tend to stay isolated within pockets of low-income communities. This results in several inequalities, such as "school offerings, teacher quality, curriculum, counseling and all manner of things that both keep students engaged in school and prepare them to graduate".<sup id="cite&#95;ref-154" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-154"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>152<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> In the case of Hispanics, the poverty rate for Hispanic children in 2004 was 28.6 percent.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-Hispanics:&#95;Education&#95;Issues&#95;108-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Hispanics:_Education_Issues-108"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>106<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Moreover, with this lack of resources, schools reproduce these inequalities for generations to come. In order to assuage poverty, many Hispanic families can turn to social and community services as resources.\n</p>\n<div style="clear:both;" class=""></div>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Cultural_matters">Cultural matters</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Hispanic_and_Latino_Americans&amp;action=edit&amp;section=29" title="Edit section: Cultural matters"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1320445320" /><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main articles: <a href="/wiki/American_culture" class="mw-redirect" title="American culture">American culture</a> and <a href="/wiki/Hispanic_culture" class="mw-redirect" title="Hispanic culture">Hispanic culture</a></div>\n<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1320445320" /><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">See also: <a href="/wiki/National_Association_of_Latino_Fraternal_Organizations" title="National Association of Latino Fraternal Organizations">National Association of Latino Fraternal Organizations</a></div>\n<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-right" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:HispanicSocietyofAmerica.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/63/HispanicSocietyofAmerica.jpg/250px-HispanicSocietyofAmerica.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="167" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/63/HispanicSocietyofAmerica.jpg/500px-HispanicSocietyofAmerica.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="1728" data-file-height="1152" /></a><figcaption>The <a href="/wiki/Hispanic_Society_of_America" title="Hispanic Society of America">Hispanic Society of America</a> was founded in 1904.</figcaption></figure>\n<p>The geographic, political, social, economic and racial diversity of Hispanic Americans makes all Hispanics very different depending on their family heritage and/or national origin. Many times, there are many cultural similarities between Hispanics from neighboring countries than from more distant countries, i.e. Spanish Caribbean, Southern Cone, Central America etc. Yet several features tend to unite Hispanics from these diverse backgrounds.\n</p>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Language">Language</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Hispanic_and_Latino_Americans&amp;action=edit&amp;section=30" title="Edit section: Language"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1320445320" /><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">See also: <a href="/wiki/Spanish_language_in_the_United_States" title="Spanish language in the United States">Spanish language in the United States</a> and <a href="/wiki/Languages_of_the_United_States" title="Languages of the United States">Languages of the United States</a></div>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading4"><h4 id="Spanish">Spanish</h4><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Hispanic_and_Latino_Americans&amp;action=edit&amp;section=31" title="Edit section: Spanish"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1273380762/mw-parser-output/.tmulti" /><div class="thumb tmulti tleft"><div class="thumbinner multiimageinner" style="width:308px;max-width:308px"><div class="trow"><div class="tsingle" style="width:152px;max-width:152px"><div class="thumbimage"><span typeof="mw:File"><a href="/wiki/File:Proclama_al_Pueblo_de_California_(1849)_(cropped).jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4f/Proclama_al_Pueblo_de_California_%281849%29_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-Proclama_al_Pueblo_de_California_%281849%29_%28cropped%29.jpg" decoding="async" width="150" height="193" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4f/Proclama_al_Pueblo_de_California_%281849%29_%28cropped%29.jpg/330px-Proclama_al_Pueblo_de_California_%281849%29_%28cropped%29.jpg 2x" data-file-width="871" data-file-height="1122" /></a></span></div></div><div class="tsingle" style="width:152px;max-width:152px"><div class="thumbimage"><span typeof="mw:File"><a href="/wiki/File:California_Constitution_1849_title_page.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/bc/California_Constitution_1849_title_page.jpg/250px-California_Constitution_1849_title_page.jpg" decoding="async" width="150" height="194" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/bc/California_Constitution_1849_title_page.jpg/330px-California_Constitution_1849_title_page.jpg 2x" data-file-width="539" data-file-height="697" /></a></span></div></div></div><div class="trow" style="display:flex"><div class="thumbcaption">The <a href="/wiki/Constitution_of_California" title="Constitution of California">Constitution of California</a> was written in both <a href="/wiki/Spanish_language" title="Spanish language">Spanish</a> (left) and <a href="/wiki/English_language" title="English language">English</a> (right) in 1849.</div></div></div></div>\n<p>As one of the most important uniting factors of Hispanic Americans, <a href="/wiki/Spanish_language" title="Spanish language">Spanish</a> is an important part of Hispanic culture. Teaching Spanish to children is often one of the most valued skills taught amongst Hispanic families. Spanish is not only closely tied with the person\'s family, heritage, and overall culture, but valued for increased opportunities in business and one\'s future professional career. A 2013 Pew Research survey showed that 95% of Hispanics adults said "it\'s important that future generations of Hispanics speak Spanish".<sup id="cite&#95;ref-pewresearch.org&#95;155-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-pewresearch.org-155"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>153<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-156" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-156"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>154<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Given the United States\' proximity to other <a href="/wiki/Latin_America" title="Latin America">Spanish-speaking countries</a>, Spanish is being passed on to future American generations. Amongst second-generation Hispanics, 80% speak fluent Spanish, and amongst third-generation Hispanics, 40% speak fluent Spanish.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-157" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-157"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>155<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Spanish is also the most popular language taught in the United States.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-158" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-158"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>156<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-159" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-159"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>157<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p>\n<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Coachella_City_Hall.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0e/Coachella_City_Hall.jpg/250px-Coachella_City_Hall.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="167" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0e/Coachella_City_Hall.jpg/500px-Coachella_City_Hall.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="3982" data-file-height="2655" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Coachella,_California" title="Coachella, California">Coachella</a> is an example of a city government that is officially bilingual in English and Spanish.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-Coachella&#95;160-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Coachella-160"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>158<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup></figcaption></figure>\n<p>Hispanics have revived the <a href="/wiki/Spanish_language_in_the_United_States" title="Spanish language in the United States">Spanish language in the United States</a>, first brought to <a href="/wiki/North_America" title="North America">North America</a> during the Spanish colonial period in the 16th century. Spanish is the oldest European language in the United States, spoken uninterruptedly for four and a half centuries, since the founding of <a href="/wiki/Saint_Augustine,_Florida" class="mw-redirect" title="Saint Augustine, Florida">Saint Augustine, Florida</a> in 1565.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-legacies&#95;161-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-legacies-161"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>159<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-st-aug&#95;162-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-st-aug-162"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>160<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-amlib&#95;163-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-amlib-163"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>161<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-mhs&#95;164-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-mhs-164"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>162<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> As of 2006 90% of all Hispanics spoke English, and at least 78% speak fluent Spanish.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-lang&#95;165-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-lang-165"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>163<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Additionally, 2.8 million non-Hispanic Americans also speak Spanish at home for a total of 41.1 million.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-Pew&#95;Research&#95;Center-2013&#95;96-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Pew_Research_Center-2013-96"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>96<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>With 40% of Hispanic Americans being immigrants,<sup id="cite&#95;ref-profile&#95;166-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-profile-166"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>164<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> and with many of the 60% who are US-born being the children or grandchildren of immigrants, <a href="/wiki/Bilingualism" class="mw-redirect" title="Bilingualism">bilingualism</a> is the norm in the community at large. At home, at least 69% of all Hispanics over the age of five are bilingual in English and Spanish, whereas up to 22% are monolingual English-speakers, and 9% are monolingual Spanish speakers. Another 0.4% speak a language other than English and Spanish at home.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-lang&#95;165-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-lang-165"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>163<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading4"><h4 id="American_Spanish_dialects">American Spanish dialects</h4><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Hispanic_and_Latino_Americans&amp;action=edit&amp;section=32" title="Edit section: American Spanish dialects"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1320445320" /><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">See also: <a href="/wiki/Isle%C3%B1o_Spanish" title="Isleño Spanish">Isleño Spanish</a>, <a href="/wiki/New_Mexican_Spanish" title="New Mexican Spanish">New Mexican Spanish</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Spanish_language_in_California" title="Spanish language in California">Spanish language in California</a></div>\n<table class="wikitable" style="float:right; margin-left:1em; font-size:90%">\n<caption>Spanish speakers<br /> in the United States\n</caption>\n<tbody><tr>\n<th>Year\n</th>\n<th>Number of<br /> speakers\n</th>\n<th>Percent of<br />population\n</th></tr>\n<tr>\n<td>1980\n</td>\n<td style="text-align:right;">11.0 million\n</td>\n<td style="text-align:right;">5%\n</td></tr>\n<tr>\n<td>1990\n</td>\n<td style="text-align:right;">17.3 million\n</td>\n<td style="text-align:right;">7%\n</td></tr>\n<tr>\n<td>2000\n</td>\n<td style="text-align:right;">28.1 million\n</td>\n<td style="text-align:right;">10%\n</td></tr>\n<tr>\n<td>2010\n</td>\n<td style="text-align:right;">37.0 million\n</td>\n<td style="text-align:right;">13%\n</td></tr>\n<tr>\n<td>2012\n</td>\n<td style="text-align:right;">38.3 million\n</td>\n<td style="text-align:right;">13%\n</td></tr>\n<tr>\n<td>2020*\n</td>\n<td style="text-align:right;">40.0 million\n</td>\n<td style="text-align:right;">14%\n</td></tr>\n<tr>\n<td colspan="3">*-Projected; sources:<sup id="cite&#95;ref-pewresearch.org&#95;155-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-pewresearch.org-155"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>153<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-167" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-167"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>165<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-168" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-168"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>166<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-169" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-169"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>167<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</td></tr></tbody></table>\n<p>The Spanish dialects spoken in the United States differ depending on the country of origin of the person or the person\'s family heritage. However, generally, Spanish spoken in the <a href="/wiki/Southwestern_United_States" title="Southwestern United States">Southwest</a> is <a href="/wiki/Mexican_Spanish" title="Mexican Spanish">Mexican Spanish</a> or <a href="/wiki/Chicano" title="Chicano">Chicano Spanish</a>. A variety of Spanish native to the Southwest spoken by descendants of the early Spanish colonists in <a href="/wiki/New_Mexico" title="New Mexico">New Mexico</a> and <a href="/wiki/Colorado" title="Colorado">Colorado</a> is known as Traditional <a href="/wiki/New_Mexican_Spanish" title="New Mexican Spanish">New Mexican Spanish</a>. One of the major distinctions of Traditional New Mexican Spanish is its use of distinct vocabulary and grammatical forms that make <a href="/wiki/New_Mexican_Spanish" title="New Mexican Spanish">New Mexican Spanish</a> unique amongst Spanish dialects. The Spanish spoken in the <a href="/wiki/East_Coast_of_the_United_States" title="East Coast of the United States">East Coast</a> is generally <a href="/wiki/Caribbean_Spanish" title="Caribbean Spanish">Caribbean Spanish</a> and is heavily influenced by the Spanish of <a href="/wiki/Cuban_Spanish" title="Cuban Spanish">Cuba</a>, the <a href="/wiki/Dominican_Spanish" title="Dominican Spanish">Dominican Republic</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Puerto_Rican_Spanish" title="Puerto Rican Spanish">Puerto Rico</a>. <a href="/wiki/Isle%C3%B1o_Spanish" title="Isleño Spanish">Isleño Spanish</a>, descended from <a href="/wiki/Canarian_Spanish" title="Canarian Spanish">Canarian Spanish</a>, is the historic Spanish dialect spoken by the descendants of the earliest Spanish colonists beginning in the 18th century in <a href="/wiki/Louisiana" title="Louisiana">Louisiana</a>. Spanish spoken elsewhere throughout the country varies, although is generally <a href="/wiki/Mexican_Spanish" title="Mexican Spanish">Mexican Spanish</a>.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-Pew&#95;Research&#95;Center-2013&#95;96-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Pew_Research_Center-2013-96"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>96<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-170" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-170"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>168<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>Heritage Spanish speakers tend to speak Spanish with near-native level phonology, but a more limited command of morphosyntax.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-171" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-171"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>169<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Hispanics who speak Spanish as a second language often speak with English accents.\n</p>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading4"><h4 id="Spanglish_and_English_dialects">Spanglish and English dialects</h4><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Hispanic_and_Latino_Americans&amp;action=edit&amp;section=33" title="Edit section: Spanglish and English dialects"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1320445320" /><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main articles: <a href="/wiki/Chicano_English" title="Chicano English">Chicano English</a>, <a href="/wiki/Spanglish" title="Spanglish">Spanglish</a>, <a href="/wiki/Miami#Dialect" title="Miami">Miami §&#160;Dialect</a>, and <a href="/wiki/New_York_Latino_English" title="New York Latino English">New York Latino English</a></div>\n<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1320445320" /><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">See also: <a href="/wiki/List_of_English_words_of_Spanish_origin" title="List of English words of Spanish origin">List of English words of Spanish origin</a></div>\n<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-right" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:WTM3_The_Fixers_0056.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/ca/WTM3_The_Fixers_0056.jpg/250px-WTM3_The_Fixers_0056.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="166" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/ca/WTM3_The_Fixers_0056.jpg/500px-WTM3_The_Fixers_0056.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="3008" data-file-height="2000" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/El_Museo_del_Barrio" title="El Museo del Barrio">El Museo del Barrio</a>, in Manhattan, is the oldest museum in the country dedicated to Latino art.</figcaption></figure>\n<p>Hispanics have influenced the way Americans speak with the introduction of many Spanish words into the English language. Amongst younger generations of Hispanics, <a href="/wiki/Spanglish" title="Spanglish">Spanglish</a>, a term for any mix of Spanish and English, is common in speaking. As they are fluent in both languages, speakers will often switch between Spanish and English throughout the conversation. Spanglish is particularly common in Hispanic-majority cities and communities such as <a href="/wiki/Miami" title="Miami">Miami</a>, <a href="/wiki/Hialeah" class="mw-redirect" title="Hialeah">Hialeah</a>, <a href="/wiki/San_Antonio" title="San Antonio">San Antonio</a>, <a href="/wiki/Los_Angeles" title="Los Angeles">Los Angeles</a> and parts of <a href="/wiki/New_York_City" title="New York City">New York City</a>.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-172" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-172"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>170<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>Hispanics have also influenced the way English is spoken in the United States. In Miami, for example, the <a href="/wiki/Miami#Dialect" title="Miami">Miami dialect</a> has evolved as the most common form of English spoken and heard in Miami today. This is a native dialect of English, and was developed amongst second and third generations of <a href="/wiki/Cuban_American" class="mw-redirect" title="Cuban American">Cuban Americans</a> in Miami. Today, it is commonly heard everywhere throughout the city. <a href="/wiki/Gloria_Estefan" title="Gloria Estefan">Gloria Estefan</a> and <a href="/wiki/Enrique_Iglesias" title="Enrique Iglesias">Enrique Iglesias</a> are examples of people who speak with the Miami dialect. Another major English dialect is spoken by <a href="/wiki/Chicano" title="Chicano">Chicanos</a> and <a href="/wiki/Tejano" class="mw-redirect" title="Tejano">Tejanos</a> in the <a href="/wiki/Southwestern_United_States" title="Southwestern United States">Southwestern United States</a>, called <a href="/wiki/Chicano_English" title="Chicano English">Chicano English</a>. <a href="/wiki/George_Lopez" title="George Lopez">George Lopez</a> and <a href="/wiki/Selena" title="Selena">Selena</a> are examples of speakers of Chicano English.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-173" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-173"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>171<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> An English dialect spoken by Puerto Ricans and other Hispanic groups is called <a href="/wiki/New_York_Latino_English" title="New York Latino English">New York Latino English</a>; <a href="/wiki/Jennifer_Lopez" title="Jennifer Lopez">Jennifer Lopez</a> and <a href="/wiki/Cardi_B" title="Cardi B">Cardi B</a> are examples of people who speak with the New York Latino dialect.\n</p><p>When speaking in English, American Hispanics may often insert Spanish tag and filler items such as <span title="Spanish-language text"><i lang="es">tú sabes</i></span>, <span title="Spanish-language text"><i lang="es">este</i></span>, and <span title="Spanish-language text"><i lang="es">órale</i></span>, into sentences as a marker of ethnic identity and solidarity. The same often occurs with grammatical words like <span title="Spanish-language text"><i lang="es">pero</i></span>.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-174" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-174"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>172<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Religion">Religion</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Hispanic_and_Latino_Americans&amp;action=edit&amp;section=34" title="Edit section: Religion"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-right" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:The_Cathedral_of_San_Carlos_Borromeo,_Monterey,_California_LCCN2013630519.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/bd/The_Cathedral_of_San_Carlos_Borromeo%2C_Monterey%2C_California_LCCN2013630519.jpg/250px-The_Cathedral_of_San_Carlos_Borromeo%2C_Monterey%2C_California_LCCN2013630519.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="242" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/bd/The_Cathedral_of_San_Carlos_Borromeo%2C_Monterey%2C_California_LCCN2013630519.jpg/500px-The_Cathedral_of_San_Carlos_Borromeo%2C_Monterey%2C_California_LCCN2013630519.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="4912" data-file-height="4747" /></a><figcaption>Built in 1791, the <a href="/wiki/Cathedral_of_San_Carlos_Borromeo_(Monterey,_California)" title="Cathedral of San Carlos Borromeo (Monterey, California)">Cathedral of San Carlos Borromeo</a> in <a href="/wiki/Monterey,_California" title="Monterey, California">Monterey, California</a> is the oldest serving cathedral in the country.</figcaption></figure>\n<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-right" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Mission_Concepcion_San_Antonio.JPG" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/93/Mission_Concepcion_San_Antonio.JPG/250px-Mission_Concepcion_San_Antonio.JPG" decoding="async" width="250" height="199" class="mw-file-element" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/San_Antonio_Missions_National_Historical_Park" title="San Antonio Missions National Historical Park">San Antonio Missions National Park</a> in Texas a <a href="/wiki/UNESCO_World_Heritage_Site" class="mw-redirect" title="UNESCO World Heritage Site">UNESCO World Heritage Site</a> comprising four historic mission sites.</figcaption></figure>\n<p>According to a <a href="/wiki/Pew_Center" class="mw-redirect" title="Pew Center">Pew Center</a> study which was conducted in 2019, the majority of Hispanic Americans are <a href="/wiki/Christianity" title="Christianity">Christians</a> (72%),<sup id="cite&#95;ref-Decline2019&#95;175-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Decline2019-175"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>173<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Among American Hispanics, as of 2018–19, 47% are <a href="/wiki/Catholic" class="mw-redirect" title="Catholic">Catholic</a>, 24% are <a href="/wiki/Protestant" class="mw-redirect" title="Protestant">Protestant</a>, 1% are <a href="/wiki/Mormon" class="mw-redirect" title="Mormon">Mormon</a>, less than 1% are <a href="/wiki/Orthodoxy#Christianity" title="Orthodoxy">Orthodox Christian</a>, 3% are members of non-Christian faiths, and 23% are <a href="/wiki/Irreligion_in_the_United_States" title="Irreligion in the United States">unaffiliated</a>.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-Decline2019&#95;175-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Decline2019-175"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>173<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> The proportion of Hispanics who are Catholic has dropped from 2009 (when it was 57%), while the proportion of unaffiliated Hispanics has increased since 2009 (when it was 15%).<sup id="cite&#95;ref-Decline2019&#95;175-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Decline2019-175"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>173<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Among Hispanic Protestant community, most are <a href="/wiki/Evangelical" class="mw-redirect" title="Evangelical">evangelical</a>, but some belong to <a href="/wiki/Mainline_Protestant" title="Mainline Protestant">mainline denominations</a>.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-ShiftingIdentity&#95;176-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-ShiftingIdentity-176"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>174<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Compared to Catholic, unaffiliated, and mainline Protestant Hispanics; Evangelical Protestant Hispanics are substantially more likely to attend services weekly, pray daily, and adhere to <a href="/wiki/Biblical_liberalism" class="mw-redirect" title="Biblical liberalism">biblical liberalism</a>.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-ShiftingIdentity&#95;176-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-ShiftingIdentity-176"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>174<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> As of 2014, about 67% of Hispanic Protestants and about 52% of Hispanic Catholics were renewalist, meaning that they described themselves as <a href="/wiki/Pentecostal" class="mw-redirect" title="Pentecostal">Pentecostal</a> or <a href="/wiki/Charismatic_Christian" class="mw-redirect" title="Charismatic Christian">charismatic Christians</a> (in the Catholic tradition, called <a href="/wiki/Catholic_charismatic_renewal" class="mw-redirect" title="Catholic charismatic renewal">Catholic charismatic renewal</a>).<sup id="cite&#95;ref-177" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-177"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>175<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>Catholic affiliation is much higher among first-generation Hispanic immigrants than it is among second and third-generation Hispanic immigrants, who exhibit a fairly high rate of conversion to Protestantism or the unaffiliated camp.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-178" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-178"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>176<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> According to <a href="/wiki/Andrew_Greeley" title="Andrew Greeley">Andrew Greeley</a>, as many as 600,000 American Hispanics leave Catholicism for Protestant churches every year, and this figure is much higher in <a href="/wiki/Texas" title="Texas">Texas</a> and <a href="/wiki/Florida" title="Florida">Florida</a>.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-179" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-179"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>177<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Hispanic Catholics are developing youth and social programs to retain members.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-180" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-180"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>178<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p>\n<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-right" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Our_Lady_of_La_Leche_Shrine_Exterior.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/cc/Our_Lady_of_La_Leche_Shrine_Exterior.jpg/250px-Our_Lady_of_La_Leche_Shrine_Exterior.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="195" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/cc/Our_Lady_of_La_Leche_Shrine_Exterior.jpg/500px-Our_Lady_of_La_Leche_Shrine_Exterior.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="2879" data-file-height="2242" /></a><figcaption>Founded in 1609, the <a href="/wiki/National_Shrine_of_Our_Lady_of_La_Leche" title="National Shrine of Our Lady of La Leche">National Shrine of Our Lady of La Leche</a>, in <a href="/wiki/St._Augustine,_Florida" title="St. Augustine, Florida">St. Augustine, Florida</a>, is the oldest shrine in the country.</figcaption></figure>\n<p>Hispanics make up a substantial proportion (almost 40%) of <a href="/wiki/Catholic_Church_in_the_United_States" title="Catholic Church in the United States">Catholics in the United States</a>,<sup id="cite&#95;ref-Dias&#95;181-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Dias-181"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>179<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> although the number of American Hispanic <a href="/wiki/Catholic_priests" class="mw-redirect" title="Catholic priests">priests</a> is low relative to Hispanic membership in the church.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-182" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-182"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>180<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> In 2019, <a href="/wiki/Jos%C3%A9_Horacio_G%C3%B3mez" title="José Horacio Gómez">José Horacio Gómez</a>, <a href="/wiki/Archbishop_of_Los_Angeles" class="mw-redirect" title="Archbishop of Los Angeles">Archbishop of Los Angeles</a> and a naturalized American citizen born in Mexico, was elected as president of the <a href="/wiki/US_Conference_of_Catholic_Bishops" class="mw-redirect" title="US Conference of Catholic Bishops">US Conference of Catholic Bishops</a>.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-Dias&#95;181-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Dias-181"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>179<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p>\n<table class="wikitable">\n<caption>Pew Research Center: Hispanic and Latino Religious Affiliation (2010–2022)<sup id="cite&#95;ref-183" class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Media">Media</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Hispanic_and_Latino_Americans&amp;action=edit&amp;section=35" title="Edit section: Media"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1320445320" /><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">See also: <a href="/wiki/Latino_literature" title="Latino literature">Latino literature</a></div>\n<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-left" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:LA_Plaza_de_Cultura_y_Artes,_Los_Angeles,_California_(14523832122).jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3f/LA_Plaza_de_Cultura_y_Artes%2C_Los_Angeles%2C_California_%2814523832122%29.jpg/250px-LA_Plaza_de_Cultura_y_Artes%2C_Los_Angeles%2C_California_%2814523832122%29.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="188" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3f/LA_Plaza_de_Cultura_y_Artes%2C_Los_Angeles%2C_California_%2814523832122%29.jpg/500px-LA_Plaza_de_Cultura_y_Artes%2C_Los_Angeles%2C_California_%2814523832122%29.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="4000" data-file-height="3000" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/LA_Plaza_de_Cultura_y_Artes" title="LA Plaza de Cultura y Artes">LA Plaza de Cultura y Artes</a> is a museum and cultural center in Los Angeles.</figcaption></figure>\n<p>The United States is home to thousands of Spanish-language <a href="/wiki/Mass_media" title="Mass media">media</a> outlets, which range in size from giant commercial and some non-commercial <a href="/wiki/List_of_United_States_over-the-air_television_networks" title="List of United States over-the-air television networks">broadcasting networks</a> and major magazines with circulations numbering in the millions, to low-power <a href="/wiki/AM_radio" class="mw-redirect" title="AM radio">AM radio</a> stations with listeners numbering in the hundreds. There are hundreds of Internet media outlets targeting US Hispanic consumers. Some of the outlets are online versions of their printed counterparts and some online exclusively.\n</p><p>Increased use of Spanish-language media leads to increased levels of group consciousness, according to survey data. The differences in attitudes are due to the diverging goals of Spanish-language and English-language media. The effect of using Spanish-language media serves to promote a sense of group consciousness among Hispanics by reinforcing roots in the Hispanic world and the commonalities among Hispanics of varying national origin.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-184" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-184"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>182<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-185" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-185"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>183<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>The first Hispanic-American owned major <a href="/wiki/Film_studio" title="Film studio">film studio</a> in the United States is based in <a href="/wiki/Atlanta,_Georgia" class="mw-redirect" title="Atlanta, Georgia">Atlanta, Georgia</a>. In 2017, Ozzie and Will Areu purchased <a href="/wiki/Tyler_Perry" title="Tyler Perry">Tyler Perry\'s</a> former studio to establish Areu Bros. Studios.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-186" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-186"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>184<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-187" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-187"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>185<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>Hispanics are more likely to use social media such as <a href="/wiki/TikTok" title="TikTok">TikTok</a> and <a href="/wiki/Instagram" title="Instagram">Instagram</a> than non-Hispanics.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-188" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-188"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>186<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading4"><h4 id="Radio">Radio</h4><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Hispanic_and_Latino_Americans&amp;action=edit&amp;section=36" title="Edit section: Radio"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-right" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:The_Cheech_Marin_Center_for_Chicano_Art_and_Culture_2023_07_26.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/58/The_Cheech_Marin_Center_for_Chicano_Art_and_Culture_2023_07_26.jpg/250px-The_Cheech_Marin_Center_for_Chicano_Art_and_Culture_2023_07_26.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="196" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/58/The_Cheech_Marin_Center_for_Chicano_Art_and_Culture_2023_07_26.jpg/500px-The_Cheech_Marin_Center_for_Chicano_Art_and_Culture_2023_07_26.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="3451" data-file-height="2708" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/The_Cheech_Marin_Center_for_Chicano_Art_%26_Culture" title="The Cheech Marin Center for Chicano Art &amp; Culture">The Cheech Marin Center for Chicano Art &amp; Culture</a> in Riverside, California.</figcaption></figure>\n<p>Spanish language radio is the largest non-English broadcasting media.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-189" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-189"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>187<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> While other foreign language broadcasting declined steadily, Spanish broadcasting grew steadily from the 1920s to the 1970s. The 1930s were boom years.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-190" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-190"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>188<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> The early success depended on the concentrated geographical audience in Texas and the Southwest.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-191" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-191"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>189<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> American stations were close to Mexico which enabled a steady circular flow of entertainers, executives and technicians, and stimulated the creative initiatives of Hispanic radio executives, brokers, and advertisers. Ownership was increasingly concentrated in the 1960s and 1970s. The industry sponsored the now-defunct trade publication <i>Sponsor</i> from the late 1940s to 1968.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-192" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-192"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>190<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Spanish-language radio has influenced American and Hispanic discourse on key current affairs issues such as citizenship and immigration.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-193" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-193"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>191<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading4"><h4 id="Networks">Networks</h4><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a Spanish-language news network based in <a href="/wiki/Atlanta,_Georgia" class="mw-redirect" title="Atlanta, Georgia">Atlanta, Georgia</a>;</li>\n<li><a href="/wiki/ESPN_Deportes" title="ESPN href="/wiki/List_of_television_stations_in_North_America_by_media_market" title="List of television stations in North America by media market">U.S. market</a>, and numerous affiliates internationally;\n<ul><li><a href="/wiki/TeleXitos" title="TeleXitos">TeleXitos</a> an American Spanish language digital multicast television network owned by NBCUniversal Telemundo class="mw-redirect" title="List of Spanish-language television channels">Spanish-language television network</a> in the United States, with affiliates in nearly every major U.S. market, and numerous affiliates internationally. It is the country\'s fourth-largest network overall;<sup id="cite&#95;ref-194" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-194"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>192<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n<ul><li><a href="/wiki/UniM%C3%A1s" title="UniMás">UniMás</a>, an American Spanish language free-to-air television network owned by <a href="/wiki/TelevisaUnivision" title="TelevisaUnivision">TelevisaUnivision</a>.</li>\n<li><a href="/wiki/Fusion_TV" title="Fusion TV">Fusion TV</a>, an English television channel targeting Hispanic entertainment programming;</li></ul></li>\n<li><a href="/wiki/Estrella_TV" title="Estrella TV">Estrella TV</a>, an American Spanish-language broadcast television network owned by the Estrella Media.</li>\n<li><a href="/wiki/V-me" title="V-me">V-me</a>, a Spanish-language television network;\n<ul><li><a href="/wiki/Primo_TV" title="Primo TV">Primo TV</a>, an English-language cable channel aimed at Hispanic youth.;</li></ul></li>\n<li><a href="/wiki/Azteca_Am%C3%A9rica" title="Azteca América">Azteca América</a>, a Spanish-language television network in the United States, with affiliates in nearly every major U.S. market, and numerous affiliates internationally;</li>\n<li><a href="/wiki/Fuse_(TV_channel)" title="Fuse (TV channel)">Fuse</a>, a former music channel that merged with the Hispanic-oriented <a href="/wiki/NuvoTV" title="NuvoTV">NuvoTV</a> in 2015.\n<ul><li><a href="/wiki/FM_(TV_channel)" class="mw-redirect" title="FM (TV channel)">FM</a>, a music-centric channel that replaced NuvoTV following the latter\'s merger with Fuse in 2015.</li></ul></li>\n<li><a href="/wiki/3ABN" class="mw-redirect" title="3ABN">3ABN</a> Latino, a Spanish-language Christian television USA">TBN Enlace USA</a>, a Spanish-language Christian television network based in <a href="/wiki/Tustin,_California" title="Tustin, California">Tustin, California</a>;</li></ul>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading4"><h4 id="Print">Print</h4><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<ul><li><i><a href="/wiki/La_Opini%C3%B3n" title="La Opinión">La Opinión</a></i>, a Spanish-language daily newspaper published in Los Angeles, California and distributed throughout the six counties of <a href="/wiki/Southern_California" title="Southern California">Southern California</a>. It is the largest Spanish-language newspaper in the United States</li>\n<li><i><a href="/wiki/El_Nuevo_Herald" title="El Nuevo Herald">El Nuevo Herald</a></i> and <i>Diario Las Américas</i>, Spanish-language daily newspapers serving the greater <a href="/wiki/Miami,_Florida" class="mw-redirect" title="Miami, Florida">Miami, Florida</a>, market</li>\n<li><i><a href="/wiki/El_Tiempo_Latino"
