scope="row" class="infobox-label">Website</th><td class="infobox-data"><span class="url"><a rel="nofollow" class="external text" href="http://www.puebla.gob.mx/">www<wbr />.puebla<wbr />.gob<wbr />.mx</a></span></td></tr></tbody></table>\n<p><b>Puebla</b>,<sup id="cite&#95;ref-9" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-9"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>a<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> officially the <b>Free and Sovereign State of Puebla</b>,<sup id="cite&#95;ref-10" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-10"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>b<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> is one of the 31 states that, along with <a href="/wiki/Mexico_City" title="Mexico City">Mexico City</a>, comprise the <a href="/wiki/Political_divisions_of_Mexico" class="mw-redirect" title="Political divisions of Mexico">Federal Entities</a> of <a href="/wiki/Mexico" title="Mexico">Mexico</a>. It is divided into <a href="/wiki/Municipalities_of_Puebla" title="Municipalities of Puebla">217 municipalities</a> and its capital is <a href="/wiki/Puebla_(city)" title="Puebla (city)">Puebla City</a>. Part of east-central Mexico, it is bordered by the states of <a href="/wiki/Veracruz" title="Veracruz">Veracruz</a> to the north and east, <a href="/wiki/Hidalgo_(state)" title="Hidalgo (state)">Hidalgo</a>, <a href="/wiki/State_of_Mexico" title="State of Mexico">México</a>, <a href="/wiki/Tlaxcala" title="Tlaxcala">Tlaxcala</a> and <a href="/wiki/Morelos" title="Morelos">Morelos</a> to the west, and <a href="/wiki/Guerrero" title="Guerrero">Guerrero</a> and <a href="/wiki/Oaxaca" title="Oaxaca">Oaxaca</a> to the south. The origins of the state lie in the city of Puebla, which was founded by the Spanish in this valley in 1531 to secure the trade route between <a href="/wiki/Mexico_City" title="Mexico City">Mexico City</a> and the <a href="/wiki/Veracruz,_Veracruz" class="mw-redirect" title="Veracruz, Veracruz">port of Veracruz</a>. By the end of the 18th century, the area had become a colonial province with its own governor, which would become the State of Puebla, after the <a href="/wiki/Mexican_War_of_Independence" title="Mexican War of Independence">Mexican War of Independence</a> in the early 19th century. Since that time the area, especially around the capital city, has continued to grow economically, mostly through industry, despite being the scene of a number of battles, the most notable of which being the <a href="/wiki/Battle_of_Puebla" title="Battle of Puebla">Battle of Puebla</a>. Today, the state is one of the most industrialized in the country, but since most of its development is concentrated in Puebla and other cities, many of its rural areas are undeveloped.\n</p><p>The state is home to the <i><a href="/wiki/China_poblana" title="China poblana">china poblana</a></i>, <a href="/wiki/Mole_poblano" class="mw-redirect" title="Mole poblano">mole poblano</a>, active literary and arts scenes, and festivals such as <a href="/wiki/Cinco_de_Mayo" title="Cinco de Mayo">Cinco de Mayo</a>, Ritual of Quetzalcoatl, <a href="/wiki/Day_of_the_Dead" title="Day of the Dead">Day of the Dead</a> celebrations (especially in <a href="/wiki/Huaquechula" title="Huaquechula">Huaquechula</a>) and <a href="/wiki/Carnival" title="Carnival">Carnival</a> (especially in <a href="/wiki/Carnival_of_Huejotzingo" title="Carnival of Huejotzingo">Huejotzingo</a>). It is home to five major indigenous groups: <a href="/wiki/Nahuas" title="Nahuas">Nahuas</a>, the <a href="/wiki/Totonac" title="Totonac">Totonacs</a>, the <a href="/wiki/Mixtec" title="Mixtec">Mixtecs</a>, the <a href="/wiki/Popoloca" class="mw-redirect" title="Popoloca">Popolocas</a> and the <a href="/wiki/Otomi_people" class="mw-redirect" title="Otomi people">Otomi</a>, which can mostly be found in the far north and the far south of the state.\n</p>\n<meta property="mw:PageProp/toc" />\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Geography">Geography</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Puebla&amp;action=edit&amp;section=1" title="Edit section: Geography"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<p>The state is in the central highlands of Mexico between the <a href="/wiki/Trans-Mexican_Volcanic_Belt" title="Trans-Mexican Volcanic Belt">Sierra Nevada</a> and the <a href="/wiki/Sierra_Madre_Oriental" title="Sierra Madre Oriental">Sierra Madre Oriental</a>. It has a triangular shape with its narrow part to the north. It borders the states of Veracruz, Oaxaca, Guerrero, Morelos, State of Mexico, Tlaxcala and Hidalgo. The state occupies 33,919&#160;km<sup>2</sup>, ranking 20th of 31 states in size, and has \n4,930 named communities.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-mediofisico&#95;11-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-mediofisico-11"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>9<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Mountains">Mountains</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Puebla&amp;action=edit&amp;section=2" title="Edit section: Mountains"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<p>Most of the mountains of Puebla belong to the Sierra Madre Oriental and the Trans-Mexican Volcanic Belt. The first is locally called the Sierra Norte del Puebla, entering the state from the northwest and then breaks up into the smaller chains of Sierra de Zacapoaxtla, Sierra de Huauchinango, Sierra de Teziutlán, Sierra de Tetela de Ocampo, Sierra de Chignahuapan and Sierra de Zacatlán, although these names may vary among localities. Some of the highest elevations include Apulco, Chichat, Chignahuapan, Soltepec and Tlatlaquitepec. The highest elevations are the volcanoes <a href="/wiki/Pico_de_Orizaba" title="Pico de Orizaba">Pico de Orizaba</a> or Citlaltepetl (5,747masl), <a href="/wiki/Popocat%C3%A9petl" title="Popocatépetl">Popocatépetl</a> (5,452masl), <a href="/wiki/Iztacc%C3%ADhuatl" class="mw-redirect" title="Iztaccíhuatl">Iztaccíhuatl</a> (5,286masl) and <a href="/wiki/Matlalcueitl_(volcano)" class="mw-redirect" title="Matlalcueitl (volcano)">Malinche</a> (4,461masl) which are found on the state\'s borders with Veracruz, Mexico State and Tlaxcala respectively. In the south of the state, the major elevations are the Sierra de Atenahuacán, Zapotitlán, Lomerio al Suroeste and the Sierra de Tehuacán. Dividing much of the state from Veracruz is a small chain of mountains called the Sierra Madre del Golfo.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-mediofisico&#95;11-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-mediofisico-11"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>9<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>The natural geography of the state subdivides into the Huasteco Plateau, Llanuras y Lomeríos zone, Lagos y Volcanes del Anáhuac, Chiconquiaco, Llanuras y Sierras de Querétaro e Hidalgo, Cordillera Costera del Sur, Mixteca Alta, Sierras y Valles Guerrenses, Sierras Centrales de Oaxaca, Sierras Orientales and Sur de Puebla. The Huasteco Plateau and the Llanuras y Lomeríos zone are located in the north and northeast, with the Lagos y Volcanes del Anáhuc in the center and north. Together, they account for over 50% of the state. The east and northeast are occupies by the Chiconquiaco and Llanudras y Sierras de Querétaro e Hidalgo areas and account for about three percent of the state. The Cordillera del Sur and Mixteca Alta are located in the west and southwest covering less than 2.5% of the state. The Sur de Puebla is in the southwest and accounts for 26% of the state. Other southern subregions include the Sierras y Valles Guerrerenses, the Sierras Centrales de Oaxaca and the Sierras Orientales. Together, they account for about 15% of the state.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-mediofisico&#95;11-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-mediofisico-11"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>9<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Hydrology">Hydrology</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Puebla&amp;action=edit&amp;section=3" title="Edit section: Hydrology"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:R%C3%ADo_Petlapa.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/cd/R%C3%ADo_Petlapa.jpg/250px-R%C3%ADo_Petlapa.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="188" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/cd/R%C3%ADo_Petlapa.jpg/500px-R%C3%ADo_Petlapa.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="2576" data-file-height="1932" /></a><figcaption><a href="/w/index.php?title=Petlapa_River&amp;action=edit&amp;redlink=1" class="new" title="Petlapa River (page does not exist)">Petlapa River</a></figcaption></figure>\n<p>The hydrology of Puebla is formed by three major river systems. One is based on the <a href="/wiki/Balsas_River" title="Balsas River">Balsas River</a>, also known as the Atoyac, which originates with the melting runoff of the Halos, Telapón and Papagayo mountains along with those from the Iztaccihuatl volcano and waters from the Zahuapan River, which enters from Tlaxcala. This river receives further water from tributaries such as the Acateno, Atila, Amacuzac, Molinos and Cohetzala. The river has one major dam called Valsequllo or Manuel Avila Camacho. This river eventually flows west to the <a href="/wiki/Pacific_Ocean" title="Pacific Ocean">Pacific Ocean</a>. The next system empties into the Gulf of Mexico and consists of the <a href="/wiki/Pantepec_River" title="Pantepec River">Pantepec</a>, <a href="/wiki/Cazones_River" title="Cazones River">Cazones</a>, <a href="/wiki/Necaxa_River" title="Necaxa River">Necaxa</a>, Laxaxalpan, San Pedro/Zun, Zempoala, Apulco, Cedro Viejo, Salteros, Martínez de la Torre and other rivers on the east side of the state. This system has two major dams called the Necaxa and Mazatepec. The third is the closed <a href="/wiki/Oriental_Basin" title="Oriental Basin">Oriental Basin</a>, with a large number of small lakes fresh water springs as well as some volcanically heated springs. The best known of these include Chignahuapan, Agua Azúl, Amalucan, Cisnaqullas, Garcicrespo, Almoloya and Rancho Colorado. Lakes include Chapulco, San Bernardino, Lagunas Epatlán, Ayutla, Almoloyan, Alchichica, Pahuatlán, Las Minas, Aljojuca and Tecuitlapa.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-mediofisico&#95;11-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-mediofisico-11"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>9<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Climate">Climate</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Puebla&amp;action=edit&amp;section=4" title="Edit section: Climate"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-left" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:PiedrasEncimadas90.JPG" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f2/PiedrasEncimadas90.JPG/250px-PiedrasEncimadas90.JPG" decoding="async" width="250" height="167" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f2/PiedrasEncimadas90.JPG/500px-PiedrasEncimadas90.JPG 1.5x" data-file-width="3872" data-file-height="2592" /></a><figcaption>Fog in the mountains near <a href="/wiki/Zacatl%C3%A1n" title="Zacatlán">Zacatlán</a></figcaption></figure>\n<p>Puebla has many different climates owing to its range of altitudes. It has an average temperature of 16&#160;°C (61&#160;°F) but this varies greatly locally. There is a rainy season from May until October with an overall precipitation of 801&#160;mm (31.54&#160;in). The state has eleven different climate zones, but five predominate. The centre and south of the state has a temperate and semi-moist climate, with an average temperature of 15&#160;°C (59&#160;°F) and 858&#160;mm (33.78&#160;in) of rainfall. The southwest has a warm to hot and semi-moist climate with 830&#160;mm (32.68&#160;in) of precipitation and 22&#160;°C (72&#160;°F) average temperature. The north is also warm and hot, and additionally very wet; it has a 22&#160;°C (72&#160;°F) average temperature but with an average rainfall of 2,250&#160;mm (88.58&#160;in). The southeast is semi-dry with warm and temperate temperatures, having an average temperature of 22&#160;°C (72&#160;°F) and precipitation of 550&#160;mm (21.65&#160;in). The high volcano peaks have a cold climate.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-mediofisico&#95;11-4" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-mediofisico-11"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>9<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Ecosystems">Ecosystems</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Puebla&amp;action=edit&amp;section=5" title="Edit section: Ecosystems"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Barranca_Zacatl%C3%A1n_CRC.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/74/Barranca_Zacatl%C3%A1n_CRC.jpg/250px-Barranca_Zacatl%C3%A1n_CRC.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="58" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/74/Barranca_Zacatl%C3%A1n_CRC.jpg/500px-Barranca_Zacatl%C3%A1n_CRC.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="1767" data-file-height="408" /></a><figcaption>Ravines at Zacatlán</figcaption></figure>\n<p>The state has three main ecosystems, tropical rainforests, forests in temperate and cold areas, and arid and semi-arid zones.\n</p><p>Tropical forests are divided into moist, semi-moist and dry forests. These can be found in the Huasteca Plateau, Chiconguiaco, Lagos y Volcánes de Anahuac, Sur de Puebla, Cordillera Costera del Sur, Sierras y Valles Guerrerenses, Sierras Orientales, Sierras Centrales de Oaxaca and Mixteca Alta. The most common species include <i><a href="/w/index.php?title=Ceiba_parviflora&amp;action=edit&amp;redlink=1" class="new" title="Ceiba parviflora (page does not exist)">Ceiba parviflora</a>, <a href="/wiki/Bursera_simaruba" title="Bursera simaruba">Bursera simaruba</a>, <a href="/wiki/Cedrela_odorata" title="Cedrela odorata">Cedrela odorata</a>, <a href="/wiki/Swietenia_macrophylla" title="Swietenia macrophylla">Swietenia macrophylla</a>, <a href="/wiki/Spondias_mombin" title="Spondias mombin">Spondias mombin</a>, <a href="/wiki/Brosimum_alicastrum" title="Brosimum alicastrum">Brosimum alicastrum</a>, <a href="/w/index.php?title=Coccoloba_barbadensis&amp;action=edit&amp;redlink=1" class="new" title="Coccoloba barbadensis (page does not exist)">Coccoloba barbadensis</a>, <a href="/wiki/Pithecellobium_arboreum" class="mw-redirect" title="Pithecellobium arboreum">Pithecellobium arboreum</a>, <a href="/wiki/Lysiloma_divaricatum" title="Lysiloma divaricatum">Lysiloma divaricatum</a>, <a href="/w/index.php?title=Phoebe_tampicensis&amp;action=edit&amp;redlink=1" class="new" title="Phoebe tampicensis (page does not exist)">Phoebe tampicensis</a>, <a href="/w/index.php?title=Acacia_coulteri&amp;action=edit&amp;redlink=1" class="new" title="Acacia coulteri (page does not exist)">Acacia coulteri</a></i> and <i><a href="/wiki/Ficus" title="Ficus">Ficus spp.</a></i> These forests are also exploited for wood and other products, including traditional handcrafts. Low growing plants are used to feed livestock. Little is known about the ecosystems of these forests, but it is known that these areas are important to the regulation of water in area rivers. Human activity has severely damaged over 32,000 hectares.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-mediofisico&#95;11-5" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-mediofisico-11"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>9<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>Tropical forests are divided by altitude. Upper forests are characterized by dense vegetation in fairly humid climates. The tree canopy reaches an average height of 15 meters. Not all species are evergreen, with a number losing leaves during the dry season. During the same season, a number of species also flower. For this reason, these forests never completely lose their color. Common species include <i><a href="/wiki/Cedrela" title="Cedrela">Cedrela sp.</a>, <a href="/wiki/Brosimum_alicastrum" title="Brosimum alicastrum">Brosimum alicastrum</a>, <a href="/wiki/Heliocarpus" title="Heliocarpus">Heliocarpus spp.</a>, <a href="/wiki/Calophyllum_brasiliense" title="Calophyllum brasiliense">Calophyllum brasiliense</a>, <a href="/wiki/Zuelania_guidonia" class="mw-redirect" title="Zuelania guidonia">Zuelania guidonia</a></i> and <i><a href="/wiki/Ficus" title="Ficus">Ficus spp.</a></i> Most forests of this type are located near the borders with Veracruz and Hidalgo. Tropical forests at lower altitudes are found in areas with median temperatures of over 20 C, and annual rainfall of between 800 and 1,200&#160;mm (47.24&#160;in). These areas often have a dry season of seven or eight months, and many of these forests will lose most or all of their leaves during this time. Common species include <i><a href="/wiki/Bursera_simaruba" title="Bursera simaruba">Bursera simaruba</a>, Lysiloma divaricatum, <a href="/w/index.php?title=Phoebe_tampicensis&amp;action=edit&amp;redlink=1" class="new" title="Phoebe tampicensis (page does not exist)">Phoebe tampicensis</a>, <a href="/w/index.php?title=Acacia_coulteri&amp;action=edit&amp;redlink=1" class="new" title="Acacia coulteri (page does not exist)">Acacia coulteri</a>, <a href="/wiki/Beaucarnea_recurvata" title="Beaucarnea recurvata">Beaucarnea recurvata</a>, <a href="/w/index.php?title=Lysiloma_acapulcensis&amp;action=edit&amp;redlink=1" class="new" title="Lysiloma acapulcensis (page does not exist)">Lysiloma acapulcensis</a></i> and <i><a href="/wiki/Zuelania_guidonia" class="mw-redirect" title="Zuelania guidonia">Zuelania guidonia</a></i>.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-mediofisico&#95;11-6" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-mediofisico-11"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>9<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>Colder <a href="/wiki/Trans-Mexican_Volcanic_Belt_pine%E2%80%93oak_forests" title="Trans-Mexican Volcanic Belt pine–oak forests">pine–oak forests</a> can be found in the Huasteca Plateau, <a href="/wiki/Sierra_de_Chiconquiaco" title="Sierra de Chiconquiaco">Sierra de Chiconquiaco</a>, Lagos de Volcanos de Anáhuac, Sierras Orientales and Sierras Centrales de Oaxaca. These forests mostly consist of pines, <a href="/wiki/Oak" title="Oak">oaks</a>, <a href="/wiki/Oyamel" class="mw-redirect" title="Oyamel">oyamel</a> fir and other conifers (<i><a href="/wiki/Abies_religiosa" title="Abies religiosa">Abies religiosa</a>, <a href="/wiki/Pinus_pseudostrobus" title="Pinus pseudostrobus">Pinus pseudostrobus</a>, <a href="/wiki/Pinus_attenuata" class="mw-redirect" title="Pinus attenuata">Pinus attenuata</a>, <a href="/wiki/Pinus_ayacahuite" title="Pinus ayacahuite">Pinus ayacahuite</a>, <a href="/wiki/Pinus_leiophylla" title="Pinus leiophylla">Pinus leiophylla</a>, <a href="/wiki/Pinus_patula" title="Pinus patula">Pinus patula</a>, <a href="/wiki/Pinus_teocote" title="Pinus teocote">Pinus teocote</a>, <a href="/wiki/Quercus" class="mw-redirect" title="Quercus">Quercus spp</a>, <a href="/wiki/Quercus_rugosa" title="Quercus rugosa">Quercus rugosa</a>, <a href="/wiki/Alder" title="Alder">Alnus spp</a>, <a href="/wiki/Arbutus" title="Arbutus">Arbutus spp</a>, <a href="/wiki/Cupressus" title="Cupressus">Cupressus spp</a></i> and <i><a href="/wiki/Juniperus" class="mw-redirect" title="Juniperus">Juniperus spp.</a></i>). Much of these areas have been extensively logged and some areas are used to farm trees. These trees are used for wood, paper and other wood-derived products. Due to human activity over 107,000 hectares are considered to be severely damaged.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-mediofisico&#95;11-7" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-mediofisico-11"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>9<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p>\n<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-left" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:ValleyNaupan05.JPG" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/19/ValleyNaupan05.JPG/250px-ValleyNaupan05.JPG" decoding="async" width="250" height="167" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/19/ValleyNaupan05.JPG/500px-ValleyNaupan05.JPG 1.5x" data-file-width="3872" data-file-height="2592" /></a><figcaption>Pine forest near <a href="/wiki/Huauchinango" title="Huauchinango">Huauchinango</a> in the Sierra Norte</figcaption></figure>\n<p>Temperate and cold area forests cover just under 22% of the surface of the state with various species of pine accounting for more than 80% of the trees. These are mostly found in the higher elevations of the mountains where the average temperature is around 15C and at heights of between 2,500 and 2,750masl. Above 3,000m <i><a href="/wiki/Pinus_hartwegii" title="Pinus hartwegii">Pinus hartwegii</a></i> is dominant. Pine species which are the most economically valuable and include <i><a href="/wiki/Pinus_montezumae" title="Pinus montezumae">Pinus montezumae</a>, <a href="/wiki/Pinus_pseudostrobus" title="Pinus pseudostrobus">Pinus pseudostrobus</a>, <a href="/wiki/Pinus_ayacahuite" title="Pinus ayacahuite">Pinus ayacahuite</a>, <a href="/wiki/Pinus_greggii" title="Pinus greggii">Pinus greggii</a>, Pinus hartwegii, <a href="/wiki/Pinus_lawsonii" title="Pinus lawsonii">Pinus lawsonii</a>, <a href="/wiki/Pinus_leiophylla" title="Pinus leiophylla">Pinus leiophylla</a>, <a href="/wiki/Pinus_michoacana" class="mw-redirect" title="Pinus michoacana">Pinus michoacana</a>, <a href="/wiki/Pinus_oocarpa" title="Pinus oocarpa">Pinus oocarpa</a>, <a href="/wiki/Pinus_patula" title="Pinus patula">Pinus patula</a></i> and <i><a href="/wiki/Pinus_teocote" title="Pinus teocote">Pinus teocote</a></i>. The second most common kind of forest is dominated by oyamel fir, often intermingling with pines and oaks. These forests are found at altitudes of between 2,500 and 3,600masl and with an average temperature of between 7 and 15C and annual precipitation of 1,000&#160;mm (39.37&#160;in). Forests with trees such as <i>Juniperus</i> spp., <i><a href="/wiki/Pseudotsuga" title="Pseudotsuga">Pseudotsuga spp.</a>, <a href="/wiki/Pseudotsuga_menziesii" class="mw-redirect" title="Pseudotsuga menziesii">Pseudotsuga menziesii</a></i>, and <i><a href="/wiki/Cupressus_lindleyi" class="mw-redirect" title="Cupressus lindleyi">Cupressus lindleyi</a></i> can also be found.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-mediofisico&#95;11-8" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-mediofisico-11"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>9<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>The arid and semi arid area can be found in the Lagos y Volcanes de Anáhuac, Sur de Puebla, Cordillera Costera del Sur, Sierras y Valles Guerrerenses, Sierras Orientales and Sierras Centrales de Oaxaca. Types of vegetation often found includes mesquite, huizachal and agave, with species such as <i>Agave</i> spp, <i>Yuca</i> spp, <i><a href="/wiki/Opuntia" title="Opuntia">Opuntia</a></i> spp, <i>Aristida</i> spp., and <i>Stipa</i> spp. There is no forestry here but a number of plants are used for fibers, waxes, resins, handcrafts, medicine and a number are edible to both humans and livestock. Many of these arid areas subdivide into microclimates depending on minor variations in temperature and precipitation. Some areas, especially dry grasslands, have suffered overgrazing and soil erosion.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-mediofisico&#95;11-9" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-mediofisico-11"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>9<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>In the south, near Puebla\'s borders with Oaxaca and Guerrero are dry mountainous areas, some of which are completely devoid of vegetation, similar to African deserts. Other are populated only by the occasional cactus, with those belonging to the <i><a href="/wiki/Fouquieria" title="Fouquieria">Fouquieria</a></i> genus standing out on the landscape. Where there are arroyos, the vegetation changes drastically to include a wide variety of plants packed along a narrow strip. Other areas in this part of the state are semi-arid, home to a variety of plant and bird species.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-mexdesdesierto&#95;12-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-mexdesdesierto-12"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>10<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Natural_attractions">Natural attractions</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Puebla&amp;action=edit&amp;section=6" title="Edit section: Natural attractions"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Paco_en_el_Pico_de_Orizaba_2.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a6/Paco_en_el_Pico_de_Orizaba_2.jpg/250px-Paco_en_el_Pico_de_Orizaba_2.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="188" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a6/Paco_en_el_Pico_de_Orizaba_2.jpg/500px-Paco_en_el_Pico_de_Orizaba_2.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="2592" data-file-height="1944" /></a><figcaption>View from the summit of Pico de Orizaba</figcaption></figure>\n<p>Natural attractions in the state include the Bosque Mesófilos de la Sierra Madre Oriental in the north of the state, <a href="/wiki/Piedras_Encimadas_Valley" title="Piedras Encimadas Valley">Piedras Encimadas Valley</a>, <a href="/wiki/Izta-Popo_Zoquiapan_National_Park" class="mw-redirect" title="Izta-Popo Zoquiapan National Park">Izta-Popo Zoquiapan National Park</a>, <a href="/wiki/La_Malinche_National_Park" title="La Malinche National Park">La Malinche National Park</a>, and the <a href="/wiki/Pico_de_Orizaba_National_Park" class="mw-redirect" title="Pico de Orizaba National Park">Pico de Orizaba National Park</a>.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-rincones5253&#95;13-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-rincones5253-13"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>11<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> The best known wilderness area is the Izta-Popo National park, which the state shares with neighboring <a href="/wiki/State_of_Mexico" title="State of Mexico">State of Mexico</a>. It is located only 55&#160;km (34&#160;mi) west of the state capital and the two often snow covered volcanoes are easily visible from this area, and important to the state culturally. The park is an area protected by the federal government because of its biological diversity and considered to be the "lungs" of the area due to its forests. Access to the park, especially to the volcanoes themselves is more restricted than in the past due to past ecological damage. Even further restrictions are put into place when the Popocatepetl volcano is active. However, the park has numerous hiking and horse paths in the forests that cover the lower elevations. On the slopes, there are many small caves, which in pre-Hispanic times were often used for ceremonies.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-rincones56&#95;14-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-rincones56-14"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>12<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>The Sierra Madre Oriental, locally called the Sierra Norte, is a series of rugged mountains covered in abundant vegetation, which has had an isolating effect on the people here over the centuries.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-rincones59&#95;15-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-rincones59-15"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>13<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> The Valle de Piedras Encimadas (Valley of the Stacked Stones) is located near the town of <a href="/wiki/Zacatl%C3%A1n_(municipality)" title="Zacatlán (municipality)">Zacatlán</a>. It is really a series of small valleys covering 400 hectares filled with conifer forest. The attraction here are the stone formations which resemble stones stacked one over the other which take on numerous forms. Some have been said to resemble objects such as dogs, elephants, human heads and monsters. Most of the area is only accessible by foot or horseback.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-rincones66&#95;16-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-rincones66-16"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>14<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>In the center of the state, just before the land rises to the north to form the Sierra Norte, there is an area called the <a href="/wiki/Oriental_Basin" title="Oriental Basin">Oriental Basin</a> filled with lakes, both with water and dry. The dry lakebeds contain water only during the rainy season, which runs from summer through fall. The two largest are Salado and Totocingo Lakes. The first is seven km long and two km wide and the second is larger. The largest "wet" lakes are Laguna Preciosa, Laguna Quechulac, Laguna de Atexcac and Laguna de Aijojuca.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-rincones8182&#95;17-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-rincones8182-17"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>15<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="History">History</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Puebla&amp;action=edit&amp;section=7" title="Edit section: History"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<figure typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Las_Bocas_Olmec_baby-face_figurine_(Bookgrrrl).jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4e/Las_Bocas_Olmec_baby-face_figurine_%28Bookgrrrl%29.jpg/250px-Las_Bocas_Olmec_baby-face_figurine_%28Bookgrrrl%29.jpg" decoding="async" width="175" height="233" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4e/Las_Bocas_Olmec_baby-face_figurine_%28Bookgrrrl%29.jpg/330px-Las_Bocas_Olmec_baby-face_figurine_%28Bookgrrrl%29.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4e/Las_Bocas_Olmec_baby-face_figurine_%28Bookgrrrl%29.jpg/500px-Las_Bocas_Olmec_baby-face_figurine_%28Bookgrrrl%29.jpg 2x" data-file-width="960" data-file-height="1280" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Olmec_figurine" title="Olmec figurine">Olmec figurine</a> of <a href="/wiki/Las_Bocas" title="Las Bocas">Las Bocas</a></figcaption></figure>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Pre-Hispanic_period">Pre-Hispanic period</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Puebla&amp;action=edit&amp;section=8" title="Edit section: Pre-Hispanic period"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<p>The territory of the state was one of the first in modern Mexico to be inhabited by humans. Most of the earliest settlements have been found in the valley of Tehuacán, with the oldest near the Agujereado Mountain, which dates back to 10,000 BCE. At this site the oldest sample of corn ever found in the world has been found, which dates back to 1500 BCE.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-rincones32&#95;18-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-rincones32-18"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>16<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Along with Agujereado Mountain, there are more than 450 prehistoric sites in the Tehuacan Valley alone. Stone tools date to between 6500 and 4900 BCE, and evidence of agriculture to 3500 and 2000 BCE in areas such as <a href="/w/index.php?title=Aljojuca_(municipality)&amp;action=edit&amp;redlink=1" class="new" title="Aljojuca (municipality) (page does not exist)">Aljojuca</a>, <a href="/w/index.php?title=Totimiuacan&amp;action=edit&amp;redlink=1" class="new" title="Totimiuacan (page does not exist)">Totimiuacan</a>, <a href="/wiki/Cholula,_Puebla" title="Cholula, Puebla">Cholula</a> and <a href="/wiki/Iz%C3%BAcar_de_Matamoros" title="Izúcar de Matamoros">Izucar</a>. By 900 BCE, there is ample evidence of the cultivation of corn, beans, squash, <a href="/wiki/Chili_pepper" title="Chili pepper">chili peppers</a> and cotton. The rise of city states was established by 700 BCE.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-enchistoria&#95;19-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-enchistoria-19"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>17<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>By the <a href="/wiki/Mesoamerica" title="Mesoamerica">Mesoamerican</a> period, the area was inhabited by a number of ethnicities. The regions of <a href="/wiki/Acatl%C3%A1n_de_Osorio,_Puebla" class="mw-redirect" title="Acatlán de Osorio, Puebla">Acatlán</a> and part of <a href="/w/index.php?title=Chiautla_(municipality)&amp;action=edit&amp;redlink=1" class="new" title="Chiautla (municipality) (page does not exist)">Chiautla</a> were dominated by the <a href="/wiki/Mixtec" title="Mixtec">Mixtecs</a>. <a href="/wiki/Tepexi_de_Rodr%C3%ADguez_(municipality)" class="mw-redirect" title="Tepexi de Rodríguez (municipality)">Tepexi</a> was dominated by the Popolocas. The central part of the state was dominated by the <a href="/wiki/Olmec-Xicalancas" class="mw-redirect" title="Olmec-Xicalancas">Olmec-Xicalancas</a> and <a href="/wiki/Nahuas" title="Nahuas">Nahuas</a>, with strong cultural links to the <a href="/wiki/Toltec" title="Toltec">Toltec</a>-based culture at Cholula. The north was populated by the <a href="/wiki/Totonac" title="Totonac">Totonacs</a>, the <a href="/wiki/Mazatec_people" class="mw-redirect" title="Mazatec people">Mazatecs</a> and the <a href="/wiki/Otomi_peoples" class="mw-redirect" title="Otomi peoples">Otomi</a>, whose cultural center was in <a href="/wiki/El_Taj%C3%ADn" title="El Tajín">El Tajín</a>. In the 14th century, <a href="/wiki/Nonoalca" title="Nonoalca">Nonoalca</a> ruler Xelhua, came to dominate almost all of the territory of Puebla. In the 15th century, <a href="/wiki/Aztec_Empire" title="Aztec Empire">Aztec domination</a> took over the same area and more. Initially, the center and south areas were under the control of <a href="/wiki/Tenochtitlan" title="Tenochtitlan">Tenochtitlan</a> with <a href="/wiki/Texcoco_(altepetl)" class="mw-redirect" title="Texcoco (altepetl)">Texcoco</a> dominant in the north. Aztec domination continued until the Spanish Conquest.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-enchistoria&#95;19-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-enchistoria-19"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>17<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Viceroyalty_of_New_Spain_(1535–1821)"><span id="Viceroyalty_of_New_Spain_.281535.E2.80.931821.29"></span>Viceroyalty of New Spain (1535–1821)</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Puebla&amp;action=edit&amp;section=9" title="Edit section: Viceroyalty of New Spain (1535–1821)"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-right" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Cholula_Massacre_(1519).jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/79/Cholula_Massacre_%281519%29.jpg/250px-Cholula_Massacre_%281519%29.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="195" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/7/79/Cholula_Massacre_%281519%29.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="370" data-file-height="288" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Spanish_conquest_of_the_Aztec_Empire#Massacre_of_Cholula" title="Spanish conquest of the Aztec Empire">Massacre of Cholula</a></figcaption></figure>\n<p><a href="/wiki/Hern%C3%A1n_Cort%C3%A9s" title="Hernán Cortés">Hernán Cortés</a> entered Puebla state in 1519, along with his indigenous allies from Veracruz, on his way to <a href="/wiki/Tlaxcala_(Nahua_state)" title="Tlaxcala (Nahua state)">Tlaxcala</a>.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-sucesos&#95;20-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-sucesos-20"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>18<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> The Spanish takeover of the Puebla area was relatively easy. Many of the peoples here were under Aztec domination and saw the foreigners as a way to escape.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-rincones32&#95;18-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-rincones32-18"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>16<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> One notable exception was the city of Cholula. While negotiating with the city\'s leaders, Cortés was told of a plot to attack him and his men. Cortés ordered his army to commit the <a href="/wiki/Spanish_conquest_of_the_Aztec_Empire#Massacre_of_Cholula" title="Spanish conquest of the Aztec Empire">Massacre of Cholula</a> on 12 October 1519. This act terrified those who opposed the Spanish and they submitted.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-sucesos&#95;20-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-sucesos-20"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>18<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> In 1520, after his initial defeat in Tenochtitlan (<a href="/wiki/La_Noche_Triste" title="La Noche Triste">La Noche Triste</a>) Hernán Cortés founded a Spanish settlement at <a href="/wiki/Tepeaca_(municipality)" class="mw-redirect" title="Tepeaca (municipality)">Tepeaca</a>, and took areas such as <a href="/wiki/Huaquechula" title="Huaquechula">Huaquechula</a> and <a href="/w/index.php?title=Itzocan&amp;action=edit&amp;redlink=1" class="new" title="Itzocan (page does not exist)">Itzocan</a>. Many natives leaders then provided men and supplies for the conquest of Tenochtitlan in 1521, and later to go with <a href="/wiki/Pedro_de_Alvarado" title="Pedro de Alvarado">Pedro de Alvarado</a> to <a href="/wiki/Guatemala" title="Guatemala">Guatemala</a>.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-rincones32&#95;18-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-rincones32-18"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>16<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-enchistoria&#95;19-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-enchistoria-19"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>17<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Local indigenous governments survived in the very early colonial period, subject to the Spanish. These included Tuchpa, Tzicoac, Metztitlán, Tlapacoyan, Atotonilco, Tlatlaquitepec, Huaxtepec, Tepeaca, Tlacozautitlán, Quiauhteopan, Yoaltepec, Teotitlán del Camino, Cuautochco and Coixtlahuacan.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-enchistoria&#95;19-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-enchistoria-19"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>17<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p>\n<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-left" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Huejotzingo.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/84/Huejotzingo.jpg/250px-Huejotzingo.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="167" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/84/Huejotzingo.jpg/500px-Huejotzingo.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="960" data-file-height="640" /></a><figcaption>The <i>Convento de San Miguel Arcángel</i> in <a href="/wiki/Huejotzingo" title="Huejotzingo">Huejotzingo</a>, part of the <a href="/wiki/Monasteries_on_the_slopes_of_Popocat%C3%A9petl" title="Monasteries on the slopes of Popocatépetl">Monasteries on the slopes of Popocatépetl</a>.</figcaption></figure>\n<p>The origins of the modern state lie in the founding of the city of Puebla in the Cuetlaxcoapan Valley in 1531 by <a href="/wiki/Toribio_de_Benavente" title="Toribio de Benavente">Toribio de Benavente</a> and <a href="/wiki/Juan_de_Salmer%C3%B3n" title="Juan de Salmerón">Juan de Salmerón</a>.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-angelopolis&#95;21-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-angelopolis-21"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>19<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> The city was laid out by Hernando de Elgueta, marking out residential areas, commercial areas etc. The city received its royal seal in 1532 but flooding forced the settlement to move across the San Francisco River and start over that same year. The city\'s (and now state\'s) seal was granted in 1538.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-sucesos&#95;20-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-sucesos-20"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>18<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> The city of Puebla was created to secure the route between Mexico City and the port of Veracruz, and was initially populated by soldiers and those who made a living by providing shelter and supplies to travelers between the two cities. However, it soon became the economic and cultural center of the valley areas between the <a href="/wiki/Valley_of_Mexico" title="Valley of Mexico">Valley of Mexico</a> and the <a href="/wiki/Gulf_of_Mexico" title="Gulf of Mexico">Gulf Coast</a>, as it provided a starting point for Spanish settlement. The area\'s economy expanded rapidly as many Europeans and indigenous decided to settle permanently, with the settlement of Puebla reaching city status in 1532 with the name of Ciudad de los Angeles.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-rincones33&#95;22-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-rincones33-22"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>20<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p>\n<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-right" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Exconvento_franciscano_(siglo_XVI).jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a4/Exconvento_franciscano_%28siglo_XVI%29.jpg/250px-Exconvento_franciscano_%28siglo_XVI%29.jpg" decoding="async" width="190" height="253" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a4/Exconvento_franciscano_%28siglo_XVI%29.jpg/330px-Exconvento_franciscano_%28siglo_XVI%29.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a4/Exconvento_franciscano_%28siglo_XVI%29.jpg/500px-Exconvento_franciscano_%28siglo_XVI%29.jpg 2x" data-file-width="1536" data-file-height="2048" /></a><figcaption>Former Franciscan monastery at Tecali de Herrera</figcaption></figure>\n<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-right" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Cuetzalan_ig.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/32/Cuetzalan_ig.jpg/250px-Cuetzalan_ig.jpg" decoding="async" width="190" height="253" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/32/Cuetzalan_ig.jpg/330px-Cuetzalan_ig.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/32/Cuetzalan_ig.jpg/500px-Cuetzalan_ig.jpg 2x" data-file-width="1536" data-file-height="2048" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Cuetzalan_del_Progreso" class="mw-redirect" title="Cuetzalan del Progreso">Cuetzalan del Progreso</a></figcaption></figure>\n<p>The <a href="/wiki/Franciscans" title="Franciscans">Franciscans</a> were in charge of the evangelization process in the state, starting from 1524, when they founded the monastery of <a href="/wiki/Huejotzingo_(municipality)" class="mw-redirect" title="Huejotzingo (municipality)">Huejotzingo</a>. Between 1540 and 1560, they founded others such as those in <a href="/w/index.php?title=Tecamachalco_(municipality)&amp;action=edit&amp;redlink=1" class="new" title="Tecamachalco (municipality) (page does not exist)">Tecamachalco</a>, <a href="/wiki/Quecholac_(municipality)" class="mw-redirect" title="Quecholac (municipality)">Quecholac</a>, <a href="/wiki/Tecali_de_Herrera_(municipality)" class="mw-redirect" title="Tecali de Herrera (municipality)">Tecali</a>, <a href="/wiki/Calpan_(municipality)" class="mw-redirect" title="Calpan (municipality)">Calpan</a>, <a href="/wiki/Cuautinch%C3%A1n" title="Cuautinchán">Cuautinchán</a>, <a href="/wiki/Zacatl%C3%A1n_(municipality)" title="Zacatlán (municipality)">Zacatlán</a>, <a href="/wiki/Cholula,_Puebla" title="Cholula, Puebla">Cholula</a>, Huaquechula, Tepeaca, <a href="/wiki/Tehuac%C3%A1n_Municipality" class="mw-redirect" title="Tehuacán Municipality">Tehuacán</a>, <a href="/w/index.php?title=Xalpa&amp;action=edit&amp;redlink=1" class="new" title="Xalpa (page does not exist)">Xalpa</a> and <a href="/wiki/Coatepec,_Puebla" title="Coatepec, Puebla">Coatepec</a>. The <a href="/wiki/Augustinians" title="Augustinians">Augustinians</a> arrived next, constructing monasteries in <a href="/w/index.php?title=Chiautla_(municipality)&amp;action=edit&amp;redlink=1" class="new" title="Chiautla (municipality) (page does not exist)">Chiautla</a>, <a href="/wiki/Chietla_(municipality)" class="mw-redirect" title="Chietla (municipality)">Chietla</a>, <a href="/wiki/Huatlatlauca_(municipality)" class="mw-redirect" title="Huatlatlauca (municipality)">Huatlatlauca</a>, <a href="/wiki/Tlapa" class="mw-redirect" title="Tlapa">Tlapa</a>, <a href="/wiki/Xicotepec_(municipality)" class="mw-redirect" title="Xicotepec (municipality)">Xicotepec</a> and <a href="/w/index.php?title=Papaloticpac&amp;action=edit&amp;redlink=1" class="new" title="Papaloticpac (page does not exist)">Papaloticpac</a>. The last of the evangelists were the Dominicans, who built monasteries at <a href="/wiki/Iz%C3%BAcar_de_Matamoros" title="Izúcar de Matamoros">Izúcar de Matamoros</a>, <a href="/w/index.php?title=Tepapayeca&amp;action=edit&amp;redlink=1" class="new" title="Tepapayeca (page does not exist)">Tepapayeca</a>, <a href="/w/index.php?title=Huehuatl%C3%A1n&amp;action=edit&amp;redlink=1" class="new" title="Huehuatlán (page does not exist)">Huehuatlán</a> and <a href="/wiki/Tepexi_de_Rodr%C3%ADguez_(municipality)" class="mw-redirect" title="Tepexi de Rodríguez (municipality)">Tepexi</a>. The bishopric was established in 1526. Initially, the seat was in the <a href="/wiki/Yucat%C3%A1n_Peninsula" title="Yucatán Peninsula">Yucatán</a>, but it was eventually moved to <a href="/wiki/Tlaxcala" title="Tlaxcala">Tlaxcala</a>, then to Puebla by 1550. Eventually, its extension included the current states of Tlaxcala and Puebla during much of the colonial period.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-enchistoria&#95;19-4" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-enchistoria-19"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>17<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>In 1783, the royal government in Spain divided New Spain into "intendencias" or provinces, one of which was centered on the city of Puebla.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-enchistoria&#95;19-5" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-enchistoria-19"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>17<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> The first governor of Puebla was Manuel de Flon, Count of La Cadena.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-sucesos&#95;20-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-sucesos-20"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>18<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Initially, this intendencia included Tlaxcala, but it was separated out in 1793. Other parts were eventually separated out into other provinces/states such as Mexico, Guerrero and Veracruz.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-enchistoria&#95;19-6" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-enchistoria-19"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>17<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Post-independence">Post-independence</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Puebla&amp;action=edit&amp;section=10" title="Edit section: Post-independence"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<p>During the <a href="/wiki/Mexican_War_of_Independence" title="Mexican War of Independence">Mexican War of Independence</a>, the city of Puebla remained loyal to the <a href="/wiki/Viceroy" title="Viceroy">viceroy</a> in Mexico City, sending troops to defend it at the <a href="/wiki/Battle_of_Monte_de_las_Cruces" title="Battle of Monte de las Cruces">Battle of Monte de las Cruces</a> against <a href="/wiki/Miguel_Hidalgo_y_Costilla" title="Miguel Hidalgo y Costilla">Miguel Hidalgo y Costilla</a>. Ecclesiastical authorities in the Cathedral excommunicated insurgent priests and battles took place in Izúcar and Chiautla. Most of the south of the state, especially Izucar and the Sierra Mixteca were firmly in insurgent hands. Control then bypassed the capital and reached the more northern settlements of Tehuacan and <a href="/wiki/Atlixco" title="Atlixco">Atlixco</a>.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-enchistoria&#95;19-7" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-enchistoria-19"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>17<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-rincones34&#95;23-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-rincones34-23"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>21<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> After Independence, the first governor of the state was Carlos García Arriaga in 1821. The first state congress was seated in 1824, with the first state constitution adopted the same year. The new state was divided initially into 21 parts. The Spanish were expelled from the state in 1827. In 1849, the state was reorganized into eight departments and 162 municipalities and again in 1895 with 21 districts and 180 municipalities.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-enchistoria&#95;19-8" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-enchistoria-19"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>17<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>During the rest of the 19th century, the state developed economically through industry. The first mechanized textile mill was established in 1831, soon followed by 17 others in the city of Puebla. Progress was interrupted by <a href="/wiki/Antonio_L%C3%B3pez_de_Santa_Anna" title="Antonio López de Santa Anna">Santa Anna\'s</a> siege of the city in 1845 and two years later when the Americans under <a href="/wiki/Winfield_Scott" title="Winfield Scott">General Winfield Scott</a> took the city on their way to Mexico City. The Americans left three years later at the end of the war.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-enchistoria&#95;19-9" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-enchistoria-19"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>17<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p>\n<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-left" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:BattleofPuebla2.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0f/BattleofPuebla2.jpg/250px-BattleofPuebla2.jpg" decoding="async" width="190" height="248" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0f/BattleofPuebla2.jpg/330px-BattleofPuebla2.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/0/0f/BattleofPuebla2.jpg 2x" data-file-width="400" data-file-height="523" /></a><figcaption>Mexican cavalry charge at the Battle of Puebla</figcaption></figure>\n<p>Much of the rest of the century was occupied with civil strife such as the insurrection of Francisco Ortega against the federal government, the <a href="/wiki/Reform_War" title="Reform War">Reform War</a> and the <a href="/wiki/Second_French_intervention_in_Mexico" title="Second French intervention in Mexico">French Intervention</a>. The last provoked the <a href="/wiki/Battle_of_Puebla" title="Battle of Puebla">Battle of Puebla</a> on 5 May 1862, when 6,000 French troops attacked the forts named Loreto and Guadalupe outside of the city of Puebla, but they were repelled by forces under <a href="/wiki/Ignacio_Zaragoza" title="Ignacio Zaragoza">Ignacio Zaragoza</a>. Zaragoza died some months after this battle, and he would be later honored by having his name added to that of the city. However, less than a year later, the city would be taken and shortly after, <a href="/wiki/Emperor_Maximilian_I_of_Mexico" class="mw-redirect" title="Emperor Maximilian I of Mexico">Emperor Maximilian I of Mexico</a> would be installed. However, his rule would be brief and the French, along with their conservative Mexican allies, were expelled from the state in 1867.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-enchistoria&#95;19-10" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-enchistoria-19"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>17<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-sucesos&#95;20-4" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-sucesos-20"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>18<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>From this time to the Mexican Revolution, a number of important infrastructure projects were undertaken. One was the Puebla-Veracruz rail line in 1873 and the Escuela Normal para Profesores (Teachers’ College) in 1879. In 1907, a hydroelectric plant was built in Necaxa. However, the economic policies of this area caused widespread unrest, beginning with workers’ strikes. Directly against the regime of <a href="/wiki/Porfirio_D%C3%ADaz" title="Porfirio Díaz">Porfirio Díaz</a> was the Club Antireeleccionista (Anti-reelection Club) headed by <a href="/wiki/Aquiles_Serd%C3%A1n" title="Aquiles Serdán">Aquiles Serdán</a> in 1909. In November 1910, after long government surveillance, troops attacked the Serdán house in Puebla killing Aquiles and his brother Máximo. For this reason, the state claims one of the first battles of the <a href="/wiki/Mexican_Revolution" title="Mexican Revolution">Mexican Revolution</a>.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-enchistoria&#95;19-11" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-enchistoria-19"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>17<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Following_the_Mexican_Revolution">Following the Mexican Revolution</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Puebla&amp;action=edit&amp;section=11" title="Edit section: Following the Mexican Revolution"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<p>In 1912, the <a href="/wiki/Liberation_Army_of_the_South" title="Liberation Army of the South">Liberation Army of the South</a> or Zapatistas took over a number of communities in the state. In 1914, they were challenged by forces loyal to <a href="/wiki/Venustiano_Carranza" title="Venustiano Carranza">Venustiano Carranza</a>, which occupied the capital briefly. However, the Zapatistas would hold power for the rest of the war.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-enchistoria&#95;19-12" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-enchistoria-19"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>17<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Under the <a href="/wiki/1917_Constitution_of_Mexico" class="mw-redirect" title="1917 Constitution of Mexico">1917 Constitution</a>, the state was reestablished with 222 municipalities.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-sucesos&#95;20-5" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-sucesos-20"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>18<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> One of the last skirmishes of the war occurred in <a href="/w/index.php?title=Aljibes,_Puebla&amp;action=edit&amp;redlink=1" class="new" title="Aljibes, Puebla (page does not exist)">Aljibes, Puebla</a> in May 1920 when forces of <a href="/wiki/%C3%81lvaro_Obreg%C3%B3n" title="Álvaro Obregón">Álvaro Obregón</a> attacked those of Carranza as he was headed to Veracruz. Carranza was assassinated in <a href="/w/index.php?title=Tlaxcalantongo&amp;action=edit&amp;redlink=1" class="new" title="Tlaxcalantongo (page does not exist)">Tlaxcalantongo</a> in the Sierra Norte de Puebla soon thereafter.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-enchistoria&#95;19-13" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-enchistoria-19"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>17<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>The 1920s immediately after the war was marked by instability. The governorship changed hands frequently with resistance to whoever was in power from other parts of the state. Despite this, the <a href="/wiki/Universidad_Aut%C3%B3noma_de_Puebla" class="mw-redirect" title="Universidad Autónoma de Puebla">Universidad de Puebla</a> was established by <a href="/wiki/Maximino_%C3%81vila_Camacho" title="Maximino Ávila Camacho">Maximino Ávila Camacho</a> during this decade. True political stability would not come until the governorship of <a href="/wiki/Gustavo_D%C3%ADaz_Ordaz" title="Gustavo Díaz Ordaz">Gustavo Díaz Ordaz</a> in 1942.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-enchistoria&#95;19-14" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-enchistoria-19"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>17<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Modern_times">Modern times</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Puebla&amp;action=edit&amp;section=12" title="Edit section: Modern times"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<p>Since the Mexican Revolution, the city of Puebla and its suburbs are one of the most industrialized areas in Mexico, with the metropolitan area ranked fourth in size. Its position near both Mexico City and the Gulf coast continues to be an advantage. However, modern development of the city area has been restricted to outside the city center, in order to preserve its traditional look. This historic center was named a World Heritage Site in 1987, with the <a href="/wiki/Biblioteca_Palafoxiana" title="Biblioteca Palafoxiana">Biblioteca Palafoxiana</a> named as part of the <a href="/wiki/Memory_of_the_World_Programme" title="Memory of the World Programme">Memory of the World Programme</a> in 2005.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-rincones3536&#95;24-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-rincones3536-24"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>22<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Today, Puebla\'s economic development is centered on its capital. This capital is part of the <a href="/wiki/Megalopolis_(city_type)" class="mw-redirect" title="Megalopolis (city type)">megalopolis</a> centered on Mexico City.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-enchistoria&#95;19-15" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-enchistoria-19"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>17<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>In 1977, the center of the city of Puebla was named a "Zone of Historic Monuments". The same area was later named a <a href="/wiki/World_Heritage_Site" title="World Heritage Site">World Heritage Site</a> in 1987. In 1979, Puebla was the scene of one of <a href="/wiki/Pope_John_Paul_II" title="Pope John Paul II">Pope John Paul II</a>\'s early papal visits outside Italy to Mexico for that year\'s <a href="/wiki/CELAM" class="mw-redirect" title="CELAM">CELAM</a> conference over three months after his election and <a href="/wiki/Papal_inauguration" title="Papal inauguration">papal inauguration</a>.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-sucesos&#95;20-6" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-sucesos-20"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>18<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>In 1998, the state was declared in a state of emergency due to 122 forest fires with affected 2,998 hectares of land over two weeks. Many of the fires were started by fires on agricultural lands and the extremely dry conditions made the fires out of control.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-emergencia&#95;25-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-emergencia-25"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>23<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>The 1999 Tehuacán earthquake did major damage to much of state, especially many of its colonial era churches,<sup id="cite&#95;ref-prayer&#95;26-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-prayer-26"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>24<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> and the colonial buildings of the historic center of the city of Puebla. The state of Puebla was declared a disaster area.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-latimes&#95;27-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-latimes-27"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>25<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>In the 2000s, organizations such as <a href="/wiki/Reporters_Sans_Frontieres" class="mw-redirect" title="Reporters Sans Frontieres">Reporters Sans Frontieres</a> (RSF) have accused state governmental officials of restricting and suppressing the press. Some of the threats against reporters have included false arrests and death threats.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-monitoring&#95;28-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-monitoring-28"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>26<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>More than two years after the <a href="/wiki/2017_Puebla_earthquake" title="2017 Puebla earthquake">2017 Puebla earthquake</a> when 621 buildings—mostly 16th to 19th-century churches—were damaged in the state, 46 have been restored, 88 are in process, and 380 have not been restored at all.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-29" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-29"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>27<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Demographics">Demographics</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Puebla&amp;action=edit&amp;section=13" title="Edit section: Demographics"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Largest_cities">Largest cities</h3><span style="text-align:right;padding:1px">+6.7%</td></tr></tbody></table>\n<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-left" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Nahuas_en_Zacatl%C3%A1n.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/75/Nahuas_en_Zacatl%C3%A1n.jpg/250px-Nahuas_en_Zacatl%C3%A1n.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="166" /></a><figcaption>Nahuas in Zacatlán</figcaption></figure>\n<p>In 2005, the state had a population of 5,383,133 according to the <a href="/wiki/INEGI" class="mw-redirect" title="INEGI">INEGI</a> census, ranking fifth in the country.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-habitantes&#95;32-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-habitantes-32"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>30<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-perfilsoc&#95;33-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-perfilsoc-33"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>31<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Over 93% of the state\'s population identifies as Roman Catholic with 4.4% identifying as Protestant or Evangelical.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-perfilsoc&#95;33-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-perfilsoc-33"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>31<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>In 1921, Puebla had the second largest population, after <a href="/wiki/Oaxaca" title="Oaxaca">Oaxaca</a>, of purely indigenous people according to the national census. Since then, the official census has eliminated categories for race, counting only those who speak an indigenous language. In 2000, an attempt was made to count indigenous ethnicities, regardless of language spoken. This count ranked Puebla as fifth with a total population of 957,650.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-indcensus&#95;34-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-indcensus-34"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>32<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> However, according to the 2005 census, there were 548,723 people who spoke an indigenous language.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-perfilsoc&#95;33-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-perfilsoc-33"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>31<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> According to a 2000 census, <a href="/wiki/Censo_General_de_Poblaci%C3%B3n_y_Vivienda" title="Censo General de Población y Vivienda">Censo General de Población y Vivienda</a>, Puebla has the highest number of <a href="/wiki/Nahuatl" title="Nahuatl">Nahuatl</a> speakers over 5 years of age. There are 416,968 speakers making up about 8.21% of the population of the state.\n</p><p>The state has five major indigenous ethnic groups: the <a href="/wiki/Nahuas" title="Nahuas">Nahuas</a>, the <a href="/wiki/Totonac" title="Totonac">Totonacs</a>, the <a href="/wiki/Mixtec" title="Mixtec">Mixtecs</a>, the <a href="/wiki/Popoloca" class="mw-redirect" title="Popoloca">Popolocas</a> and the <a href="/wiki/Otomi_people" class="mw-redirect" title="Otomi people">Otomi</a>.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-perfilsoc&#95;33-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-perfilsoc-33"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>31<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> The state has two well-defined areas in which indigenous peoples still maintain many ancient traditions, rites, and customs. These two regions are called the Sierra Norte in the north and the Sierra Negra in the south. In these areas, these traditions, and the agriculture they are dependent on, have survived because industrialization has not penetrated the rugged landscape.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-rincones23&#95;35-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-rincones23-35"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>33<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>The Sierra Norte, especially the municipalities of <a href="/wiki/Cuetzalan" title="Cuetzalan">Cuetzalan</a>, <a href="/wiki/Pahuatl%C3%A1n_(municipality)" class="mw-redirect" title="Pahuatlán (municipality)">Pahuatlán</a>, <a href="/wiki/Huehuetl%C3%A1n_el_Grande" title="Huehuetlán el Grande">Huehuetlán el Grande</a> and <a href="/wiki/Teziutl%C3%A1n_(municipality)" title="Teziutlán (municipality)">Teziutlán</a>, are dominated by the Nahuas, Totonacas and Otomi. There is also a small region locally called the Sierra Negra in which there are communities of Popolocas, Nahuas and <a href="/wiki/Mazateco" class="mw-redirect" title="Mazateco">Mazatecos</a>, especially in the municipality of <a href="/wiki/Eloxochitl%C3%A1n,_Puebla" title="Eloxochitlán, Puebla">Eloxochitlán</a>, <a href="/wiki/Tlacotepec_de_Benito_Ju%C3%A1rez_(municipality)" class="mw-redirect" title="Tlacotepec de Benito Juárez (municipality)">Tlacotepec</a> and part of the city of <a href="/wiki/Tehuac%C3%A1n,_Puebla" class="mw-redirect" title="Tehuacán, Puebla">Tehuacán</a>.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-perfilsoc&#95;33-4" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-perfilsoc-33"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>31<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-rincones23&#95;35-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-rincones23-35"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>33<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>The Mixtec people who live in the south of Puebla are part of an ethnic group which are still the dominant indigenous group in an area that stretches over Puebla, Oaxaca and the mountains of <a href="/wiki/Guerrero" title="Guerrero">Guerrero</a>. They are the fourth largest indigenous group in Mexico. The Sierra Mixteca region in Puebla is part of the <a href="/wiki/Mixteca_Baja" class="mw-redirect" title="Mixteca Baja">Mixteca Baja</a> region, which crosses into parts of Oaxaca as well.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-uvmixteco&#95;36-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-uvmixteco-36"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>34<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> In the <a href="/wiki/Mesoamerica" title="Mesoamerica">Mesoamerican</a> period, the Mixtecs of Puebla dominated further north than they do now and archeologists classify "Mixteca-Puebla" art as distinct from other Mixtec arts and crafts.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-mixtecaarte&#95;37-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-mixtecaarte-37"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>35<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> There are an estimated 6,700 Mixtecs living in Puebla, however, many have emigrated out of traditional Mixtec areas into other parts of the state, Mexico City and even the United States to work.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-arqueomex&#95;38-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-arqueomex-38"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>36<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-gruposetnicos&#95;39-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-gruposetnicos-39"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>37<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>A 2020 genetic study sampling 2,827 individuals from the state of Puebla found that the general population is of predominantly Indigenous descent, finding an average of 72.1% Indigenous ancestry, 21.1% European ancestry, and 6.7% African.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-40" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-40"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>38<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>According to the 2020 Census, 1.73% of Puebla\'s population identified as Black, <a href="/wiki/Afro-Mexican" class="mw-redirect" title="Afro-Mexican">Afro-Mexican</a>, or of African descent.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-41" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-41"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>39<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Economy">Economy</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Puebla&amp;action=edit&amp;section=15" title="Edit section: Economy"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="General_economy">General economy</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Puebla&amp;action=edit&amp;section=16" title="Edit section: General economy"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Artesan%C3%ADas_de_Puebla,_M%C3%A9xico.JPG" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f6/Artesan%C3%ADas_de_Puebla%2C_M%C3%A9xico.JPG/250px-Artesan%C3%ADas_de_Puebla%2C_M%C3%A9xico.JPG" decoding="async" width="250" height="162" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f6/Artesan%C3%ADas_de_Puebla%2C_M%C3%A9xico.JPG/500px-Artesan%C3%ADas_de_Puebla%2C_M%C3%A9xico.JPG 1.5x" data-file-width="5158" data-file-height="3343" /></a><figcaption>Crafts of Puebla, México</figcaption></figure>\n<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:PiedrasEncimadas35.JPG" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/46/PiedrasEncimadas35.JPG/250px-PiedrasEncimadas35.JPG" decoding="async" width="250" height="167" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/46/PiedrasEncimadas35.JPG/500px-PiedrasEncimadas35.JPG 1.5x" data-file-width="3872" data-file-height="2592" /></a><figcaption>Shearing a sheep near Zacatlán</figcaption></figure>\n<p>The state is divided into seven socioeconomic regions for planning purposes: Region I-<a href="/wiki/Huauchinango_(municipality)" title="Huauchinango (municipality)">Huauchinango</a>, Region II – <a href="/wiki/Teziutl%C3%A1n_(municipality)" title="Teziutlán (municipality)">Teziutlán</a>, Region III <a href="/wiki/Chalchicomula_de_Sesma_(municipality)" class="mw-redirect" title="Chalchicomula de Sesma (municipality)">Ciudad Serdán</a>, Region IV <a href="/wiki/San_Pedro_Cholula_(municipality)" class="mw-redirect" title="San Pedro Cholula (municipality)">San Pedro Cholula</a>, Region V – Puebla, Region VI <a href="/wiki/Iz%C3%BAcar_de_Matamoros" title="Izúcar de Matamoros">Izúcar de Matamoros</a> and Region VII <a href="/wiki/Tehuac%C3%A1n_Municipality" class="mw-redirect" title="Tehuacán Municipality">Tehuacán</a>.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-regionalizacion&#95;42-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-regionalizacion-42"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>40<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>The state was a diverse economic base supporting industries such as textiles, tourism, agribusiness, storage, medical services, furniture making and logistics services in clusters.(promotedor) In 2010, <a href="/wiki/Standard_%26_Poor%27s" class="mw-redirect" title="Standard &amp; Poor&#39;s">Standard &amp; Poor\'s</a> reconfirmed the state\'s ‘mxA+’ rating with a stable outlook due to the state\'s finances. The state\'s economy grew at a rate of 4.5% from 2003 to 2007, above the national average of 3.9%. Since then, economic growth has slowed but less than in other parts of Mexico. Its <a href="/wiki/Gross_domestic_product" title="Gross domestic product">gross domestic product</a> accounts for 3.4% of the country\'s total.\n</p><p>It is one of Mexico\'s most industrialized states.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-standardpoors&#95;43-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-standardpoors-43"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>41<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>However, almost all of the state\'s development has been centered on the capital city and the surrounding areas. This has caused a wide economic gap between rich and poor and between the city areas and the rural areas, with much of the state lacking investment by the government (infrastructure) or by private interests.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-polarizacion&#95;44-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-polarizacion-44"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>42<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-prometedor&#95;45-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-prometedor-45"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>43<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> This has led the <a href="/wiki/United_Nations" title="United Nations">United Nations</a> to rank the state as the seventh most underdeveloped in the country, despite the industry in the Puebla City area in 2006–2007, with areas lacking basic services such as health, water and education along with high unemployment.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-standardpoors&#95;43-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-standardpoors-43"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>41<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-septimo&#95;46-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-septimo-46"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>44<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> The state is even ranked lower for these than <a href="/wiki/Lebanon" title="Lebanon">Lebanon</a>, <a href="/wiki/Cuba" title="Cuba">Cuba</a> and <a href="/wiki/Bosnia" class="mw-redirect" title="Bosnia">Bosnia</a>. The UN blames poor government policies and corruption for much of the state\'s poverty.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-septimo&#95;46-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-septimo-46"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>44<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>According to several <a href="/wiki/NGO" class="mw-redirect" title="NGO">NGO</a>\'s, such as the Consejo Nacional de Evaluación de la Política de Desarrollo Social (Coneval), and Marcos Gutiérrez Barrón, professor of economics at the <a href="/wiki/Universidad_Popular_Aut%C3%B3noma_del_Estado_de_Puebla" title="Universidad Popular Autónoma del Estado de Puebla">Universidad Popular Autónoma del Estado de Puebla</a>,<sup id="cite&#95;ref-UPAEP&#95;47-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-UPAEP-47"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>45<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Puebla has the third highest level of poverty in the country. This ranking takes into account factors such as income per capita, housing, educational opportunities, food supply and family cohesion. As much as two-thirds of the state\'s population or about 3.5 million live under the poverty line. The state\'s Secretaria de Desarrollo Social (Secretariat of Social Development) increased its budget in 2008 to 757 million pesos. Ten of the state\'s municipalities are ranked among the poorest in the country.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-tercer&#95;48-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-tercer-48"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>46<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>Puebla is a state where migrant workers both head to and leave from.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-gruposetnicos&#95;39-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-gruposetnicos-39"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>37<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-septimo&#95;46-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-septimo-46"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>44<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Most incoming workers are indigenous from the states of Oaxaca and Guerrero, according to a study done by the <a href="/wiki/National_Indigenous_Institute" class="mw-redirect" title="National Indigenous Institute">National Indigenous Institute</a> and the United Nations. Most of these emigrants are Mixtecs from the south of the state, which head to areas such as Mexico City and the north of the country either seasonally or permanently.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-gruposetnicos&#95;39-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-gruposetnicos-39"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>37<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Many also head to the United States to work illegally. The migration situation has caused the population to drop in a number of areas in the state. The UN states that the main reason for emigration is the lack of local economic development especially in rural and indigenous areas.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-septimo&#95;46-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-septimo-46"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>44<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Agriculture_and_forestry">Agriculture and forestry</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Puebla&amp;action=edit&amp;section=17" title="Edit section: Agriculture and forestry"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Puebla_farmers.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d5/Puebla_farmers.jpg/250px-Puebla_farmers.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="174" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d5/Puebla_farmers.jpg/500px-Puebla_farmers.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="1365" data-file-height="951" /></a><figcaption>Farmers in a field in Puebla</figcaption></figure>\n<p>Thirty seven percent of the population is employed in agriculture, livestock and fishing. Agricultural units cover 2,233,897 hectares in rural areas of the state. Just over fifty percent is dedicated to the growing of crops, 46.5% to pasture, 2.6% is forest and .8% is wild vegetation.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-actecon&#95;49-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-actecon-49"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>47<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Agriculture is the most important economic activity of the rural areas, but it is mostly limited to the rainy season from June to October, as there are few facilities for irrigation.
