href="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/transcoded/2/2d/Patricia_Bullrich_-_nombre_%28ES-ar%29.ogg/Patricia_Bullrich_-_nombre_%28ES-ar%29.ogg.mp3" rel="nofollow" aria-label="Play audio" title="Play audio" class="oo-ui-buttonElement-button"><span class="oo-ui-iconElement-icon oo-ui-icon-volumeUp"></span><span class="oo-ui-labelElement-label"></span><span class="oo-ui-indicatorElement-indicator oo-ui-indicatorElement-noIndicator"></span></a></span><sup class="ext-phonos-attribution noexcerpt navigation-not-searchable"><a href="/wiki/File:Patricia_Bullrich_-_nombre_(ES-ar).ogg" title="File:Patricia Bullrich - nombre (ES-ar).ogg">ⓘ</a></sup></span>; born 11 June 1956) is an Argentine politician. She currently serves as a <a href="/wiki/Argentine_Senate" title="Argentine Senate">National Senator</a> for the <a href="/wiki/Buenos_Aires" title="Buenos Aires">Autonomous City of Buenos Aires</a> since December 2025, representing <a href="/wiki/La_Libertad_Avanza" title="La Libertad Avanza">La Libertad Avanza</a>.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-3"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>3<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> She previously served as the <a href="/wiki/Ministry_of_National_Security_(Argentina)" title="Ministry of National Security (Argentina)">Minister of National Security</a> from 2023 to 2025 under president <a href="/wiki/Javier_Milei" title="Javier Milei">Javier Milei</a> and from 2015 to 2019 under president <a href="/wiki/Mauricio_Macri" title="Mauricio Macri">Mauricio Macri</a>. She was the chairwoman of the <a href="/wiki/Republican_Proposal" title="Republican Proposal">Republican Proposal</a> until 2025.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-4" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-4"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>4<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>She was born in Buenos Aires, part of the <a href="/wiki/Pueyrred%C3%B3n_family" title="Pueyrredón family">Pueyrredón family</a>. Bullrich graduated from the <a href="/wiki/University_of_Palermo_(Buenos_Aires)" title="University of Palermo (Buenos Aires)">University of Palermo</a>, and as a young woman she was involved with the <a href="/wiki/Peronist_Youth" class="mw-redirect" title="Peronist Youth">Peronist Youth</a>. She married Marcelo Langieri, secretary of Rodolfo Galimberti; Galimberti was a leader of the <a href="/wiki/Montoneros" title="Montoneros">Montoneros</a> guerrilla and her brother-in-law. They went into exile in 1977, during the <a href="/wiki/Dirty_War" title="Dirty War">Dirty War</a>, and she returned in 1982, after the <a href="/wiki/Falklands_War" title="Falklands War">Falklands War</a>. She was elected deputy for the <a href="/wiki/Justicialist_Party" title="Justicialist Party">Justicialist Party</a> in 1993. She left the party and started her own, but could not secure a re-election. She joined the cabinet of president <a href="/wiki/Fernando_De_la_R%C3%BAa" class="mw-redirect" title="Fernando De la Rúa">Fernando De la Rúa</a> in 2001. \n</p><p>Following the election of <a href="/wiki/Mauricio_Macri" title="Mauricio Macri">Mauricio Macri</a> to the presidency in the <a href="/wiki/2015_Argentine_general_election" title="2015 Argentine general election">2015 Argentine general election</a>, she became the Minister of Security. She placed regulations against roadblocks from <a href="/wiki/Piquetero" title="Piquetero">piqueteros</a>, and opposed the secessionist organization <a href="/wiki/Resistencia_Ancestral_Mapuche" title="Resistencia Ancestral Mapuche">Resistencia Ancestral Mapuche</a>. Leading the "hawk" sector of the <a href="/wiki/Juntos_por_el_Cambio" title="Juntos por el Cambio">Juntos por el Cambio</a> coalition, she was appointed its president in 2020. She ran for the 2023 Argentine <a href="/wiki/2023_Argentine_primary_elections" title="2023 Argentine primary elections">primary</a> and <a href="/wiki/2023_Argentine_general_election" title="2023 Argentine general election">general</a> elections. She won the primaries against <a href="/wiki/Horacio_Rodr%C3%ADguez_Larreta" title="Horacio Rodríguez Larreta">Horacio Rodríguez Larreta</a>, but ended third in the general elections behind <a href="/wiki/Sergio_Massa" title="Sergio Massa">Sergio Massa</a> and <a href="/wiki/Javier_Milei" title="Javier Milei">Javier Milei</a>. She supported Milei on the ballotage with Massa. After Milei was elected President, he chose Bullrich to serve again as Minister of Security.\n</p><p>On November 30, 2025, Bullrich resigned from her post as Minister of National Security after she was sworn in as a Senator in the <a href="/wiki/Argentine_Senate" title="Argentine Senate">Argentine Senate</a>.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-5" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-5"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>5<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p>\n<meta property="mw:PageProp/toc" />\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Early_life">Early life</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Patricia_Bullrich&amp;action=edit&amp;section=1" title="Edit section: Early life"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<p>Bullrich was born on 11 June 1956 in <a href="/wiki/Buenos_Aires" title="Buenos Aires">Buenos Aires</a>, daughter of Alejandro Bullrich, a cardiologist, and Julieta Luro Pueyrredon. She belongs to two wealthy families on each of her parents\' sides. On her mother\'s side, she belongs to the <a href="/wiki/Pueyrred%C3%B3n_family" title="Pueyrredón family">Pueyrredón family</a>, a traditional lineage of Spanish, French, and Irish descent whose members featured prominently in the early years of Argentine Independence (such as <a href="/wiki/Juan_Mart%C3%ADn_de_Pueyrred%C3%B3n" title="Juan Martín de Pueyrredón">Juan Martín de Pueyrredón</a> and <a href="/wiki/Honorio_Pueyrredon" class="mw-redirect" title="Honorio Pueyrredon">Honorio Pueyrredon</a>).<sup id="cite&#95;ref-6" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-6"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>6<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> On her father\'s side, she descends from <a href="/wiki/Adolfo_Bullrich" title="Adolfo Bullrich">Adolfo Bullrich</a>, a businessman and politician of German ancestry, who served as <a href="/wiki/List_of_mayors_and_chiefs_of_government_of_Buenos_Aires_City" title="List of mayors and chiefs of government of Buenos Aires City">Mayor of Buenos Aires</a> from 1898 to 1902.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-7" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-7"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>7<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Although it was a wealthy family, Alejandro and Julieta divorced, and Patricia adjusted to a simpler lifestyle when her mother got a job as publicist.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-pebeta&#95;8-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-pebeta-8"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>8<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>She became politically engaged from an early age, abandoning a potential career in <a href="/wiki/Field_hockey" title="Field hockey">field hockey</a> to dedicate herself fully to political activism.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-9" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-9"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>9<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> She also worked at the <i>Cheburger</i> fast food joint and became a member of the food workers\' union, encouraging coworkers to unionise as well.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-lazos&#95;10-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-lazos-10"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>10<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>She is the cousin of the singer-songwriter <a href="/wiki/Fabiana_Cantilo" title="Fabiana Cantilo">Fabiana Cantilo</a>, and introduced her to <a href="/wiki/Argentine_rock" title="Argentine rock">Argentine rock</a>. In the TV program "<i>Almorzando con Mirtha Legrand</i>" Cantilo explained that their mothers were close as siblings, and that Bullrich invited her to a concert of the band <a href="/wiki/Pescado_Rabioso" title="Pescado Rabioso">Pescado Rabioso</a>, led by <a href="/wiki/Luis_Alberto_Spinetta" title="Luis Alberto Spinetta">Luis Alberto Spinetta</a>. This was the first concert that Fabiana Cantilo had attended, years before becoming a rock singer herself.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-familiar&#95;11-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-familiar-11"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>11<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Patricia skipped school classes one day to attend the <a href="/wiki/Music_competition" title="Music competition">music competition</a> TV program "Si lo sabe cante", where she sang the song "El extraño de pelo largo" of La Joven Guardia. She was defeated in the competition.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-pebeta&#95;8-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-pebeta-8"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>8<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> \n</p>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Peronist_Youth_years">Peronist Youth years</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Patricia_Bullrich&amp;action=edit&amp;section=2" title="Edit section: Peronist Youth years"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<p>Patricia\'s grandmother, daughter of Honorio Pueyrredon, took her to meet <a href="/wiki/Ricardo_Balb%C3%ADn" title="Ricardo Balbín">Ricardo Balbín</a>, leader of the <a href="/wiki/Radical_Civic_Union" title="Radical Civic Union">Radical Civic Union</a> (UCR). The meeting had the opposite effect than expected, as there was a huge <a href="/wiki/Generation_gap" title="Generation gap">generation gap</a> between them. Rather than make her embrace the ideas of the UCR, supportive of <a href="/wiki/Liberal_democracy" title="Liberal democracy">liberal democracy</a>, she rejected Balbín and chose <a href="/wiki/Peronism" title="Peronism">Peronism</a> instead, which proposed <a href="/wiki/Far-left_politics" title="Far-left politics">far-left politics</a> at the time.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-familiar&#95;11-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-familiar-11"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>11<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> She joined the Peronist Youth (JP), the youth wing of the Peronist movement, aged 17. On 20 June 1973, she joined the procession to <a href="/wiki/Ezeiza_Airport" class="mw-redirect" title="Ezeiza Airport">Ezeiza</a> to bear witness to <a href="/wiki/Juan_Per%C3%B3n" title="Juan Perón">Juan Perón</a>\'s return to Argentina following his 18-year exile, but left before the <a href="/wiki/Ezeiza_Massacre" class="mw-redirect" title="Ezeiza Massacre">Ezeiza Massacre</a> took place that same day.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-quien&#95;12-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-quien-12"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>12<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>She was also present at the <a href="/wiki/Plaza_de_Mayo" title="Plaza de Mayo">Plaza de Mayo</a> on the <a href="/wiki/International_Workers%27_Day" title="International Workers&#39; Day">International Workers\' Day</a> of 1974, when Perón, who had once again become president of Argentina, <a href="/wiki/Expulsion_of_Montoneros_from_Plaza_de_Mayo" title="Expulsion of Montoneros from Plaza de Mayo">expelled the Montoneros</a> and the <a href="/wiki/Tendencia_Revolucionaria" title="Tendencia Revolucionaria">left-wing youth groups</a> from the celebrations. Although both the Peronist unions and guerrillas such as <a href="/wiki/Montoneros" title="Montoneros">Montoneros</a> had worked together against the <a href="/wiki/Argentine_Revolution" title="Argentine Revolution">Argentine Revolution</a> dictatorship, they had begun a dispute over their political clout on the new democratic government; with the aforementioned expulsion Perón openly sided with the unions. Bullrich herself was a member of the Montoneros under the <i><a href="/wiki/Nom-de-guerre" class="mw-redirect" title="Nom-de-guerre">nom-de-guerre</a></i> of "Cali", and active in the <i>Columna Norte</i> subgroup commanded by <a href="https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rodolfo_Galimberti" class="extiw" title="es:Rodolfo Galimberti">Rodolfo Galimberti</a>.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-montonera&#95;13-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-montonera-13"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>13<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Galimberti was Bullrich\'s brother-in-law, as he was married to Bullrich\'s sister, Julieta.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-14" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-14"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>14<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Bullrich has denied being a Montoneros member, and maintains that she was just a member of the JP.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-15" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-15"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>15<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-autocritica&#95;16-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-autocritica-16"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>16<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>Perón died in 1974 and the <a href="/wiki/Dirty_War" title="Dirty War">Dirty War</a>, an armed conflict between the Montoneros and the military, worsened: the guerrillas resumed the tactics used years before to attempt to remove the current authorities from power. In 1975, Bullrich was arrested for spray-painting political messages on the entrance of the <a href="/wiki/Faculty_of_Philosophy_and_Letters,_University_of_Buenos_Aires" title="Faculty of Philosophy and Letters, University of Buenos Aires">University of Buenos Aires Faculty of Philosophy and Letters</a>, and spent six months in prison. Upon being released, she dropped out of her sociology degree at the University of Buenos Aires and enrolled at the <a href="/wiki/Universidad_de_Belgrano" class="mw-redirect" title="Universidad de Belgrano">Universidad de Belgrano</a> to study law.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-lazos&#95;10-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-lazos-10"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>10<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> She also rejoined the <i>Columna Norte</i>. By the end of 1975, she started dating Marcelo Langieri, secretary of Galimberti.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-17" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-17"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>17<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> The <a href="/wiki/1976_Argentine_coup_d%27%C3%A9tat" title="1976 Argentine coup d&#39;état">1976 coup d\'état</a> established a military dictatorship, the <a href="/wiki/National_Reorganization_Process" title="National Reorganization Process">National Reorganization Process</a>, that continued the armed conflict against the Montoneros. Montoneros organized an attack on 4 September 1976, that intended to kill a manager of the Sudamtex textile firm. On her way to participate, Bullrich felt that she was being followed and fled. The military had abducted one of the masterminds of the plan and learned about the attack, which allowed them to surprise the Montoneros and kill the whole unit.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-montonera&#95;13-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-montonera-13"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>13<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> In January 1977, Galimberti and Bullrich attached an <a href="/wiki/Improvised_explosive_device" title="Improvised explosive device">improvised explosive device</a> to the car of Pepe Noguer, mayor of <a href="/wiki/San_Isidro,_Buenos_Aires" title="San Isidro, Buenos Aires">San Isidro</a>. The device exploded, injuring the daughter and the daughter-in-law of the mayor, Ana María Noguer and Hortensia M. de Noguer.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-montonera&#95;13-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-montonera-13"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>13<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>Patricia Bullrich went into exile in 1977 with her partner Marcelo Langieri, first settling in Brazil, and later in Mexico, Spain and France.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-pebeta&#95;8-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-pebeta-8"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>8<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> She was still a member of Montoneros living abroad, until Galimberti cut ties with the organization in 1979.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-montonera&#95;13-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-montonera-13"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>13<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> She returned briefly to Argentina in that year, to give birth to her son Francisco.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-pebeta&#95;8-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-pebeta-8"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>8<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Political_career">Political career</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Patricia_Bullrich&amp;action=edit&amp;section=3" title="Edit section: Political career"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<p>Bullrich returned to the country after the 1982 <a href="/wiki/Falklands_War" title="Falklands War">Falklands War</a>.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-quien&#95;12-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-quien-12"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>12<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> She had conflicts with <a href="/wiki/Dante_Gullo" title="Dante Gullo">Dante Gullo</a> over the reorganization of the JP, thinking that it should have its own political leaders rather than follow the older ones.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-18" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-18"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>18<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Peronism lost the <a href="/wiki/1983_Argentine_general_election" title="1983 Argentine general election">1983 Argentine general election</a>, so she joined the internal faction of <a href="/wiki/Antonio_Cafiero" title="Antonio Cafiero">Antonio Cafiero</a> that sought to renew the party. Peronism returned to power in 1989 when <a href="/wiki/Carlos_Menem" title="Carlos Menem">Carlos Menem</a> won the <a href="/wiki/1989_Argentine_general_election" title="1989 Argentine general election">1989 Argentine general election</a>. She was elected deputy for the <a href="/wiki/Justicialist_Party" title="Justicialist Party">Justicialist Party</a> (PJ) in 1993, alongside <a href="/wiki/Erman_Gonz%C3%A1lez" class="mw-redirect" title="Erman González">Erman González</a>.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-pebeta&#95;8-4" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-pebeta-8"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>8<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> She proposed over two hundred bills, including the Art University law, the Cinema law, and the Leasing Contract law.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-ministra&#95;19-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-ministra-19"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>19<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> In 1995, she was named the Legislator of the Year.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-ministra&#95;19-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-ministra-19"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>19<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>Patricia Bullrich left the PJ in 1996 and started <a href="/wiki/New_Leadership" title="New Leadership">New Leadership</a> alongside <a href="/wiki/Gustavo_B%C3%A9liz" title="Gustavo Béliz">Gustavo Béliz</a>. She had disagreements with him because she thought that he managed the party unilaterally, without making her part of the decisions.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-20" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-20"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>20<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> She left the party as a result and, after briefly considering joining the <a href="/wiki/Front_for_a_Country_in_Solidarity" title="Front for a Country in Solidarity">Frepaso</a>, she started another party. Initially named Cambio 97, it was soon renamed "Unión por Todos" (UPT) as the Cambio 97 name had already been registered. The new party did not get enough votes to allow her to be reelected as deputy in the <a href="/wiki/1997_Argentine_legislative_election" title="1997 Argentine legislative election">1997 Argentine legislative election</a>. She then worked for the <a href="/wiki/Buenos_Aires_Province" title="Buenos Aires Province">Buenos Aires Province</a> on security matters, assisting the municipality of <a href="/wiki/Hurlingham_Partido" title="Hurlingham Partido">Hurlingham</a>. She resigned in 1998, because of conflicts with <a href="/wiki/Le%C3%B3n_Arslani%C3%A1n" title="León Arslanián">León Arslanián</a>, minister of justice of the province.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-21" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-21"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>21<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p>\n<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-left" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Patricia_Bullrich.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/52/Patricia_Bullrich.jpg/250px-Patricia_Bullrich.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="188" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/5/52/Patricia_Bullrich.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="314" data-file-height="236" /></a><figcaption>Patricia Bullrich at the time she served as deputy.</figcaption></figure>\n<p>In 1999, the UPT became part of the <a href="/wiki/Alliance_for_Work,_Justice_and_Education" class="mw-redirect" title="Alliance for Work, Justice and Education">Alliance for Work, Justice and Education</a>, which took <a href="/wiki/Fernando_de_la_R%C3%BAa" title="Fernando de la Rúa">Fernando de la Rúa</a> to the Presidency. Bullrich was appointed to office in the Department of Criminal Policy and Penitentiary Matters. In 2001, she was made a cabinet minister, as <a href="/wiki/Secretariat_of_Labour,_Employment_and_Social_Security_(Argentina)" title="Secretariat of Labour, Employment and Social Security (Argentina)">Secretary of Labour, Employment and Human Resources</a> and, later that year, as Secretary of Social Security.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-ministra&#95;19-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-ministra-19"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>19<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> In 2001 she announced a cut of 13% on retirement wages above $574, 16% of all retirees, which would reduce the <a href="/wiki/Deficit_spending" title="Deficit spending">deficit</a> by 68.6 millions of pesos.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-22" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-22"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>22<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> \n</p><p>De la Rúa resigned, and eventually the governor of Buenos Aires <a href="/wiki/Eduardo_Duhalde" title="Eduardo Duhalde">Eduardo Duhalde</a> was appointed president by the Congress. Bullrich relaunched the UPT in 2002, aiming for the <a href="/wiki/2003_Argentine_general_election" title="2003 Argentine general election">2003 presidential elections</a>. The party platform announced reforms on labor and education.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-23" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-23"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>23<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> The UPT did not take part in the elections, supporting instead <a href="/wiki/Ricardo_L%C3%B3pez_Murphy" title="Ricardo López Murphy">Ricardo López Murphy</a> of the <a href="/wiki/Recreate_for_Growth" title="Recreate for Growth">Recreate for Growth</a> party,<sup id="cite&#95;ref-24" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-24"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>24<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> who ended in the third place. Both parties united in the alliance "Unión para Recrear Buenos Aires", proposing Bullrich for mayor of Buenos Aires. She ended in the fourth place, with 9.76% of the vote.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-25" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-25"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>25<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>The UPT joined forces with the <a href="/wiki/Support_for_an_Egalitarian_Republic" class="mw-redirect" title="Support for an Egalitarian Republic">Support for an Egalitarian Republic</a> (ARI) and created the <a href="/wiki/Civic_Coalition_(Argentina)" title="Civic Coalition (Argentina)">Civic Coalition</a> to run for the <a href="/wiki/2007_Argentine_general_election" title="2007 Argentine general election">2007 Argentine general election</a>, with <a href="/wiki/Elisa_Carri%C3%B3" title="Elisa Carrió">Elisa Carrió</a> as a candidate for president. Bullrich ran instead for deputy for Buenos Aires.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-26" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-26"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>26<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Her centrist politics and polemical history as a government minister, however, contributed to the disenchantment of a group of left-wing members of ARI who left the Civic Coalition.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-27" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-27"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>27<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Minister_of_Security_(2015–2019)"><span id="Minister_of_Security_.282015.E2.80.932019.29"></span>Minister of Security (2015–2019)</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Patricia_Bullrich&amp;action=edit&amp;section=4" title="Edit section: Minister of Security (2015–2019)"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Informe_ram_2.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6d/Informe_ram_2.jpg/250px-Informe_ram_2.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="162" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6d/Informe_ram_2.jpg/500px-Informe_ram_2.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="750" data-file-height="486" /></a><figcaption>Patricia Bullrich presents a report about the <i><a href="/wiki/Resistencia_Ancestral_Mapuche" title="Resistencia Ancestral Mapuche">Resistencia Ancestral Mapuche</a></i> organization.</figcaption></figure>\n<p><a href="/wiki/Mauricio_Macri" title="Mauricio Macri">Mauricio Macri</a> was elected president in 2015 and Patricia Bullrich was appointed Minister of Security.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-28" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-28"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>28<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Within the first days, three criminals convicted for <a href="/wiki/Triple_crime" title="Triple crime">torturing and killing three pharmaceutical businessmen</a> escaped from a high-security prison, leading to a nation-wide operation to recapture them. Bullrich announced on 9 January that the three criminals had been captured, but, in reality, only one had been captured. She tendered her resignation to Macri because of the mistake, but Macri rejected it. The other two criminals were captured a few days later.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-29" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-29"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>29<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> \n</p><p>Bullrich proposed a protocol to remove roadblocks caused by <a href="/wiki/Piquetero" title="Piquetero">piqueteros</a>. Such blocks should be announced in advance, restrict only part of the roads, and last for a short time. They should cease if ordered so by the police, and those who commit violent actions shall be detained. This protocol was approved by a meeting of the ministers of security of all provinces of Argentina.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-30" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-30"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>30<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Horacio_Rodr%C3%ADguez_Larreta" title="Horacio Rodríguez Larreta">Horacio Rodríguez Larreta</a>, chief of government of the Buenos Aires city, and <a href="/wiki/Mar%C3%ADa_Eugenia_Vidal" title="María Eugenia Vidal">María Eugenia Vidal</a>, governor of the Buenos Aires province, refused to endorse it, as they thought that doing so could prove controversial. Instead, they preferred to negotiate and stay on good terms with organizations of piqueteros such as the <a href="/wiki/Evita_Movement" title="Evita Movement">Evita Movement</a>.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-31" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-31"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>31<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Larreta also explained that the city does not need to endorse the protocols because it already has regulations for roadblocks.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-32" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-32"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>32<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>  \n</p><p><a href="/wiki/Resistencia_Ancestral_Mapuche" title="Resistencia Ancestral Mapuche">Resistencia Ancestral Mapuche</a> (RAM) and the <a href="/wiki/Coordinadora_Arauco-Malleco" title="Coordinadora Arauco-Malleco">Coordinadora Arauco-Malleco</a> (CAM), two <a href="/wiki/Mapuche" title="Mapuche">Mapuche</a> organizations that normally operate in <a href="/wiki/Patagonia" title="Patagonia">Patagonia</a>, expanded their attacks to the city of Buenos Aires. Their goal is to create a Mapuche nation, seceding from Argentina and Chile. Bullrich said that "We won\'t allow an autonomous mapuche republic inside Argentina; that\'s the logic of their request, the denial of the Argentine state, the anarchist logic. Our resolution is total and absolute in not allowing a group that uses violence as a way of action in Argentina."<sup id="cite&#95;ref-33" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-33"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>33<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Facundo Jones Huala, leader of RAM, claimed to be a political prisoner, and that the RAM only acts in self-defense on lands that used to belong to them.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-34" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-34"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>34<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Bullrich organized a joint command with the ministers of security of the <a href="/wiki/Neuqu%C3%A9n_Province" title="Neuquén Province">Neuquén</a>, <a href="/wiki/R%C3%ADo_Negro_Province" title="Río Negro Province">Río Negro</a> and <a href="/wiki/Chubut_Province" title="Chubut Province">Chubut</a> provinces against the RAM, and delivered a report of the actions taken against the organization, including 96 lawsuits, 2 of them for murder.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-35" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-35"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>35<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>   \n</p><p>The <a href="/wiki/Argentine_National_Gendarmerie" title="Argentine National Gendarmerie">Argentine National Gendarmerie</a> forced a group of Mapuche demonstrators to cease a roadblock next to the <a href="/wiki/Chubut_River" title="Chubut River">Chubut River</a>, and the demonstrator <a href="/wiki/Santiago_Maldonado" class="mw-redirect" title="Santiago Maldonado">Santiago Maldonado</a> went missing after that. The case became a national scandal, with the Gendarmerie (by extension their political authorities, Bullrich and Macri) being accused of an <a href="/wiki/Enforced_disappearance" title="Enforced disappearance">enforced disappearance</a>. Bullrich gave her full support to the Gendarmerie. Maldonado was found dead some months later, drowned in the Chubut river. Bullrich said "The whole world saw what happened with Maldonado. He stayed in the same place where he drowned, without being seen or touched by anyone. Neither the Gendarmerie nor our government would have made a person disappear".<sup id="cite&#95;ref-quien&#95;12-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-quien-12"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>12<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>A tourist was stabbed ten times by thieves, who then ran away. The policeman <a href="/wiki/Luis_Chocobar" title="Luis Chocobar">Luis Chocobar</a> shot one of the thieves, claiming that the thief made a movement suggesting he was about to fire a gun. However, a video released by <a href="/wiki/Telefe_Noticias" title="Telefe Noticias">Telefe Noticias</a> showed that the criminal had his back to him. Bullrich, however, pointed out that the video was edited and did not show the exact moment of the gunshot.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-opositor&#95;36-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-opositor-36"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>36<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Bullrich and Macri supported the actions of Chocobar, on the grounds that it would be a <a href="/wiki/Right_of_self-defense" title="Right of self-defense">right of self-defense</a>,<sup id="cite&#95;ref-opositor&#95;36-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-opositor-36"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>36<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> while human rights organizations considered it a case of <a href="/wiki/Police_brutality" title="Police brutality">police brutality</a>.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-quien&#95;12-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-quien-12"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>12<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Chocobar was sentenced for homicide four years later.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-quien&#95;12-4" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-quien-12"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>12<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>In November 2018, Bullrich said that "those who wanted to be armed should be allowed to do so", prompting strong criticism and opposition.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-37" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-37"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>37<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-38" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-38"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>38<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Adrián Marcenac, father of Alfredo Marcenac, a student from <a href="/wiki/Necochea" title="Necochea">Necochea</a> who was murdered by serial shooter <a href="/wiki/Mart%C3%ADn_R%C3%ADos_(murderer)" title="Martín Ríos (murderer)">Martín Ríos</a> in July 2006 in <a href="/wiki/Belgrano,_Buenos_Aires" title="Belgrano, Buenos Aires">Belgrano, Buenos Aires</a>, labelled Bullrich\'s comments as "enormously grave" for Argentine society.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-39" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-39"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>39<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Presidential_candidate">Presidential candidate</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Patricia_Bullrich&amp;action=edit&amp;section=5" title="Edit section: Presidential candidate"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Abrazo_Milei_y_Bullrich,_pato_y_le%C3%B3n.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1b/Abrazo_Milei_y_Bullrich%2C_pato_y_le%C3%B3n.jpg/250px-Abrazo_Milei_y_Bullrich%2C_pato_y_le%C3%B3n.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="250" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1b/Abrazo_Milei_y_Bullrich%2C_pato_y_le%C3%B3n.jpg/500px-Abrazo_Milei_y_Bullrich%2C_pato_y_le%C3%B3n.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="1024" data-file-height="1024" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/AI_image" class="mw-redirect" title="AI image">AI image</a> posted by <a href="/wiki/Javier_Milei" title="Javier Milei">Javier Milei</a> to announce his alliance with Bullrich. Milei associates himself with imagery of lions, and "pato" ("duck") is a common nickname in Spanish for people named "Patricia".<sup id="cite&#95;ref-:0&#95;40-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:0-40"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>40<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup></figcaption></figure>\n<p>The <a href="/wiki/2021_Argentine_legislative_election" title="2021 Argentine legislative election">2021 Argentine legislative election</a> resulted in a victory for <a href="/wiki/Juntos_por_el_Cambio" title="Juntos por el Cambio">Juntos por el Cambio</a> (JXC), with the libertarian party <a href="/wiki/La_Libertad_Avanza" title="La Libertad Avanza">La Libertad Avanza</a> (LLA) led by <a href="/wiki/Javier_Milei" title="Javier Milei">Javier Milei</a>, emerging as a significant <a href="/wiki/Third_party_(politics)" class="mw-redirect" title="Third party (politics)">third party</a>.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-41" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-41"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>41<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Bullrich, who was appointed president of the PRO in 2020,<sup id="cite&#95;ref-42" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-42"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>42<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> maintained a positive relationship with Milei, and at one point considered forming an alliance for the <a href="/wiki/2023_Argentine_general_election" title="2023 Argentine general election">2023 Argentine general election</a>. However, Milei ultimately decided to run independently with his own party.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-43" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-43"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>43<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>There was an expectation that Mauricio Macri would run for president once again, as even in defeat he had gotten 41% of the vote in 2019 and his image had improved since then. However, he declined to do so, so the party had primary elections between Bullrich and Horacio Rodríguez Larreta. They represented the "hawks" and "doves" of the party. Macri did not openly side with any of them.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-44" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-44"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>44<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Bullrich chose the former legislator <a href="/wiki/Luis_Petri" title="Luis Petri">Luis Petri</a>, from the UCR, as the candidate for vice-president. Petri had lost the primary elections for governor of Mendoza to <a href="/wiki/Alfredo_Cornejo_(politician)" title="Alfredo Cornejo (politician)">Alfredo Cornejo</a> a short time before. She chose him because he was young, sided with the "hawks", and was not from Buenos Aires; and also because he worked with her during her time as minister of security. As Petri was from the UCR, Bullrich would secure the support of the radicals that were not pleased with the leadership of <a href="/wiki/Gerardo_Morales_(politician)" title="Gerardo Morales (politician)">Gerardo Morales</a> (who supported Larreta), and with the whole party if Larreta was defeated in the primaries. Other politicians briefly considered to run for vice-president under her were <a href="/wiki/Carlos_Melconian" title="Carlos Melconian">Carlos Melconian</a>, <a href="/wiki/Maximiliano_Abad" title="Maximiliano Abad">Maximiliano Abad</a>, <a href="/w/index.php?title=Luis_Naidenoff&amp;action=edit&amp;redlink=1" class="new" title="Luis Naidenoff (page does not exist)">Luis Naidenoff</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Ricardo_L%C3%B3pez_Murphy" title="Ricardo López Murphy">Ricardo López Murphy</a>.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-45" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-45"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>45<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>  \n</p><p>Carlos Melconian was proposed instead as Bullrich\'s potential minister of economy. In contrast with Milei, who proposed a full <a href="/wiki/Dollarization" class="mw-redirect" title="Dollarization">dollarization</a> of the economy, Melconian proposed instead a bimonetary economy, where both the <a href="/wiki/Argentine_peso" title="Argentine peso">Argentine peso</a> and the <a href="/wiki/United_States_dollar" title="United States dollar">United States dollar</a> would be legal tender. Before implementing it, the fiscal deficit would be eliminated, the by-laws of the Central Bank would be amended to prohibit <a href="/wiki/Debt_monetization" title="Debt monetization">money creation</a>, and the restrictions on the use of US dollars would be removed.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-46" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-46"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>46<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> She also proposed the creation of a maximum security prison named after former president Cristina Kirchner.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-47" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-47"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>47<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> \n</p><p>The primary elections ended with a decisive victory of Bullrich over Larreta.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-48" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-48"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>48<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Once the primaries were concluded, the candidates took part in the <a href="/wiki/Presidential_debates_in_Argentina" title="Presidential debates in Argentina">presidential debates</a>, explaining their positions and proposals over several topics.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-49" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-49"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>49<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Bullrich promised to end inflation, and to end the roadblocks caused by piqueteros.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-50" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-50"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>50<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>Although the primary elections ended with the three main candidates, Bullrich, Milei and Peronist <a href="/wiki/Sergio_Massa" title="Sergio Massa">Sergio Massa</a> in a close tie, Massa got ahead in the general election and won with 36% of the vote, followed by Milei with 30%. As a result, both candidates went to a third <a href="/wiki/Ballotage" class="mw-redirect" title="Ballotage">ballotage</a> election. Bullrich did not take part in it, as JXC ended in third place, but both candidates sought to get the support of her voters. Massa made a speech about institutional stability and public security, usual topics of the UCR and PRO respectively, and Milei focused on the need to join forces against Kirchnerism.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-51" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-51"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>51<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> On 25 October 2023, Bullrich officially endorsed Javier Milei for the runoff election.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-52" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-52"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>52<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> She did not ask the other parties within JXC, the UCR and the CC, for their opinion, as they have conflicting views over Milei. Both of them met the Wednesday after the elections to negotiate this support, alongside Macri. Milei announced the alliance on his <a href="/wiki/X_(Twitter)" class="mw-redirect" title="X (Twitter)">X</a> account, with an <a href="/wiki/AI_image" class="mw-redirect" title="AI image">AI image</a> of an embrace between a lion and a duck. Milei associates himself with imagery of lions, and "pato" ("duck") is a common nickname in Spanish for people named "Patricia".<sup id="cite&#95;ref-:0&#95;40-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:0-40"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>40<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Minister_of_Security_(2023–2025)"><span id="Minister_of_Security_.282023.E2.80.932025.29"></span>Minister of Security (2023–2025)</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Patricia_Bullrich&amp;action=edit&amp;section=6" title="Edit section: Minister of Security (2023–2025)"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Bullrich_Plan_Bandera_1.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d7/Bullrich_Plan_Bandera_1.jpg/250px-Bullrich_Plan_Bandera_1.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="141" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d7/Bullrich_Plan_Bandera_1.jpg/500px-Bullrich_Plan_Bandera_1.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="1920" data-file-height="1080" /></a><figcaption>Patricia Bullrich announced a decrease in homicides in <a href="/wiki/Rosario" title="Rosario">Rosario</a>.</figcaption></figure>\n<p>In December 2023, Patricia Bullrich returned to government as security minister in  president <a href="/wiki/Presidency_of_Javier_Milei" title="Presidency of Javier Milei">Javier Milei\'s Cabinet.</a><sup id="cite&#95;ref-53" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-53"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>53<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Bullrich immediately issued a protocol to deal with demonstrations and roadblocks made by <a href="/wiki/Piquetero" title="Piquetero">piqueteros</a>. The <a href="/wiki/Workers%27_Party_(Argentina)" title="Workers&#39; Party (Argentina)">Workers\' Party</a> made an <i><a href="/wiki/Habeas_corpus" title="Habeas corpus">habeas corpus</a></i> request to prevent the protocol from coming into force, which judge Gustavo Pierretti rejected. Several groups of Piqueteros called for a massive demonstration on 20 December, a week after the <a href="/wiki/Inauguration_of_Javier_Milei" title="Inauguration of Javier Milei">inauguration of Javier Milei</a>. The government announced that demonstrators who committed crimes during demonstrations, such as roadblocks or vandalism, would lose their welfare payments, and provided a phone number to denounce piquetero leaders who would be coercing people to take part in such demonstrations. The demonstration had very little attendance, and the phone calls were used to start 660 criminal complaints.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-54" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-54"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>54<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> The policies were kept for all later protests. The welfare aid that was outsourced to piquetero organizations returned to the direct state control, and social leaders that worked at the <a href="/wiki/Ministry_of_Social_Development_(Argentina)" title="Ministry of Social Development (Argentina)">ministry of Social Development</a> despite the conflict of interest were fired. Several audits also revealed that several social organizations that used to control the outsourced welfare aid only used a fraction of it for such a purpose. All this decreased the power of piqueteros, and protests and demonstrations rapidly decreased in size.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-55" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-55"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>55<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>The city of <a href="/wiki/Rosario" title="Rosario">Rosario</a> had ongoing problems with narcotics trafficking cartels, who had moved beyond the <a href="/wiki/Illegal_drug_trade" title="Illegal drug trade">illegal drug trade</a> into other illicit activities, such as <a href="/wiki/Extortion" title="Extortion">extortion</a> and <a href="/wiki/Contract_killing" title="Contract killing">contract killing</a>. Bullrich announced the "Plan Bandera" ("Flag plan") with <a href="/wiki/Governor_of_Santa_Fe_Province" title="Governor of Santa Fe Province">governor of Santa Fe Province</a> <a href="/wiki/Maximiliano_Pullaro" title="Maximiliano Pullaro">Maximiliano Pullaro</a> to deal with the problem. One of the initial actions was to enforce stricter conditions at the local prisons, as several crime bosses were already jailed but managed to control the criminal operations nonetheless. The national government installed <a href="/wiki/Mobile_phone_jammer" title="Mobile phone jammer">mobile phone jammers</a> at those prisons, which led to death threats against Pullaro and his family.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-56" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-56"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>56<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Bullrich provided a report of the results of the operation six months later: homicides decreased by 73%, they detained 400 people linked to drug trade, 118 kilograms of cocaine and dope, 50,000 parts of <a href="/wiki/Synthetic_drug" title="Synthetic drug">synthetic drugs</a>, 900 kilograms of ammonia, 57,005,062 <a href="/wiki/Argentine_peso" title="Argentine peso">pesos</a>, 18,050 US dollars and 70 weapons.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-57" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-57"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>57<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>Bullrich stayed president of PRO despite being a minister of a government for another party. Initially, both PRO and LLA were allies, but as both parties began to drift apart she sided with Milei\'s party instead of PRO. Both parties ran for the 2025 legislative elections on their own after the failure of the negotiations to create an electoral alliance. Bullrich took part in electoral parades of LLA, and encouraged politicians close to her move to the party. In May 2025 she formally left the PRO and joined LLA.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-58" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-58"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>58<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-59" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-59"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>59<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>Following her election as senator in the 2025 legislative election, on 22 November 2025 President Javier Milei confirmed that <a href="/wiki/Alejandra_Monteoliva" title="Alejandra Monteoliva">Alejandra Monteoliva</a> would be her successor.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-perfil&#95;60-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-perfil-60"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>60<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Bullrich resigned on 1 December 2025 and Monteoliva took office the following day.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-61" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-61"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>61<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-bio&#95;62-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-bio-62"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>62<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Political_positions">Political positions</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Patricia_Bullrich&amp;action=edit&amp;section=7" title="Edit section: Political positions"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:La_ministra_de_seguridad_Patricia_Bullrich_anuncio_el_nuevo_protocolo_de_actuaci%C3%B3n_antipiquetes.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b9/La_ministra_de_seguridad_Patricia_Bullrich_anuncio_el_nuevo_protocolo_de_actuaci%C3%B3n_antipiquetes.jpg/250px-La_ministra_de_seguridad_Patricia_Bullrich_anuncio_el_nuevo_protocolo_de_actuaci%C3%B3n_antipiquetes.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="167" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b9/La_ministra_de_seguridad_Patricia_Bullrich_anuncio_el_nuevo_protocolo_de_actuaci%C3%B3n_antipiquetes.jpg/500px-La_ministra_de_seguridad_Patricia_Bullrich_anuncio_el_nuevo_protocolo_de_actuaci%C3%B3n_antipiquetes.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="1600" data-file-height="1066" /></a><figcaption>Patricia Bullrich announces new policies against <a href="/wiki/Traffic_obstruction" title="Traffic obstruction">traffic obstructions</a> by <a href="/wiki/Piquetero" title="Piquetero">piqueteros</a>.</figcaption></figure> \n<p>Patricia Bullrich was a member of Peronist guerrillas in her youth, but grew critical of them as an adult. She described the ideas held by those organizations as an improvised blend of <a href="/wiki/Argentine_nationalism" title="Argentine nationalism">nationalism</a>, <a href="/wiki/Christianity_in_Argentina" class="mw-redirect" title="Christianity in Argentina">Christianity</a> and <a href="/wiki/Socialism_in_Argentina" title="Socialism in Argentina">socialism</a>. She explained that back then she thought that she was taking part in a <a href="/wiki/Revolution" title="Revolution">revolution</a> and that the people would eventually get used to it, but eventually realized that revolutions rarely have a positive outcome. She also thinks that she deluded herself by thinking that <a href="/wiki/Peronism" title="Peronism">Peronism</a> had goals that were not its actual goals. She started to have doubts over her allegiance to the guerrillas when she found out that Montoneros had killed the priest <a href="/wiki/Carlos_Mugica" title="Carlos Mugica">Carlos Mugica</a>, and the aide of Perón <a href="/wiki/Jos%C3%A9_Ignacio_Rucci" title="José Ignacio Rucci">José Ignacio Rucci</a>. She realized that Montoneros and the <a href="/wiki/People%27s_Revolutionary_Army_(Argentina)" title="People&#39;s Revolutionary Army (Argentina)">People\'s Revolutionary Army</a> killed people, even if they had not said so openly, and that she was helping that even if from a passive role.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-autocritica&#95;16-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-autocritica-16"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>16<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> \n</p><p>In her book <i>Yo Propongo</i>, written during the presidency of Cristina Kirchner, Bullrich talks about <a href="/wiki/Populism" title="Populism">populism</a> and <a href="/wiki/Authoritarianism" title="Authoritarianism">authoritarianism</a>. She considers that democracy in Argentina has been weakened by a <a href="/wiki/Dominant-party_system" title="Dominant-party system">dominant-party system</a> coupled with the dismantling of the lead party, which led to a system where only the president has authority, the party is an extension of the president\'s will, and government and state lost any meaningful difference. She considers that <a href="/wiki/Political_polarization" title="Political polarization">political polarization</a> grew beyond only politics and engulfed other areas as well, such as academics and unions. She also pointed out that the Kirchners may want to organize a set of controlled media to advance a "narrative" that is positive towards their policies and hostile against the opposition. She also considers that this style of government was used by the Kirchners to advance policies that are long outdated in the rest of the world, and to conceal its negative results.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-63" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-63"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>63<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> In contrast, she proposes to dismantle in politics the dominant-party system, and in economics to advance a sustainable capitalist model.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-64" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-64"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>64<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>  \n</p><p>In relation to the severity of <a href="/wiki/Law_enforcement" title="Law enforcement">law enforcement</a>, she supports a hardline policy against crime, rejecting the policies of <a href="/wiki/Kirchnerism" title="Kirchnerism">Kirchnerism</a> that grant too many rights to criminals and place rigid controls and obstacles on police work. Although those policies are largely a reaction against the policies of the military dictatorship, Bullrich says that "Argentina must leave the past and look to the future".<sup id="cite&#95;ref-autocritica&#95;16-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-autocritica-16"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>16<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> In particular, she had conflicting views with <a href="/wiki/Sabina_Frederic" title="Sabina Frederic">Sabina Frederic</a>, minister of security of Alberto Fernández, over the use of <a href="/wiki/Taser" title="Taser">taser</a> guns, as Frederic restricted the police of the <a href="/wiki/Argentine_Federal_Police" title="Argentine Federal Police">Argentine Federal Police</a> from using either those or regular guns.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-65" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-65"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>65<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> When she was appointed minister of security by Javier Milei, she said "True change is possible if the law is applied in every corner of the country, equally for everyone and without privileges. Argentina needs order. We will be relentless against crime and we will wage a relentless fight against drug trafficking. It\'s simple: whoever does something, pays for it".<sup id="cite&#95;ref-quien&#95;12-5" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-quien-12"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>12<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>Patricia Bullrich supported <a href="/wiki/Abortion" title="Abortion">abortion</a> during the debate in 2018 for a bill that would make it legal. She said that it did not make sense that only the woman could go to jail for it.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-66" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-66"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>66<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> However, she also supported a clause for <a href="/wiki/Conscientious_objection_to_abortion" title="Conscientious objection to abortion">conscientious objection to abortion</a> from medics that may refuse to do it, and to set a <a href="/wiki/Minors_and_abortion" title="Minors and abortion">minimum age</a> higher than in the proposed bill.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-67" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-67"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>67<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> The bill was not approved, and was proposed again in 2020. That time, Bullrich refused to comment her personal opinion on abortion, and considered instead that the country had more pressing economic and societal priorities.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-68" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-68"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>68<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> For similar reasons, she did not agree with the proposal of <a href="/wiki/Javier_Milei" title="Javier Milei">Javier Milei</a> to celebrate a referendum to abolish the bill approved in 2020: she said that it would halt the whole country for a couple of months, and that the priority was to solve the economic crisis.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-69" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-69"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>69<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Electoral_history">Electoral history</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Patricia_Bullrich&amp;action=edit&amp;section=8" title="Edit section: Electoral history"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Executive">Executive</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Patricia_Bullrich&amp;action=edit&amp;section=9" title="Edit section: Executive"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<table class="wikitable" style="font-size:90%;
