David Polly">Polly</a> (2020).<sup id="cite&#95;ref-227" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-227"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>227<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup></li>\n<li>Description of the tarsal bones of the <a href="/wiki/Bear_dogs" class="mw-redirect" title="Bear dogs">bear dogs</a> from the Paleogene of Europe, and a study on the evolution of posture and locomotion of European bear dogs, is published by Fournier <i>et al.</i> (2020).<sup id="cite&#95;ref-228" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-228"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>228<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup></li>\n<li>New fossil material of <i><a href="/w/index.php?title=Megamphicyon&amp;action=edit&amp;redlink=1" class="new" title="Megamphicyon (page does not exist)">Megamphicyon</a> giganteus</i>, providing new information on the locomotor adaptations of this species and allowing an estimation of its body mass, is described from the middle Miocene (<a href="/wiki/MN_zonation" class="mw-redirect" title="MN zonation">MN6</a>) site of Carpetana (<a href="/wiki/Spain" title="Spain">Spain</a>) by Siliceo <i>et al.</i> (2020).<sup id="cite&#95;ref-229" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-229"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>229<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup></li>\n<li>A study aiming to determine the impact of large body size and adaptation to <a href="/wiki/Hypercarnivore" title="Hypercarnivore">hypercarnivory</a> on extinction risk throughout the evolutionary history of North American <a href="/wiki/Canidae" title="Canidae">canids</a> is published by Balisi &amp; Van Valkenburgh (2020).<sup id="cite&#95;ref-230" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-230"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>230<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup></li>\n<li>A study on the anatomy of the <a href="/wiki/Holotype" title="Holotype">holotype</a> specimen of <i><a href="/w/index.php?title=Vulpes_alopecoides&amp;action=edit&amp;redlink=1" class="new" title="Vulpes alopecoides (page does not exist)">Vulpes alopecoides</a></i> and on the diversity of the Plio-Pleistocene members of the genus <i><a href="/wiki/Vulpes" title="Vulpes">Vulpes</a></i> from Europe is published by Bartolini Lucenti &amp; Madurell-Malapeira (2020), who consider the species <i>Vulpes praeglacialis</i> and <i>V. praecorsac</i> to be <a href="/wiki/Synonym_(taxonomy)" title="Synonym (taxonomy)">junior synonyms</a> of <i>V. alopecoides</i>.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-231" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-231"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>231<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup></li>\n<li>A study on the anatomy and likely diet of <i><a href="/wiki/Canis_ferox" class="mw-redirect" title="Canis ferox">"Canis" ferox</a></i> is published online by Bartolini Lucenti &amp; Rook (2020), who transfer this species to the genus <i><a href="/wiki/Eucyon" title="Eucyon">Eucyon</a></i>.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-232" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-232"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>232<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup></li>\n<li>Tong <i>et al.</i> (2020) document dental injuries (likely caused by processing hard food, such as bones) and infections and a healed <a href="/wiki/Tibia" title="Tibia">tibia</a> fracture in specimens of <i><a href="/wiki/Canis_chihliensis" class="mw-redirect" title="Canis chihliensis">Canis chihliensis</a></i> from the Early Pleistocene <a href="/wiki/Nihewan_Basin" class="mw-redirect" title="Nihewan Basin">Nihewan Basin</a> (China), and interpret these findings as possible evidence of social hunting and family care in this canid.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-233" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-233"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>233<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup></li>\n<li>A study comparing the anatomy of <a href="/wiki/Hyoid_bone" title="Hyoid bone">hyoid bones</a> of <a href="/wiki/Dire_wolf" title="Dire wolf">dire wolves</a> and <a href="/wiki/Coyote" title="Coyote">coyotes</a> from <a href="/wiki/La_Brea_Tar_Pits" title="La Brea Tar Pits">La Brea Tar Pits</a> with those of extant <a href="/wiki/Canidae" title="Canidae">canids</a>, and evaluating the implications of reported anatomical differences for the knowledge of likely vocalizations of fossil canids, is published by Flores <i>et al.</i> (2020).<sup id="cite&#95;ref-234" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-234"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>234<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup></li>\n<li>The study of the extensive record of <i>Canis</i> from <a href="/wiki/Dmanisi" title="Dmanisi">Dmanisi</a> showed the combination so primitive and derived species that contrast with the previous interpretation of these specimens to <a href="/wiki/Canis_etruscus" title="Canis etruscus"><i>Canis</i> <i>etruscus</i></a> and support the description of the new species <i><a href="/wiki/Canis_borjgali" title="Canis borjgali">Canis borjgali</a></i>, very close to <i><a href="/wiki/Canis_mosbachensis" title="Canis mosbachensis">Canis mosbachensis</a></i> and probably to modern <a href="/wiki/Wolf" title="Wolf">wolves</a>, <a href="/wiki/Coyote" title="Coyote">coyotes</a>  and affine <a href="/wiki/Canis" title="Canis">dogs</a> (Bartolini Lucenti <i>et al.</i> 2020 <sup id="cite&#95;ref-:0&#95;235-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:0-235"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>235<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>)</li>\n<li>Partial fragment of the mandible of a dire wolf is described from the Late Pleistocene of northeastern China by Lu <i>et al.</i> (2020), representing the first record of this species from Eurasia reported so far.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-236" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-236"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>236<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup></li>\n<li>Ramos-Madrigal <i>et al.</i> (2020) sequence the genomes of four Pleistocene wolves from Northeast Siberia, including specimens with divergent skull morphologies.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-237" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-237"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>237<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup></li>\n<li>A study on a 57,000-years-old wolf pup mummy discovered in thawing permafrost in the Klondike goldfields (<a href="/wiki/Yukon" title="Yukon">Yukon</a>, <a href="/wiki/Canada" title="Canada">Canada</a>), aiming to determine her appearance, evolutionary relationships, life history and ecology, is published by Meachen <i>et al.</i> (2020).<sup id="cite&#95;ref-238" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-238"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>238<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup></li>\n<li>A study on fossil canid remains from the Pleistocene of the <a href="/wiki/Paglicci_Cave" title="Paglicci Cave">Paglicci Cave</a> and the Romanelli Cave (southern <a href="/wiki/Italy" title="Italy">Italy</a>) is published by Boschin <i>et al.</i> (2020), who interpret their findings as attesting the presence of dogs in Italy at least 14,000 <a href="/wiki/Radiocarbon_dating#Calibration" title="Radiocarbon dating">calibrated years</a> before present.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-239" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-239"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>239<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup></li>\n<li>A study on the genomes of modern Greenland <a href="/wiki/Sled_dog" title="Sled dog">sled dogs</a>, an ~9500-year-old Siberian dog associated with archaeological evidence for sled technology, and an ~33,000-year-old Siberian wolf is published by Sinding <i>et al.</i> (2020), who interpret their findings as indicating that sled dogs represent an ancient lineage going back at least 9500 years and that wolves bred with the ancestors of sled dogs and precontact American dogs.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-240" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-240"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>240<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup></li>\n<li>A study on aiming to reconstruct dog population history, based on data from 27 ancient (up to 10.9 thousand years old) dog genomes from Europe, the Near East and Siberia, is published by Bergström <i>et al.</i> (2020).<sup id="cite&#95;ref-241" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-241"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>241<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup></li>\n<li>New specimen of <i><a href="/wiki/Agnotherium" title="Agnotherium">Agnotherium</a> antiquum</i>, providing new information on the anatomy of this species, is described from the <a href="/wiki/Miocene" title="Miocene">Miocene</a> locality of <a href="/wiki/Eppelsheim" title="Eppelsheim">Eppelsheim</a> (<a href="/wiki/Germany" title="Germany">Germany</a>) by Morlo <i>et al.</i> (2020), who interpret this species as a powerful, strictly carnivorous ambush hunter.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-242" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-242"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>242<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup></li>\n<li>A <a href="/wiki/Metacarpal_bones" title="Metacarpal bones">metacarpal bone</a> of a <a href="/wiki/Arctodus" title="Arctodus">short-faced bear</a> is described from Daisy Cave (<a href="/wiki/San_Miguel_Island" title="San Miguel Island">San Miguel Island</a>, <a href="/wiki/Channel_Islands_(California)" title="Channel Islands (California)">California Channel Islands</a>) by Mychajliw <i>et al.</i> (2020), who attempt to the determine the most likely explanation of the occurrence of this specimen on San Miguel Island.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-243" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-243"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>243<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup></li>\n<li>A study on anatomical <i>et al.</i> (2020).<sup id="cite&#95;ref-244" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-244"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>244<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup></li>\n<li>A study on the diet of cave bears from cave sites in <a href="/wiki/Romania" title="Romania">Romania</a>, as indicated by nitrogen isotope values of individual amino acids from fossil collagen, is published research</h4><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=2020_in_paleomammalogy&amp;action=edit&amp;section=32" title="Edit section: Miscellaneous laurasiatherian research"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<ul><li>A review of the origins, evolution and paleoecology of major <a href="/wiki/Clade" title="Clade">clades</a> of extinct native South American ungulates is published by Croft, Gelfo &amp; López (2020).<sup id="cite&#95;ref-294" class="reference"><a class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-295"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>295<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup></li>\n<li>A study on the phylogenetic relationships of the <a affinities.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-296" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-296"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>296<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup></li>\n<li>A study on the dietary habits of <i><a href="/wiki/Macrauchenia" title="Macrauchenia">Macrauchenia</a> patachonica</i> and <i><a href="/wiki/Xenorhinotherium" title="Xenorhinotherium">Xenorhinotherium</a> bahiense</i> is published by de Oliveira <i>et al.</i> (2020);<sup id="cite&#95;ref-297" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-297"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>297<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> the study is subsequently criticized by Dantas, Lobo &amp; Bernardes (2020).<sup id="cite&#95;ref-298" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-298"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>298<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-299" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-299"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>299<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup></li>\n<li>A study on the anatomy, phylogenetic relationships and likely diet and locomotion of <i><a href="/wiki/Cambaytherium" title="Cambaytherium">Cambaytherium</a></i> is published by Rose <i>et al.</i> (2020), who also name a new clade <a href="/wiki/Perissodactylamorpha" class="mw-redirect" title="Perissodactylamorpha">Perissodactylamorpha</a> containing the group <a href="/wiki/Anthracobunia" class="mw-redirect" title="Anthracobunia">Anthracobunia</a> and odd-toed ungulates.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-300" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-300"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>300<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup></li></ul>\n<div class="mw-heading Announced in 2018; the final version of the article naming it was published in 2020.\n</td>\n<td>\n</td></tr>\n</tbody></table>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Miscellaneous_eutherian_research">Miscellaneous eutherian research</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=2020_in_paleomammalogy&amp;action=edit&amp;section=34" title="Edit section: Miscellaneous eutherian research"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<ul><li>Eberle, von Koenigswald &amp; Eberth (2020) study the <a href="/wiki/Tooth_enamel" title="Tooth enamel">enamel</a> microstructure of mammalian tooth fragments from the Strathcona Fiord Fossil Forest (Eocene <a href="/wiki/Margaret_Formation" title="Margaret Formation">Margaret Formation</a>; <a href="/wiki/Ellesmere_Island" title="Ellesmere Island">Ellesmere Island</a>, <a href="/wiki/Canada" title="Canada">Canada</a>), and identify them as teeth of <i><a href="/wiki/Coryphodon" title="Coryphodon">Coryphodon</a></i>.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-303" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-303"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>303<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup></li></ul>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="General_eutherian_research">General eutherian research</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=2020_in_paleomammalogy&amp;action=edit&amp;section=35" title="Edit section: General eutherian research"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<ul><li>A study on the evolution of feeding strategies in marine mammals throughout their evolutionary history is published by <a href="/wiki/Annalisa_Berta" title="Annalisa Berta">Berta</a> &amp; Lanzetti (2020).<sup id="cite&#95;ref-304" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-304"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>304<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup></li>\n<li>A study on zinc isotope ratios in <a href="/wiki/Tooth_enamel" title="Tooth enamel">tooth enamel</a> of Late Pleistocene mammals from the Tam Hay Marklot cave (<a href="/wiki/Laos" title="Laos">Laos</a>) is published by Bourgon <i>et al.</i> (2020), who evaluate potential utility of zinc isotopes as dietary tracers in paleontology and archeology.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-305" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-305"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>305<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup></li>\n<li>A study on the dietary patterns of nine herbivore families from the <a href="/wiki/Shungura_Formation" title="Shungura Formation">Shungura Formation</a> (<a href="/wiki/Ethiopia" title="Ethiopia">Ethiopia</a>) throughout the late Pliocene and early Pleistocene, as indicated by carbon isotope data from fossil teeth, is published by Negash <i>et al.</i> (2020).<sup id="cite&#95;ref-306" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-306"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>306<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup></li>\n<li>Hominin and non-hominin mammal footprints and fossils dating to the <a href="/wiki/Eemian" class="mw-redirect" title="Eemian">last interglacial</a> are reported from the Alathar lacustrine deposit in the western Nefud Desert (<a href="/wiki/Saudi_Arabia" title="Saudi Arabia">Saudi Arabia</a>) by Stewart <i>et al.</i> (2020), who interpret this finding as likely to be the earliest evidence of <i>Homo sapiens</i> in the <a href="/wiki/Arabian_Peninsula" title="Arabian Peninsula">Arabian Peninsula</a> reported so far.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-307" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-307"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>307<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup></li>\n<li>A study on ancient DNA recovered from fragmented <a href="/wiki/Bovidae" title="Bovidae">bovid</a> and rhinoceros specimens from the <a href="/wiki/Neolithic" title="Neolithic">Neolithic</a> site of Shannashuzha is published by Chen <i>et al.</i> (2020), who interpret their findings as indicating that the <a href="/wiki/Gaur" title="Gaur">gaur</a> and a rhinoceros closely related to the extant <a href="/wiki/Sumatran_rhinoceros" title="Sumatran rhinoceros">Sumatran rhinoceros</a> lived as far north as the margin of the northeastern <a href="/wiki/Tibetan_Plateau" title="Tibetan Plateau">Tibetan Plateau</a> during the late Neolithic.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-308" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-308"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>308<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup></li></ul>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Metatherians">Metatherians</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=2020_in_paleomammalogy&amp;action=edit&amp;section=36" title="Edit section: class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Metatherian_research">Metatherian research</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=2020_in_paleomammalogy&amp;action=edit&amp;section=37" title="Edit section: Metatherian research"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<ul><li>Two isolated teeth of <a href="/wiki/Stagodontidae" title="Stagodontidae">stagodontid</a> metatherians are described from the <a href="/wiki/Cenomanian" title="Cenomanian">Cenomanian</a> of <a href="/wiki/France" title="France">France</a> by Vullo <i>et al.</i> (2020), representing the first reported occurrence of stagodontids in Europe.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-320" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-320"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>320<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup></li>\n<li>A study on the anatomy of the skull of <i><a href="/wiki/Andinodelphys" title="Andinodelphys">Andinodelphys</a> cochabambensis</i>, and on the phylogenetic relationships of this species, is published by de Muizon &amp; Ladevèze (2020).<sup id="cite&#95;ref-321" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-321"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>321<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup></li>\n<li>A study comparing the anatomy of the skull and teeth of <i><a href="/wiki/Thylacosmilus" title="Thylacosmilus">Thylacosmilus</a> atrox</i> and <a href="/wiki/Placentalia" title="Placentalia">placental</a> saber-toothed carnivores is published by <a href="/wiki/Christine_Janis" title="Christine Janis">Janis</a> <i>et al.</i> (2020), who question the interpretation of <i>T. atrox</i> as having a similar type of predatory behavior to placental saber-tooths, and consider it unlikely that <i>T. atrox</i> used its <a href="/wiki/Canine_tooth" title="Canine tooth">canines</a> to dispatch its prey.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-322" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-322"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>322<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup></li>\n<li>A study on the anatomy of the petrosal and inner ear of <i><a href="/wiki/Peratherium" title="Peratherium">Peratherium</a> elegans</i> and <i><a href="/wiki/Amphiperatherium" title="Amphiperatherium">Amphiperatherium</a> elegans</i>, and on its implications for the knowledge of the phylogenetic relationships of <a href="/wiki/Herpetotheriidae" title="Herpetotheriidae">herpetotheriids</a> and <a href="/wiki/Peradectidae" title="Peradectidae">peradectids</a>, is published online by Ladevèze, Selva &amp; de Muizon (2020).<sup id="cite&#95;ref-323" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-323"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>323<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup></li>\n<li>A study on the anatomy of the teeth of <i><a href="/w/index.php?title=Groeberia&amp;action=edit&amp;redlink=1" class="new" title="Groeberia (page does not exist)">Groeberia</a></i>, and on the phylogenetic affinities of this genus, is published by Zimicz &amp; Goin (2020).<sup id="cite&#95;ref-324" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-324"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>324<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup></li>\n<li>A study on the relationship between variation in skull and mandibular shape of extant and extinct <a href="/wiki/Macropodiformes" title="Macropodiformes">macropodiforms</a> and ecological factors such as diet, locomotion and body mass, and on the implications of this relationship for the knowledge of the feeding ecology of the fossil macropodiforms from the <a href="/wiki/Riversleigh_World_Heritage_Area" title="Riversleigh World Heritage Area">Riversleigh World Heritage Area</a>, is published online by Butler <i>et al.</i> (2020).<sup id="cite&#95;ref-325" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-325"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>325<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup></li>\n<li>A study on the morphology of the <a href="/wiki/Humerus" title="Humerus">humeri</a> of fossil kangaroos belonging to the subfamily <a href="/wiki/Sthenurinae" title="Sthenurinae">Sthenurinae</a> and of <i><a href="/wiki/Protemnodon" title="Protemnodon">Protemnodon</a></i>, evaluating its implications for the knowledge of the mode of locomotion in these marsupials, is published online by <a href="/wiki/Christine_Janis" title="Christine Janis">Janis</a> <i>et al.</i> (2020).<sup id="cite&#95;ref-326" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-326"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>326<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup></li>\n<li>The hypothesis that marsupial forelimbs are restricted by long-term developmental constraints resulting from their reproductive strategy, is challenged in a paper to be published by Martin-Serra and Benson (2020).<sup id="cite&#95;ref-327" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-327"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>327<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup></li></ul>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Allotheria">Allotheria</h2><span nov\n</p>\n</td>\n<td>\n<p>valid\n</p>\n</td>\n<td>\n<p>Jäger, Cifelli &amp; Martin\n</p>\n</td>\n<td>\n<p><a href="/wiki/Early_Cretaceous" title="Early Cretaceous">Early Cretaceous</a> (<a </span><a href="/wiki/United_Kingdom" title="United Kingdom">United Kingdom</a>\n</p>\n</td>\n<td>\n<p>A <a href="/w/index.php?title=Triconodonid&amp;action=edit&amp;redlink=1" class="new" title="Triconodonid (page does not exist)">triconodonid</a> <a href="/wiki/Eutriconodonta" title="Eutriconodonta">Eutriconodontan</a>\n</p>\n</td>\n<td>\n</td></tr>\n</tbody></table>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Miscellaneous_mammalian_research">Miscellaneous mammalian research</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=2020_in_paleomammalogy&amp;action=edit&amp;section=44" title="Edit section: Miscellaneous mammalian research"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<ul><li>A study on the phylogenetic relationships of <a href="/wiki/Mesozoic" title="Mesozoic">Mesozoic</a> mammals, aiming to determine the <a href="/wiki/Morphology_(biology)" title="Morphology (biology)">morphological</a> character complexes with a high potential to introduce phylogenetic error, is published by Celik &amp; Phillips (2020).<sup id="cite&#95;ref-352" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-352"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>352<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup></li>\n<li>A study on maximum lifespans and blood flow rates of <i><a href="/wiki/Morganucodon" title="Morganucodon">Morganucodon</a></i> and <i><a href="/wiki/Kuehneotherium" title="Kuehneotherium">Kuehneotherium</a></i>, evaluating their implications for the knowledge of <a href="/wiki/Basal_metabolic_rate" title="Basal metabolic rate">basal</a> and maximum metabolic rates in these taxa, is published by Newham <i>et al.</i> (2020);<sup id="cite&#95;ref-353" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-353"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>353<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> their conclusions are subsequently contested by Meiri &amp; Levin (2022).<sup id="cite&#95;ref-354" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-354"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>354<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-355" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-355"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>355<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup></li>\n<li>A study on the jaw morphology, jaw movement and <a href="/wiki/Occlusion_(dentistry)" title="Occlusion (dentistry)">occlusion</a> in <i><a href="/wiki/Priacodon" title="Priacodon">Priacodon</a></i>, and on its implications for the knowledge of the occlusal mode and likely diet of <a href="/wiki/Triconodontidae" title="Triconodontidae">triconodontids</a> in general, is published by Jäger, Cifelli &amp; Martin (2020).<sup id="cite&#95;ref-356" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-356"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>356<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup></li></ul>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="General_research">General research</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=2020_in_paleomammalogy&amp;action=edit&amp;section=45" title="Edit section: General research"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<ul><li>A study on the phylogenetic relationships of the <a href="/wiki/Haramiyida" title="Haramiyida">haramiyidans</a> and on the consistency between the known <a href="/wiki/Morphology_(biology)" title="Morphology (biology)">morphology</a> and age of <i><a href="/wiki/Juramaia" title="Juramaia">Juramaia</a></i> and other <a href="/wiki/Mammaliaformes" title="Mammaliaformes">mammaliaforms</a> from the <a href="/wiki/Yanliao_Biota" title="Yanliao Biota">Yanliao Biota</a>, as indicated by Bayesian <a href="/wiki/Tip_dating" title="Tip dating">tip-dated</a> phylogenetic methods, is published by King &amp; Beck (2020).<sup id="cite&#95;ref-357" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-357"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>357<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup></li>\n<li>A study on the community-level response of North American mammals to <a href="/wiki/Paleocene%E2%80%93Eocene_Thermal_Maximum" class="mw-redirect" title="Paleocene–Eocene Thermal Maximum">Paleocene–Eocene Thermal Maximum</a> is published by Fraser &amp; Lyons (2020).<sup id="cite&#95;ref-358" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-358"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>358<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup></li>\n<li>A study aiming to determine resource and habitat use, niche occupation and trophic interactions of mammals living during the <a href="/wiki/Great_American_Interchange" title="Great American Interchange">Great American Interchange</a>, as indicated by carbon and oxygen stable isotope compositions of <a href="/wiki/Tooth_enamel" title="Tooth enamel">tooth enamel</a> of fossil mammals from the late <a href="/wiki/Miocene" title="Miocene">Miocene</a> to the late <a href="/wiki/Pleistocene" title="Pleistocene">Pleistocene</a> of the Pampean region of <a href="/wiki/Argentina" title="Argentina">Argentina</a>, is published by Domingo <i>et al.</i> (2020).<sup id="cite&#95;ref-359" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-359"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>359<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup></li>\n<li>A study on predator richness in mammalian communities from the Miocene <a href="/wiki/Santa_Cruz_Formation,_Argentina" class="mw-redirect" title="Santa Cruz Formation, Argentina">Santa Cruz Formation</a> (Argentina), aiming to determine whether the mammalian predator guild from this area was impoverished prior to the Great American Interchange, is published by Rodríguez-Gómez <i>et al.</i> (2020).<sup id="cite&#95;ref-360" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-360"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>360<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup></li>\n<li>A study on the causes of the asymmetrical character of the Great American Biotic Interchange, with an increasing dominance of mammals of North American origin in South America during the Pleistocene, is published by Carrillo <i>et al.</i> (2020), who argue that the asymmetry was caused by higher extinction of mammals with South American origin, which in turn reduced the diversity of South American taxa that dispersed into North America.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-361" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-361"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>361<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup></li>\n<li>A study on environmental changes in Southeast Asia from the Early Pleistocene to the Holocene, based on stable isotope data from Southeast Asian mammals, and on their impact on the evolution of mammals (including hominins), is published by Louys &amp; Roberts (2020).<sup id="cite&#95;ref-362" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-362"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>362<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup></li>\n<li>A study on changes of mammalian extinction rates over the past 126,000 years, aiming to determine whether, and to what extent, species extinctions during this time period can be attributed to anthropogenic or to climatic factors, is published by Andermann <i>et al.</i> (2020).<sup id="cite&#95;ref-363" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-363"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>363<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup></li></ul>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="References">References</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span 2026-02-26 13:10:06 | DEBUG    | Scraped content: ScrapedContent(url='https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018–19_Cruz_Azul_season', title='2018–19 Cruz Azul season - Wikipedia', text='From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia Cruz Azul 2018–19 football season Cruz Azul 2018–19 season President Guillermo Álvarez Cuevas Manager Pedro Caixinha Stadium Estadio Azteca Liga MX Apertura : 1st ( Runners-up ) Clausura : 4th ( Quarter-finals ) Copa MX Apertura : Winners Clausura : Group stage Top goalscorer League: Elías Hernández (8) All: Martín Cauteruccio Elías Hernández (11 each) Highest home attendance 71,240 vs América (16 December 2018) Lowest home attendance 4,471 vs León (16 January 2019) Average home league attendance Apertura : 35,958 Clausura : 18,474 Total : 31,587 Home colours Away colours ← 2017–18 2019–20 → The 2018–19 Cruz Azul Fútbol Club season was the 92nd season in the football club\'s history and the 54th consecutive season in the top flight of Mexican football . Cruz Azul competed in Liga MX and Copa MX . Kits [ edit ] Apertura [ edit ] Supplier: Under Armour Home Away Third Clausura [ edit ] Supplier: Joma Home Away Alternate Season overview [ edit ] October [ edit ] On 31 October, Cruz Azul faced Monterrey in the Copa MX final in the Estadio BBVA Bancomer . Cruz Azul won the match 0–2, with goals from Hernández and Cauteruccio, clinching their fourth title. December [ edit ] On 13 December, Cruz Azul played the first leg of the Liga MX final against América which ended as a goalless draw. The second leg was played on 16 December with Cruz Azul losing the match 0–2. This was the first final with both legs played in the same stadium since Verano 2002 . January [ edit ] Cruz Azul\'s four-year association with Under Armour ended with the Apertura 2018 season after being unable to reach an agreement on a new deal. Cruz Azul announced Joma as their new kit manufacturer on 1 January. Aggregate table [ edit ] The aggregate table (the sum of points of both the Apertura and Clausura tournaments) will be used to determine the participants of the Apertura 2019 Copa MX . This table also displays teams that have qualified for the 2020 CONCACAF Champions League . Monterrey">Monterrey</a> in the <a href="/wiki/Apertura_2018_Copa_MX_Final" class="mw-redirect" title="Apertura 2018 Copa MX Final">Copa MX final</a> in the <a href="/wiki/Estadio_BBVA_Bancomer" class="mw-redirect" title="Estadio BBVA Bancomer">Estadio BBVA Bancomer</a>. Cruz Azul won the match 0–2, with goals from Hernández and Cauteruccio, clinching their fourth title.\n</p>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="December">December</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=2018%E2%80%9319_Cruz_Azul_season&amp;action=edit&amp;section=6" title="Edit section: December"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<p>On 13 December, Cruz Azul played the first leg of the Liga MX final against <a href="/wiki/Club_Am%C3%A9rica" title="Club América">América</a> which ended as a goalless draw. The second leg was played on 16 December with Cruz Azul losing the match 0–2. This was the first final with both legs played in the same stadium since <a href="/wiki/Primera_Divisi%C3%B3n_de_M%C3%A9xico_Verano_2002" title="Primera División de México Verano 2002">Verano 2002</a>.\n</p>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="January">January</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=2018%E2%80%9319_Cruz_Azul_season&amp;action=edit&amp;section=7" title="Edit section: January"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<p>Cruz Azul\'s four-year association with <a href="/wiki/Under_Armour" title="Under Armour">Under Armour</a> ended with the Apertura 2018 season after being unable to reach an agreement on a new deal. Cruz Azul announced <a href="/wiki/Joma" title="Joma">Joma</a> as their new kit manufacturer on 1 January.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-1"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Players">Players</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span 2026-02-26 13:10:08 | DEBUG    | Scraped content: ScrapedContent(url='https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shavkat_Rakhmonov', title='Shavkat Rakhmonov - Wikipedia', text='From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia Kazakh mixed martial artist (born 1994) Shavkat Rakhmonov Rakhmonov in 2024 Born Shavkat Bakhtibaevich Rakhmonov [ 1 ] ( 1994-10-23 ) October 23, 1994 (age\xa031) Shoʻrchi , Surxondaryo Region , Uzbekistan Native name Шавкат Бақтыбайұлы Рахмонов [ 2 ] Nickname Nomad Nationality Kazakh Height 6\xa0ft 1\xa0in (185\xa0cm) Weight 170\xa0lb (77\xa0kg; 12\xa0st 2\xa0lb) Division Welterweight Reach 77\xa0in (196\xa0cm) [ 3 ] Fighting out of Kokshetau , Kazakhstan Team DAR Pro Team Kill Cliff FC (2021–present) [ 4 ] [ 5 ] Rank Master of Sport in Combat Sambo [ 4 ] [ 6 ] Master of Sport in MMA [ 6 ] Years active 2014–present Mixed martial arts record Total 19 Wins 19 By\xa0knockout 8 By\xa0submission 10 By\xa0decision 1 Losses 0 Amateur record Total 13 Wins 11 By\xa0knockout 1 By\xa0submission 1 Losses 2 By\xa0decision 2 Other information Mixed martial arts record from Sherdog Shavkat Baqtibaiuly Rakhmonov [ 2 ] [ 1 ] ( Kazakh : Шавкат Бақтыбайұлы Рахмонов , [ʂɑfˈkɑt bɑqtʰɯˈbɑjo̙ɫɯ rɑhˈmonɯf] ; born October 23, 1994) is a Kazakh professional mixed martial artist . He currently competes in the Welterweight division of the Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC). A professional since 2014,\nRakhmonov is also a former M-1 Global Welterweight Champion . Background [ edit ] Rakhmonov was born on October 23, 1994, in the city of Shoʻrchi , Uzbekistan , into a Kazakh family. His father is a Kazakh of the Altynbay clan and his mother is a Kazakh of the Konyrat tribe. Rakhmonov is from the Altynbai clan of Alimuly tribe of the Junior Zhuz . [ 7 ] [ 8 ] Mixed martial arts career [ edit ] Early career [ edit ] As an amateur, Rakhmonov won the WMMAA World and Asian Championships titles. [ 9 ] Rakhmonov\'s professional career began in October 2014, debuting with a first round triangle choke victory against Adam Tsurov at M-1 Challenge 52. He would continue fighting mainly under the M-1 banner, with seven of his professional fights taking place with promotion, with the remaining five wins coming in his home country\'s own MMA organization, Kazakhstan Mixed Martial Arts Federation (KZMMAF). He would alternate back-and-forth between the two organizations, earning his first shot at title as a pro against Faridun Odilov for the KZMMAF welterweight belt. He won the title by third-round TKO. [ 10 ] As an 18-year-old, Rakhmonov became a world champion in amateur MMA for WMMAA (World MMA Association) in 2013. [ 11 ] [ 12 ] In 2014 he became WMMAA\'s Asian MMA champion, [ 13 ] and in the same year he finished as runner-up in WMMAA\'s World Championship to Gadzhimurad Khiramagomedov. [ 14 ] In 2015 Rakhmonov again finished as a runner-up in WMMAA’s World Championship to Khiramagomedov. [ 15 ] Gadzhimurad Khiramagomedov is the only person to defeat Rakhmonov on two occasions while competing in a MMA fight. [ 16 ] [ 17 ] Rakhmonov defended his belt in his next fight at Battle of Nomads 11 against Rinat Sayakbaev in December 2018, returning to M-1 at the start of the new year, facing Daniil Prikaza at M-1 Challenge 101 for the vacant M-1 Welterweight Championship . With a second-round TKO stoppage, the Kazakhstani secured his second belt. [ 18 ] During this period, Rakhmonov received the nickname “Nomad”. [ 19 ] In his last appearance on the regional scene, Rakhmonov defended his M-1 welterweight title with a first-round stoppage of Tiago Varejão at M-1 Challenge 102 . [ 20 ] Ultimate Fighting Championship [ edit ] Rakhmonov was the first Kazakh fighter to sign a contract with the UFC. [ 21 ] Rakhmonov was scheduled to face Bartosz Fabiński on March 21, 2020, at UFC Fight Night: Woodley vs. Edwards . [ 22 ] However, due to the COVID-19 pandemic the event was cancelled. [ 23 ] Rakhmonov was expected to face Ramazan Emeev on July 26, 2020, at UFC on ESPN: Whittaker vs. Till . [ 24 ] However, in early July, it was reported that Rakhmonov was forced to pull out due to injury [ 25 ] and was replaced by Niklas Stolze. [ 26 ] Rakhmonov was scheduled to fight Elizeu Zaleski dos Santos on October 24, 2020, at UFC 254 . [ 27 ] However, Zaleski pulled out due to injury [ 28 ] and was replaced by Alex Oliveira . [ 29 ] At the weigh-ins, Oliveira weighed in at 173 pounds, two pounds over the welterweight non-title fight limit. As a result, the bout proceeded as a catchweight and he was fined 20% of his purse, which went to Rakhmonov. [ 30 ] Rakhmonov won the fight via guillotine choke submission in the first round. [ 31 ] Rakhmonov faced Michel Prazeres at UFC Fight Night: Gane vs. Volkov on June 26, 2021. [ 32 ] He won the bout via rear-naked choke submission in the second round. [ 33 ] Rakhmonov faced Carlston Harris on February 5, 2022, at UFC Fight Night: Hermansson vs. Strickland . [ 34 ] He won the fight via knockout in round one. [ 35 ] This fight earned him the Performance of the Night award. [ 36 ] As the first bout of his new five-fight contract, Rakhmonov faced Neil Magny on June 25, 2022, at UFC on ESPN 38 . [ 37 ] [ 38 ] He won the fight via a guillotine choke submission in the second round. [ 39 ] This win earned him the Performance of the Night bonus award. [ 40 ] Rakhmonov was scheduled to face Geoff Neal on January 14, 2023, at UFC Fight Night: Strickland vs. Imavov . [ 41 ] However, Neal pulled out due to an undisclosed injury. [ 42 ] The pair was rescheduled for UFC 285 on March 4, 2023. [ 43 ] At the weigh-ins, Neal weighed in at 175 pounds, 4 pounds over the non-title fight welterweight limit. As a result, the bout proceeded as a catchweight and Neal was fined 30% of his fight purse, which went to Rakhmonov. [ 44 ] He won the fight via a rear-naked choke submission in the third round. [ 45 ] This fight earned Rakhmonov his first Fight of the Night award. [ 46 ] Rakhmonov was scheduled to face Kelvin Gastelum on September 16, 2023, at UFC Fight Night 227 . [ 47 ] However, Gastelum withdrew in late July after sustaining a facial fracture. [ 48 ] Rakhmonov faced Stephen Thompson on December 16, 2023, at UFC 296 . [ 49 ] He won via a rear-naked choke submission with just four seconds remaining in the second round, making him the first person to ever finish Thompson by submission in his MMA career. [ 50 ] Rakhmonov was scheduled to compete for the UFC Welterweight Championship against current champion Belal Muhammad on December 7, 2024 at UFC 310 . [ 51 ] However, due to a bone infection in his foot, Muhammad was forced to withdraw. [ 52 ] Rakhmonov instead faced Ian Machado Garry in a 5-round title eliminator. [ 53 ] Rakhmonov won the fight by unanimous decision in his first MMA decision victory. [ 54 ] [ 55 ] Due to injury, Rakhmonov was unable to compete for the championship against then champion Belal Muhammad at UFC 315 but stated that he would be offered a title shot later in the year after recovering. [ 56 ] In January 2026, it was reported that Rakhmonov\'s knee injury would keep him out of action for nine-to-ten months. [ 57 ] He was removed from #2 in the rankings as a result of this injury. [ 58 ] Championships and accomplishments [ edit ] World Mixed Martial Arts Association (WMMAA) World Championship Welterweight (2013) [ 59 ] [ 11 ] Asian Championship Welterweight (2014) [ 60 ] [ 11 ] World Championship Welterweight (2014) [ 61 ] World Championship Welterweight (2015) [ 62 ] Ultimate Fighting Championship Performance of the Night (Two times) vs. Carlston Harris and Neil Magny [ 36 ] [ 40 ] Fight of the Night (One time) vs. Geoff Neal [ 46 ] Longest finish streak in UFC Welterweight division history (6) [ 63 ] UFC Honors Awards 2023: President\'s Choice Fight of the Year Nominee vs. Geoff Neal [ 64 ] UFC.com Awards 2023: Ranked #2 Submission of the Year , [ 65 ] Ranked #4 Fight of the Year [ 66 ] & Ranked #10 Upset of the Year [ 67 ] vs. Geoff Neal M-1 Global M-1 Welterweight Championship (One time) [ 4 ] One successful title defense [ 4 ] Kazakhstan Mixed Martial Arts Federation KZMMAF Welterweight Championship (One time) [ 10 ] One successful title defense [ 10 ] MMA Fighting 2023 First Team MMA All-Star [ 68 ] Bleacher Report 2023 #4 Ranked UFC Fight of the Year vs. Geoff Neal at UFC 285 [ 69 ] Personal life [ edit ] Rakhmonov\'s younger sister, Sora Rakhmonova, is also a mixed martial artist. [ 70 ] On July 27th, 2025, Rakhmonov\'s wife and son were involved in a car accident which resulted in the death of two women (friends of his wife). Rakhmonov\'s wife and son were hospitalized following the wreck and later released. [ 71 ] [ 72 ] Rakhmonov is a Muslim . title="Sherdog">Sherdog</a></td></tr></tbody></table>\n<p><b>Shavkat Baqtibaiuly Rakhmonov</b><sup id="cite&#95;ref-azattyqruhy&#95;2-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-azattyqruhy-2"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-fn&#95;1-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-fn-1"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> (<a href="/wiki/Kazakh_language" title="Kazakh language">Kazakh</a>: <span lang="kk">Шавкат Бақтыбайұлы Рахмонов</span>, <span class="IPA nowrap" lang="kk-Latn-fonipa"><a href="/wiki/Help:IPA/Kazakh" title="Help:IPA/Kazakh">&#91;ʂɑfˈkɑt<span class="wrap"> </span>bɑqtʰɯˈbɑjo̙ɫɯ<span class="wrap"> </span>rɑhˈmonɯf&#93;</a></span>; born October 23, 1994) is a Kazakh professional <a href="/wiki/Mixed_martial_arts" title="Mixed martial arts">mixed martial artist</a>. He currently competes in the <a href="/wiki/Welterweight_(MMA)" title="Welterweight (MMA)">Welterweight</a> division of the <a href="/wiki/Ultimate_Fighting_Championship" title="Ultimate Fighting Championship">Ultimate Fighting Championship</a> (UFC). A professional since 2014,\nRakhmonov is also a former <a href="/wiki/M-1_Global#M-1_Global_Welterweight_Championship" title="M-1 Global">M-1 Global Welterweight Champion</a>.\n</p>\n<meta property="mw:PageProp/toc" />\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Background">Background</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Shavkat_Rakhmonov&amp;action=edit&amp;section=1" title="Edit section: Background"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<p>Rakhmonov was born on October 23, 1994, in the city of <a href="/wiki/Sho%CA%BBrchi" title="Shoʻrchi">Shoʻrchi</a>, <a href="/wiki/Uzbekistan" title="Uzbekistan">Uzbekistan</a>, into a <a href="/wiki/Kazakhs" title="Kazakhs">Kazakh</a> family. His father is a Kazakh of the Altynbay clan and his mother is a Kazakh of the <a href="/wiki/Khongirad" title="Khongirad">Konyrat</a> tribe. Rakhmonov is from the Altynbai clan of <a href="/wiki/Zhuz" class="mw-redirect" title="Zhuz">Alimuly tribe</a> of the Junior <a href="/wiki/Zhuz" class="mw-redirect" title="Zhuz">Zhuz</a>.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-7" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-7"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>7<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-sports.kz&#95;8-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-sports.kz-8"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>8<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Mixed_martial_arts_career">Mixed martial arts career</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Shavkat_Rakhmonov&amp;action=edit&amp;section=2" title="Edit section: Mixed martial arts career"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Early_career">Early career</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Shavkat_Rakhmonov&amp;action=edit&amp;section=3" title="Edit section: Early career"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<p>As an amateur, Rakhmonov won the WMMAA World and Asian Championships titles.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-9" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-9"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>9<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>Rakhmonov\'s professional career began in October 2014, debuting with a first round triangle choke victory against Adam Tsurov at M-1 Challenge 52. He would continue fighting mainly under the <a href="/wiki/M-1_Global" title="M-1 Global">M-1</a> banner, with seven of his professional fights taking place with promotion, with the remaining five wins coming in his home country\'s own MMA organization, Kazakhstan Mixed Martial Arts Federation (KZMMAF). He would alternate back-and-forth between the two organizations, earning his first shot at title as a pro against Faridun Odilov for the KZMMAF welterweight belt. He won the title by third-round TKO.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-KZMMAF&#95;10-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-KZMMAF-10"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>10<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>As an 18-year-old, Rakhmonov became a world champion in amateur MMA for WMMAA (World MMA Association) in 2013.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-IMMAF&#95;&#123;&#123;!&#125;&#125;&#95;IMMAF&#95;Alumni&#95;11-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-IMMAF_{{!}}_IMMAF_Alumni-11"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>11<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-12" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-12"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>12<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>In 2014 he became WMMAA\'s Asian MMA champion,<sup id="cite&#95;ref-13" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-13"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>13<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> and in the same year he finished as runner-up in WMMAA\'s World Championship to Gadzhimurad Khiramagomedov.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-14" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-14"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>14<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> In 2015 Rakhmonov again finished as a runner-up in WMMAA’s World Championship to Khiramagomedov.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-15" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-15"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>15<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Gadzhimurad Khiramagomedov is the only person to defeat Rakhmonov on two occasions while competing in a MMA fight.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-16" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-16"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>16<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-17" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-17"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>17<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>Rakhmonov defended his belt in his next fight at Battle of Nomads 11 against Rinat Sayakbaev in December 2018, returning to M-1 at the start of the new year, facing Daniil Prikaza at <a href="/wiki/2019_in_M-1_Global#M-1_Challenge_101_-_Prikaza_vs._Rakhmonov" title="2019 in M-1 Global">M-1 Challenge 101</a> for the vacant <a href="/wiki/M-1_Global#M-1_Global_Welterweight_Championship" title="M-1 Global">M-1 Welterweight Championship</a>. With a second-round TKO stoppage, the Kazakhstani secured his second belt.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-18" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-18"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>18<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> During this period, Rakhmonov received the nickname “Nomad”.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-19" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-19"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>19<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>In his last appearance on the regional scene, Rakhmonov defended his M-1 welterweight title with a first-round stoppage of Tiago Varejão at <a href="/wiki/2019_in_M-1_Global#M-1_Challenge_102_-_Rakhmonov_vs._Lacerda" title="2019 in M-1 Global">M-1 Challenge 102</a>.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-20" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-20"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>20<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Ultimate_Fighting_Championship">Ultimate Fighting Championship</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Shavkat_Rakhmonov&amp;action=edit&amp;section=4" title="Edit section: Ultimate Fighting Championship"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<p>Rakhmonov was the first Kazakh fighter to sign a contract with the UFC.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-21" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-21"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>21<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Rakhmonov was scheduled to face <a href="/wiki/Bartosz_Fabi%C5%84ski" title="Bartosz Fabiński">Bartosz Fabiński</a> on March 21, 2020, at <a href="/wiki/UFC_Fight_Night:_Woodley_vs._Edwards" title="UFC Fight Night: Woodley vs. Edwards">UFC Fight Night: Woodley vs. Edwards</a>.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-22" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-22"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>22<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> However, due to the <a href="/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic" title="COVID-19 pandemic">COVID-19 pandemic</a> the event was cancelled.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-23" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-23"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>23<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>Rakhmonov was expected to face <a href="/wiki/Ramazan_Emeev" title="Ramazan Emeev">Ramazan Emeev</a> on July 26, 2020, at <a href="/wiki/UFC_on_ESPN:_Whittaker_vs._Till" title="UFC on ESPN: Whittaker vs. Till">UFC on ESPN: Whittaker vs. Till</a>.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-24" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-24"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>24<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> However, in early July, it was reported that Rakhmonov was forced to pull out due to injury<sup id="cite&#95;ref-25" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-25"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>25<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> and was replaced by Niklas Stolze.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-26" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-26"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>26<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>Rakhmonov was scheduled to fight <a href="/wiki/Elizeu_Zaleski_dos_Santos" title="Elizeu Zaleski dos Santos">Elizeu Zaleski dos Santos</a> on October 24, 2020, at <a href="/wiki/UFC_254" title="UFC 254">UFC 254</a>.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-27" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-27"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>27<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> However, Zaleski pulled out due to injury<sup id="cite&#95;ref-28" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-28"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>28<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> and was replaced by <a href="/wiki/Alex_Oliveira" title="Alex Oliveira">Alex Oliveira</a>.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-29" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-29"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>29<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> At the weigh-ins, Oliveira weighed in at 173 pounds, two pounds over the welterweight non-title fight limit. As a result, the bout proceeded as a catchweight and he was fined 20% of his purse, which went to Rakhmonov.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-30" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-30"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>30<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Rakhmonov won the fight via guillotine choke submission in the first round.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-31" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-31"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>31<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>Rakhmonov faced <a href="/wiki/Michel_Prazeres" title="Michel Prazeres">Michel Prazeres</a> at <a href="/wiki/UFC_Fight_Night:_Gane_vs._Volkov" title="UFC Fight Night: Gane vs. Volkov">UFC Fight Night: Gane vs. Volkov</a> on June 26, 2021.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-32" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-32"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>32<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> He won the bout via rear-naked choke submission in the second round.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-33" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-33"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>33<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>Rakhmonov faced <a href="/wiki/Carlston_Harris" title="Carlston Harris">Carlston Harris</a> on February 5, 2022, at <a href="/wiki/UFC_Fight_Night:_Hermansson_vs._Strickland" title="UFC Fight Night: Hermansson vs. Strickland">UFC Fight Night: Hermansson vs. Strickland</a>.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-34" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-34"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>34<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> He won the fight via knockout in round one.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-35" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-35"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>35<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> This fight earned him the <a href="/wiki/List_of_UFC_bonus_award_recipients" title="List of UFC bonus award recipients">Performance of the Night</a> award.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-UFN200&#95;36-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-UFN200-36"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>36<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>As the first bout of his new five-fight contract, Rakhmonov faced <a href="/wiki/Neil_Magny" title="Neil Magny">Neil Magny</a> on June 25, 2022, at <a href="/wiki/UFC_on_ESPN_38" class="mw-redirect" title="UFC on ESPN 38">UFC on ESPN 38</a>.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-37" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-37"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>37<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-38" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-38"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>38<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> He won the fight via a guillotine choke submission in the second round.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-39" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-39"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>39<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> This win earned him the <i><a href="/wiki/Performance_of_the_Night" class="mw-redirect" title="Performance of the Night">Performance of the Night</a></i> bonus award.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-UFCESPN38&#95;40-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-UFCESPN38-40"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>40<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>Rakhmonov was scheduled to face <a href="/wiki/Geoff_Neal" title="Geoff Neal">Geoff Neal</a> on January 14, 2023, at <a href="/wiki/UFC_Fight_Night:_Strickland_vs._Imavov" title="UFC Fight Night: Strickland vs. Imavov">UFC Fight Night: Strickland vs. Imavov</a>.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-41" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-41"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>41<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> However, Neal pulled out due to an undisclosed injury.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-42" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-42"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>42<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> The pair was rescheduled for <a href="/wiki/UFC_285" title="UFC 285">UFC 285</a> on March 4, 2023.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-43" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-43"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>43<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> At the weigh-ins, Neal weighed in at 175 pounds, 4 pounds over the non-title fight welterweight limit. As a result, the bout proceeded as a <a href="/wiki/Catchweight" title="Catchweight">catchweight</a> and Neal was fined 30% of his fight purse, which went to Rakhmonov.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-44" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-44"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>44<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> He won the fight via a rear-naked choke submission in the third round.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-45" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-45"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>45<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> This fight earned Rakhmonov his first <i><a href="/wiki/List_of_UFC_bonus_award_recipients" title="List of UFC bonus award recipients">Fight of the Night</a></i> award.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-UFC285&#95;46-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-UFC285-46"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>46<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>Rakhmonov was scheduled to face <a href="/wiki/Kelvin_Gastelum" title="Kelvin Gastelum">Kelvin Gastelum</a> on September 16, 2023, at <a href="/wiki/UFC_Fight_Night_227" class="mw-redirect" title="UFC Fight Night 227">UFC Fight Night 227</a>.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-47" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-47"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>47<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> However, Gastelum withdrew in late July after sustaining a facial fracture.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-Gastelum&#95;out&#95;48-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Gastelum_out-48"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>48<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>Rakhmonov faced <a href="/wiki/Stephen_Thompson_(fighter)" title="Stephen Thompson (fighter)">Stephen Thompson</a> on December 16, 2023, at <a href="/wiki/UFC_296" title="UFC 296">UFC 296</a>.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-Wonderboy&#95;vs.&#95;Shavkat&#95;49-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Wonderboy_vs._Shavkat-49"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>49<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> He won via a rear-naked choke submission with just four seconds remaining in the second round, making him the first person to ever finish Thompson by submission in his MMA career.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-50" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-50"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>50<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>Rakhmonov was scheduled to compete for the <a href="/wiki/UFC_Welterweight_Championship" class="mw-redirect" title="UFC Welterweight Championship">UFC Welterweight Championship</a> against current champion <a href="/wiki/Belal_Muhammad" title="Belal Muhammad">Belal Muhammad</a> on December 7, 2024 at <a href="/wiki/UFC_310" title="UFC 310">UFC 310</a>.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-51" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-51"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>51<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> However, due to a bone infection in his foot, Muhammad was forced to withdraw.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-52" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-52"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>52<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Rakhmonov instead faced <a href="/wiki/Ian_Machado_Garry" title="Ian Machado Garry">Ian Machado Garry</a> in a 5-round title eliminator.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-53" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-53"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>53<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Rakhmonov won the fight by unanimous decision in his first MMA decision victory.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-54" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-54"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>54<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-55" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-55"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>55<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>Due to injury, Rakhmonov was unable to compete for the championship against then champion <a href="/wiki/Belal_Muhammad" title="Belal Muhammad">Belal Muhammad</a> at <a href="/wiki/UFC_315" title="UFC 315">UFC 315</a> but stated that he would be offered a title shot later in the year after recovering.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-56" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-56"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>56<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> In January 2026, it was reported that Rakhmonov\'s knee injury would keep him out of action for nine-to-ten months.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-57" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-57"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>57<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> He was removed from #2 in the rankings as a result of this injury.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-58" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-58"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>58<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p>\n<div class="mw-heading class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-69"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>69<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup></li></ul></li></ul>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Personal_life">Personal life</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Shavkat_Rakhmonov&amp;action=edit&amp;section=6" title="Edit section: Personal life"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<p>Rakhmonov\'s younger sister, Sora Rakhmonova, is also a mixed martial artist.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-70" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-70"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>70<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> \n</p><p>On July 27th, 2025, Rakhmonov\'s wife and son were involved in a car accident which resulted in the death of two women (friends of his wife). 2026-02-26 13:10:08 | DEBUG    | Scraped content: ScrapedContent(url='https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devon_Alexander', title='Devon Alexander - Wikipedia', text='From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia American boxer (born 1987) Devon Alexander Alexander (right) vs. DeMarcus Corley , 2008 Personal information Nickname The Great Born Devon Eugene Alexander ( 1987-02-10 ) February 10, 1987 (age\xa039) St. Louis, Missouri , U.S. Height 5\xa0ft 8 + 1 ⁄ 2 in (174\xa0cm) Weight Light welterweight Welterweight Boxing career Reach 69\xa0in (175\xa0cm) Stance Southpaw Boxing record Total\xa0fights 37 Wins 27 Win\xa0by\xa0KO 14 Losses 9 Draws 1 Devon Alexander (born February 10, 1987) is an American professional boxer . He has held world championships in two weight divisions , including the unified World Boxing Council (WBC) and International Boxing Federation (IBF) light welterweight titles and the IBF welterweight title. Biography [ edit ] Alexander grew up in the Hyde Park neighborhood of north St. Louis, Missouri in an area described as rough, gang- and drug-infested. [ 1 ] Alexander was mentored by various people at a young age including Former NFL players Eric Drain and Demetrius Johnson , principal of Clay Community Education Center Frank Muelhauser, and PE teacher, Brad Slinkard.  He would later join the boxing gym that Kevin Cunningham , a former police officer and security officer at Clay Community Center, turned trainer, founded in the basement of an old police station. [ 2 ] Thirty kids joined the boxing program of Cunningham, who had hoped to keep the kids out of trouble, off the streets, and in the ring. A stablemate of Alexander\'s, Cory Spinks would become welterweight champion. [ 3 ] Amateur career [ edit ] Alexander had an outstanding amateur career, compiling a record of 300-10 under the tutelage of Cunningham. He was a four-time Silver Gloves champion from ages 10–14; three-time PAL national champion; Junior Golden Gloves and Junior Olympics national champion; 2003 United States national champion in the 19-and-under division; and 2004 United States light welterweight national champion . Alexander made it to the final round of the 2004 Olympic trials, where he battled Rock Allen to a draw and was knocked down once before losing on a tie-breaker. [ 4 ] Professional career [ edit ] Light welterweight [ edit ] At age 17, Alexander made his professional debut, defeating Vincent Torres by first round technical knockout in Sault Sainte Marie, Michigan . [ 4 ] He went up against former WBO junior welterweight champion DeMarcus Corley on January 19, 2008, at Madison Square Garden in New York City . Alexander easily defeated Corley by unanimous decision. [ 5 ] Light welterweight title [ edit ] On August 1, 2009, Alexander defeated Junior Witter to claim the vacant WBC light welterweight championship. Witter gave up on his stool after the eighth round, claiming that he had re-injured his left hand. Alexander was hurt by a right hand in round 2. All three judges had Alexander ahead at the time of the stoppage 79-73, 79-73, 80-72. Alexander vs. Urango [ edit ] Alexander was next scheduled to face two-time champion Juan Urango of Colombia in a title unification bout. The 6 March 2010 bout was held at the Mohegan Sun in Uncasville, Connecticut and was televised on HBO \'s "Boxing After Dark" telecast. [ 2 ] To train for the fight, Alexander used a Las Vegas house lent by promoter Don King as training base. [ 3 ] Devon Alexander defeated Juan Urango by TKO in round 8.\nAlexander threw an uppercut which dropped Urango. Urango made the count but Alexander resumed his attack and threw a hook to Urango\'s temple which again dropped him. Urango stood up but was clearly dazed, resulting in a stoppage by the referee. Urango, who suffered his first KO defeat, called out Timothy Bradley after the fight, but a fight was never made because Bradley just moved up to welterweight. In his next fight he faced Andreas Kotelnik , the former WBA Light Welterweight champion, in his hometown of St. Louis Missouri on 7 August in front of members of the St. Louis Rams , Evander Holyfield and Floyd Mayweather . [ 6 ] Alexander won the fight by a controversial unanimous decision with all judges scoring the fight 116-112. On October 22, 2010, Alexander was stripped of the IBF Junior Welterweight title for not fighting the no. 1 contender, Kaizer Mabuza . Alexander vs. Bradley [ edit ] Main article: Timothy Bradley vs. Devon Alexander Alexander\'s next fight, on January 29, 2011, took place against Timothy Bradley , which he lost via 10th round TD after an unintentional head-butt forced a stop to the bout. [ 7 ] Alexander vs. Matthysse [ edit ] Main article: Devon Alexander vs. Lucas Matthysse On June 25, 2011, Alexander defeated Lucas Matthysse in a controversial split decision. The judges scored the fight 96-93 and 95-94 for Alexander and 96-93 for Matthysse. Welterweight [ edit ] Main article: Devon Alexander vs. Marcos Maidana On February 25, 2012 Alexander moved up to welterweight and put on a dominating performance against highly regarded and hard-charging Marcos Maidana . Alexander landed the right hook at will, catching Maidana with his left hand down throughout the contest. Maidana was seemingly surprised by both the speed and power Alexander displayed at his first fight at welterweight. Only one of the three judges had Maidana winning a round. The impressive nature of the win earned Alexander a title match with Randall Bailey in September 2012. Alexander was criticized by some however, for fighting illegally at some points during the fight. Alexander was scheduled to fight titlest Randall Bailey as a main event on Showtime Championship Boxing on September 8, 2012, but Bailey withdrew due to injury. Their fight was replaced with the original undercard fight between Olusegun Ajose and Lucas Matthysse and an originally scheduled non-televised fight between J\'Leon Love and Ramon Valenzuela was changed to a televised bout. [ 8 ] Welterweight title [ edit ] Alexander returned to action on October 20, 2012, at the Barclays Center in Brooklyn , where he won the IBF Welterweight title by unanimous decision against Ring Top 10 Welterweight, Randall Bailey . The fight was fought at a comfortable pace for Alexander, with very little exchanges, as Bailey did not let his hands go very often. In a one sided fight, Alexander won his third world title in his second division. Alexander\'s next fight was originally supposed to happen on January 19, 2013, against mandatory challenger and Ring No. 3 ranked Welterweight, Kell Brook . However, Brook suffered an ankle injury during training, and the fight was rescheduled for May 18, 2013 in Atlantic City. Alexander\'s camp and some boxing insiders have questioned the authenticity of this injury and assert that Brook was simply not ready to step up in class to fight Alexander. Devon would go on to lose his next two biggest fights, losing his championship belt & status as a top contender after all boxing governing bodies removed Devon Alexander from their Top rankings. [ 9 ] Shawn Porter loss [ edit ] Alexander would lose the IBF Welterweight title to Shawn Porter on December 7, 2013 by unanimous decision with scores of 115-113, 116-112 and 116-112. [ 10 ] Brook later defeated Shawn Porter for the less than sparkling IBF Welterweight belt - somewhat clearing Brook of possibly ducking Alexander. Amir Khan loss [ edit ] Alexander lost  the WBC Silver Welterweight title to Amir Khan on December 13, 2014 by a lopsided unanimous decision with scores of 119-109, 118-110, 120-108. [ 11 ] Personal life [ edit ] Devon Alexander is married to his high school sweetheart Cesily Alexander having six children together. id="mw-content-subtitle"></div></div>\n\t\t\t\t\t\n\t\t\t\t\t\n\t\t\t\t\t<div id="mw-content-text" class="mw-body-content"><div class="mw-subjectpageheader">\n</div><div class="mw-content-ltr mw-parser-output" lang="en" dir="ltr"><div class="shortdescription nomobile noexcerpt noprint searchaux" style="display:none">American boxer (born 1987)</div>\n<style
