class="infobox-label">Draws</th><td class="infobox-data">2</td></tr><tr style="display:none"><td colspan="2">\n</td></tr></tbody></table>\n<p><b>Nobuhiro Ishida</b><span style="font-weight: normal"> (<span title="Japanese-language text"><span lang="ja">石田 順裕</span></span>, <span title="Hepburn transliteration"><i lang="ja-Latn">Ishida Nobuhiro</i></span>; born August 18, 1975)</span> is a Japanese former professional boxer. He is a former <a href="/wiki/World_Boxing_Association" title="World Boxing Association">WBA</a> <a href="/wiki/Interim_championship" title="Interim championship">interim</a> <a href="/wiki/Super_welterweight" class="mw-redirect" title="Super welterweight">super welterweight</a> champion who is best known for knocking out <a href="/wiki/James_Kirkland_(boxer)" title="James Kirkland (boxer)">James Kirkland</a> in a <a href="/wiki/Middleweight" title="Middleweight">middleweight</a> bout at the <a href="/wiki/MGM_Grand_Las_Vegas" title="MGM Grand Las Vegas">MGM Grand Las Vegas</a> in April 2011.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-espn20110410&#95;2-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-espn20110410-2"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Ishida has so far been promoted by Canelo Promotions and <a href="/wiki/Golden_Boy_Promotions" title="Golden Boy Promotions">Golden Boy Promotions</a> among others<sup id="cite&#95;ref-espn20110516&#95;3-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-espn20110516-3"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>3<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> and has been co-trained by Rudy Hernández and Daisuke Okabe,<sup id="cite&#95;ref-ringtv20110407&#95;4-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-ringtv20110407-4"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>4<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> while residing back and forth between <a href="/wiki/Los_Angeles" title="Los Angeles">Los Angeles</a>, <a href="/wiki/California" title="California">California</a>, <a href="/wiki/United_States" title="United States">United States</a> and <a href="/wiki/Osaka" title="Osaka">Osaka</a>, Japan.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-miyata&#95;5-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-miyata-5"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>5<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p>\n<meta property="mw:PageProp/toc" />\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Early_life_and_amateur_career">Early life and amateur career</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Nobuhiro_Ishida&amp;action=edit&amp;section=1" title="Edit section: Early life and amateur career"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<p>Ishida was born in <a href="/wiki/Tamana_District,_Kumamoto" title="Tamana District, Kumamoto">Tamana District, Kumamoto</a> and moved to <a href="/wiki/Neyagawa,_Osaka" title="Neyagawa, Osaka">Neyagawa, Osaka</a> soon after. He began boxing at the <a href="/wiki/Teiken_Boxing_Gym" title="Teiken Boxing Gym">Osaka Teiken Boxing Gym</a> at the sixth grade of elementary school (at age eleven).<sup id="cite&#95;ref-6" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-6"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>6<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-sponichi20090831&#95;7-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-sponichi20090831-7"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>7<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-FOOTNOTEGoodman2006478&#95;8-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGoodman2006478-8"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>8<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> When Ishida was a high school freshman, he fought as an in-fighter in the <a href="/wiki/Flyweight" title="Flyweight">flyweight</a> division at 176 centimeters (5 feet 10 inches) tall.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-daily200908&#95;9-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-daily200908-9"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>9<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-FOOTNOTEGoodman2006478&#95;8-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGoodman2006478-8"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>8<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> He won the national high school invitational tournament in the <a href="/wiki/Lightweight" title="Lightweight">lightweight</a> division in 1993.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-FOOTNOTEBaseball&#95;Magazine&#95;Sha2005207&#95;10-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBaseball_Magazine_Sha2005207-10"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>10<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>After graduating from <a href="/wiki/Kinki_University" class="mw-redirect" title="Kinki University">Kinki University</a>, Ishida won another amateur title in the <a href="/wiki/Light_middleweight" title="Light middleweight">light middleweight</a> in 1998.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-FOOTNOTEBaseball&#95;Magazine&#95;Sha2005206&#95;11-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBaseball_Magazine_Sha2005206-11"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>11<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> He compiled an amateur record of 101–15 (50 KOs).<sup id="cite&#95;ref-FOOTNOTEBaseball&#95;Magazine&#95;Sha2004132&#95;12-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBaseball_Magazine_Sha2004132-12"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>12<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Ishida worked for the <a href="/wiki/Child_protection" title="Child protection">child welfare</a> for two years and two months from August 1998. He paused his boxing career to pursue studies, and qualified as a <a href="/wiki/Welfare_spending" title="Welfare spending">social welfare</a> secretary.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-sponichi20090823&#95;13-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-sponichi20090823-13"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>13<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-boxon20090822&#95;14-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-boxon20090822-14"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>14<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Ishida worked at an <a href="/wiki/Orphanage" title="Orphanage">orphanage</a>. His experience of living with the orphans motivated him to turn professional.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-FOOTNOTEGoodman2006487&amp;ndash;488&#95;15-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGoodman2006487&amp;ndash;488-15"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>15<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Professional_career">Professional career</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Nobuhiro_Ishida&amp;action=edit&amp;section=2" title="Edit section: Professional career"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Super_Welterweight">Super Welterweight</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Nobuhiro_Ishida&amp;action=edit&amp;section=3" title="Edit section: Super Welterweight"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<p>Ishida restarted his boxing career in 2000. He made his professional debut on May 20 of that year under the management of Kanazawa Boxing Gym.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-FOOTNOTEBaseball&#95;Magazine&#95;Sha200171&#95;16-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBaseball_Magazine_Sha200171-16"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>16<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> There he received Toshihiro Fujitani\'s guidance<sup id="cite&#95;ref-sponichi20090831&#95;7-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-sponichi20090831-7"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>7<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> until the end of 2010. Ishida won the <a href="/wiki/Oriental_and_Pacific_Boxing_Federation" title="Oriental and Pacific Boxing Federation">OPBF</a> <a href="/wiki/Super_welterweight" class="mw-redirect" title="Super welterweight">super welterweight</a> title via a <a href="/wiki/Technical_decision" title="Technical decision">technical decision</a> on March 1, 2001. The bout was stopped in the eleventh round as Ishida\'s right eye was injured after the accidental <a href="/wiki/Headbutt" title="Headbutt">headbutt</a>. He managed to get his first title in his sixth match. He lost the unification match against the OPBF <a href="/wiki/Interim_championship" title="Interim championship">interim</a> champion by a twelve-round <a href="/wiki/Unanimous_decision" title="Unanimous decision">unanimous decision</a> on May 13, 2001. That was his first loss in his professional career. Ishida lost the Japanese super welterweight title shot in his next fight on September 24 of that year by a ten-round <a href="/wiki/Majority_decision" title="Majority decision">majority decision</a>. In June and October, 2002, Ishida fought for the OPBF and interim Japanese title respectively in the same weight division, but lost two in a row.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-miyata&#95;5-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-miyata-5"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>5<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>At that time, Ishida trained in Los Angeles for the first time to get out of the slump. He watched the boxing matches in <a href="/wiki/Las_Vegas_Valley" title="Las Vegas Valley">Las Vegas</a> and felt that he would like to someday fight there.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-miyata&#95;5-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-miyata-5"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>5<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Loren_Goodman" title="Loren Goodman">Loren Goodman</a> noted the words of Ishida in his book published in 2006.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-FOOTNOTEGoodman2006479&#95;17-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGoodman2006479-17"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>17<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p>\n<style data-mw-deduplicate="TemplateStyles:r1244412712">.mw-parser-output .templatequote{overflow:hidden;margin:1em 0;padding:0 32px}.mw-parser-output .templatequotecite{line-height:1.5em;text-align:left;margin-top:0}@media(min-width:500px){.mw-parser-output .templatequotecite{padding-left:1.6em}}</style><blockquote class="templatequote"><p>...I went to L.A. at first...but the atmosphere of the gym was really good. L.A. Gym. It was like, "I\'ve come to the Mecca of boxing." It felt really good, and the atmosphere of the gym was good. At first, I went for about a month. America was fun&#8212;it was...fun.</p></blockquote><div class="templatequotecite"><p style="display: inline; padding-left: 2.3em;">—&#8202;Loren Goodman, Endless Punchers: Body, Narrative, and Performance in the World of Japanese Boxing<sup id="cite&#95;ref-FOOTNOTEGoodman2006479&#95;17-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGoodman2006479-17"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>17<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><span style="display:none" data-plural="1"></span></p></div>\n<p>Ishida married on Christmas Day, 2003.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-18" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-18"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>18<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> His wife has worked as a <a href="/wiki/Clinical_psychology" title="Clinical psychology">clinical psychologist</a>.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-19" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-19"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>19<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-hochi20091230&#95;20-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-hochi20091230-20"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>20<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-21" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-21"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>21<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> They have one daughter and two sons.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-hochi20091230&#95;20-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-hochi20091230-20"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>20<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-22" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-22"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>22<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Ishida captured the vacant Japanese super welterweight title on December 2, 2006, and defended the title twice before vacating it. He has often trained under the guidance of Rudy Hernández at the Maywood Boxing Club in <a href="/wiki/Maywood,_California" title="Maywood, California">Maywood, California</a>.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-ringtv20110407&#95;4-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-ringtv20110407-4"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>4<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-23" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-23"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>23<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-24" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-24"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>24<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> When Ishida who used to be a in-fighter outpointed the <a href="/wiki/World_Boxing_Association" title="World Boxing Association">WBA</a> number six and <a href="/wiki/World_Boxing_Council" title="World Boxing Council">WBC</a> number seven ranked Javier Alberto Mamaní with scores of 100–91, 100–91, 98–94 in October 2007, he had turned into a good defensive<sup id="cite&#95;ref-miyata&#95;5-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-miyata-5"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>5<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> out-fighter controlling the fight with his left jabs and forehand blows.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-25" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-25"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>25<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading4"><h4 id="Interim_WBA_World_title">Interim WBA World title</h4><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Nobuhiro_Ishida&amp;action=edit&amp;section=4" title="Edit section: Interim WBA World title"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<p>Ishida won the WBA super welterweight title eliminator over <a href="/wiki/Venezuelan_people" class="mw-redirect" title="Venezuelan people">Venezuelan</a> Marco Antonio Avendaño via a <a href="/wiki/Split_decision" title="Split decision">split decision</a> at the <a href="/wiki/Osaka_Prefectural_Gymnasium" title="Osaka Prefectural Gymnasium">Osaka Prefectural Gymnasium</a> on September 22, 2008. He had decided to be a bullfighter for that fight.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-daily200908&#95;9-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-daily200908-9"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>9<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> However, the world title shot against the regular champion <a href="/wiki/Daniel_Santos_(boxer)" title="Daniel Santos (boxer)">Daniel Santos</a> did not materialize.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-jiji20101109-2&#95;26-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-jiji20101109-2-26"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>26<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Ishida won the interim WBA world super welterweight title over Avendaño via a wide margin unanimous decision in front of spectators including one hundred children and staff whom he invited from the orphanage where he had worked before his professional debut,<sup id="cite&#95;ref-sponichi20090823&#95;13-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-sponichi20090823-13"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>13<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-boxon20090822&#95;14-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-boxon20090822-14"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>14<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> at the Osaka Prefectural Gymnasium on August 30, 2009.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-27" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-27"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>27<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> In order to make that matchup, his manager Kanazawa mortgaged building which served as the gym and his home.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-28" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-28"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>28<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> The purse was not paid to Ishida.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-zakzak2011&#95;29-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-zakzak2011-29"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>29<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Although it was an interim title, no Japanese boxers have regained the world super welterweight title since <a href="/wiki/Tadashi_Mihara" title="Tadashi Mihara">Tadashi Mihara</a> was dethroned in February 1982. Yet, on that day, the <a href="/wiki/2009_Japanese_general_election" title="2009 Japanese general election">general election</a> where the historical change of government occurred was made in Japan, so Ishida\'s fight was broadcast only on a pay TV channel, sky-A sports+.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-hochi20091230&#95;20-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-hochi20091230-20"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>20<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Santos lost the title to <a href="/wiki/Yuri_Foreman" title="Yuri Foreman">Yuri Foreman</a> in November 2009. Ishida was eager to fight in a unification match against Foreman, saying that he would go anywhere in the world for it and was confident to win it with his own fighting style and with a way which he most want to show to the audience.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-hochi20091230&#95;20-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-hochi20091230-20"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>20<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-30" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-30"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>30<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> But Foreman lost the title in his first defense against <a href="/wiki/Miguel_Cotto" title="Miguel Cotto">Miguel Cotto</a> in June 2010, and Ishida\'s matchup against Cotto did not happen.\n</p><p>In the first defense of the interim title on December 29, 2009, Ishida defeated <a href="/wiki/Colombian_people" class="mw-redirect" title="Colombian people">Colombian</a> Oney Valdéz by a unanimous decision after knocking him down in the tenth round<sup id="cite&#95;ref-31" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-31"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>31<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> on the undercard of <a href="/wiki/Kazuto_Ioka" title="Kazuto Ioka">Kazuto Ioka</a>\'s non-title <a href="/wiki/Light_flyweight" title="Light flyweight">light flyweight</a> ten round bout at the Osaka Prefectural Gymnasium.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-32" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-32"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>32<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> While he had been negotiating to fight against <a href="/wiki/Rigoberto_%C3%81lvarez" title="Rigoberto Álvarez">Rigoberto Álvarez</a>, <a href="/wiki/Austin_Trout" title="Austin Trout">Austin Trout</a> arbitrarily released the fight against Ishida in the United States in late August 2010.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-jiji20101109-2&#95;26-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-jiji20101109-2-26"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>26<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-33" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-33"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>33<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> So the negotiations for the fight between Ishida and Álvarez were halted. When the WBA upgraded Cotto to the status of a <a href="/wiki/Undisputed_championship_(boxing)" title="Undisputed championship (boxing)">super champion</a> in September of that year, Ishida was not automatically promoted to a regular champion. The WBA instructed Ishida and Trout to compete for the vacant WBA regular title. Ishida and Trout were supposed to bid for the match at the WBA headquarters on September 21, but both sides did not participate in it, so the bid was not met. After more twists and turns, the WBA decided Álvarez as Ishida\'s opponent for the vacant WBA world title, and announced it on their official website in late September.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-jiji20101109-2&#95;26-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-jiji20101109-2-26"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>26<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>Ishida fought against Rigoberto Álvarez for the vacant WBA world super welterweight championship as his first expedition match in <a href="/wiki/Tepic" title="Tepic">Tepic</a>, <a href="/wiki/Nayarit" title="Nayarit">Nayarit</a>, <a href="/wiki/Mexico" title="Mexico">Mexico</a> on October 9, 2010,<sup id="cite&#95;ref-34" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-34"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>34<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> and lost there.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-35" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-35"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>35<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-37" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-37"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>* 1<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> It was after several hours of the fight that Ishida was informed that the result was a narrow split decision with scores of 112–115, 113–114 and 114–113. Ishida does not think that he lost the fight,<sup id="cite&#95;ref-jiji20101109-3&#95;38-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-jiji20101109-3-38"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>37<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> partially because of the controversial knock down call against Ishida in the seventh round which appeared to have been a slip,<sup id="cite&#95;ref-ringtv20110407&#95;4-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-ringtv20110407-4"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>4<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-39" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-39"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>38<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-jiji20101109-1&#95;40-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-jiji20101109-1-40"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>39<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> but he did not protest the decision.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-jiji20101109-1&#95;40-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-jiji20101109-1-40"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>39<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> In the WBA official ratings published on October 15, Álvarez was designated as an interim champion, Ishida was ranked number four, and the regular champion remained vacant.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-jiji20101109-2&#95;26-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-jiji20101109-2-26"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>26<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> The JBC (Japan Boxing Commission) immediately asked the WBA about the title of that fight. Instead of a reply, the WBA posted an article where they released the championship for the vacant regular title between Álvarez and Trout in December on their official website.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-jiji20101109-3&#95;38-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-jiji20101109-3-38"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>37<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> As the WBA ordered, Ishida vs. Álvarez was held as a regular championship by the promoter.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-jiji20101109-2&#95;26-4" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-jiji20101109-2-26"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>26<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Ishida, Álvarez, <a href="/wiki/Televisa" title="Televisa">Televisa</a> which aired that fight and the media in many countries had recognized that they fought for the world title. Nevertheless, after all, it was positioned as per the WBA official ratings as a defense of the interim title which Ishida had held.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-jiji20101109-3&#95;38-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-jiji20101109-3-38"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>37<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>After that defeat, Ishida\'s team had to change his fighting style yet again,<sup id="cite&#95;ref-miyata&#95;5-4" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-miyata-5"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>5<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> especially because once he decided to fight outside of his own country.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-41" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-41"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>40<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Ishida signed a management contract with Japan\'s Green-Tsuda Boxing Club<sup id="cite&#95;ref-42" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-42"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>41<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-44" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-44"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>* 2<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> and a three-fight<sup id="cite&#95;ref-45" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-45"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>43<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> promotional contract with Mexico\'s Canelo Promotions under the supervision of Edison Reynoso<sup id="cite&#95;ref-notifight20110409&#95;46-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-notifight20110409-46"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>44<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> who handled the previous fight.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-47" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-47"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>45<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Middleweight">Middleweight</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Nobuhiro_Ishida&amp;action=edit&amp;section=5" title="Edit section: Middleweight"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading4"><h4 id="Ishida_vs._Kirkland">Ishida vs. Kirkland</h4><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Nobuhiro_Ishida&amp;action=edit&amp;section=6" title="Edit section: Ishida vs. Kirkland"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<p>Ishida moved up in weight division to knock out the previously undefeated <a href="/wiki/James_Kirkland_(boxer)" title="James Kirkland (boxer)">James Kirkland</a> whose record was 27–0 (24 KOs), flooring him three times in one minute and fifty-two seconds of the first round in an eight-round <a href="/wiki/Middleweight" title="Middleweight">middleweight</a> bout on the <a href="/wiki/HBO" title="HBO">HBO</a> <a href="/wiki/Pay-per-view" title="Pay-per-view">pay-per-view</a> televised undercard of <a href="/wiki/Erik_Morales_vs._Marcos_Maidana" title="Erik Morales vs. Marcos Maidana">Erik Morales vs. Marcos Maidana</a> at the <a href="/wiki/MGM_Grand_Las_Vegas" title="MGM Grand Las Vegas">MGM Grand Las Vegas</a> on April 9, 2011,<sup id="cite&#95;ref-48" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-48"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>Video 1<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-49" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-49"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>Video 2<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> in less than a month after the <a href="/wiki/2011_T%C5%8Dhoku_earthquake_and_tsunami" title="2011 Tōhoku earthquake and tsunami">Tōhoku earthquake</a>.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-espn20110410&#95;2-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-espn20110410-2"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Nori Takatani (who was the manager of <a href="/wiki/Genaro_Hern%C3%A1ndez" title="Genaro Hernández">Genaro Hernández</a>,<sup id="cite&#95;ref-50" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-50"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>46<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-51" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-51"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>47<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Oscar Albarado<sup id="cite&#95;ref-52" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-52"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>48<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> and others), Rudy Hernández, Daisuke Okabe and Hidenobu Honda from Green-Tsuda (who was the Japanese champion and two-time world title challenger) were in Ishida\'s corner.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-53" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-53"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>49<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> The fight was released just about two weeks before the fight.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-54" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-54"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>50<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> During the short preparation time, Ishida trained in Las Vegas and California, including sparring with big boxers such as <a href="/wiki/Peter_Quillin" title="Peter Quillin">Peter Quillin</a>.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-55" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-55"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>51<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Prior to the fight, Ishida\'s team decided to never throw roundhouse punches, and was careful with where on the ring he should be.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-miyata&#95;5-5" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-miyata-5"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>5<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> The announcer <a href="/wiki/Jim_Lampley" title="Jim Lampley">Jim Lampley</a> said that it was a bigger upset than <a href="/wiki/Buster_Douglas" title="Buster Douglas">Buster Douglas</a> beating <a href="/wiki/Mike_Tyson" title="Mike Tyson">Mike Tyson</a> in 1990.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-56" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-56"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>52<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> It was voted as the Upset of the Year in <i><a href="/wiki/The_Ring_(magazine)" title="The Ring (magazine)">The Ring</a>\'</i>s 83rd Annual <i>Ring</i> Awards<sup id="cite&#95;ref-FOOTNOTEDonovan201244&#95;57-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDonovan201244-57"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>53<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> and <a href="/wiki/Sports_Illustrated" title="Sports Illustrated">SI.com</a>\'s 2011 Boxing Awards.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-si201112&#95;58-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-si201112-58"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>54<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> In addition, in the <a href="/wiki/The_Ring_(magazine)" title="The Ring (magazine)">RingTV.com</a>\'s year-end polls for 2011, it attracted 22.6 percent of the vote for the Upset of the Year (ranking third),<sup id="cite&#95;ref-59" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-59"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>55<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> and 9.2 percent of the vote for the KO of the Year (ranking second by a large margin).<sup id="cite&#95;ref-60" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-60"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>56<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Ishida was not happy with the status of the former interim champion, and was still not satisfied with knocking out Kirkland on such a big stage.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-miyata&#95;5-6" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-miyata-5"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>5<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>After that upset, Reynoso announced he has a big plan for Ishida.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-notifight20110409&#95;46-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-notifight20110409-46"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>44<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Sampson Lewkowicz, the adviser of <a href="/wiki/Sergio_Mart%C3%ADnez_(boxer)" title="Sergio Martínez (boxer)">Sergio Martínez</a>, made an offer to Ishida as one of the possible opponents for Martínez.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-61" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-61"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>57<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Ishida was once scheduled to fight <a href="/wiki/Paul_Williams_(boxer)" title="Paul Williams (boxer)">Paul Williams</a> at a maximum weight of 155 pounds on July 9, 2011, at the <a href="/wiki/Boardwalk_Hall" title="Boardwalk Hall">Boardwalk Hall</a> in <a href="/wiki/Atlantic_City,_New_Jersey" title="Atlantic City, New Jersey">Atlantic City, New Jersey</a>.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-espn20110516&#95;3-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-espn20110516-3"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>3<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> However it was canceled.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-62" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-62"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>58<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Soon as <a href="/wiki/Julio_C%C3%A9sar_Ch%C3%A1vez,_Jr." class="mw-redirect" title="Julio César Chávez, Jr.">Julio César Chávez, Jr.</a> told that Ishida was his possible opponent,<sup id="cite&#95;ref-63" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-63"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>59<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Ishida phoned from <a href="/wiki/Sacramento,_California" title="Sacramento, California">Sacramento, California</a>, and welcomed the match.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-64" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-64"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>60<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> They had been negotiating the fight, but it was not also signed.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-dailysports201110&#95;43-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-dailysports201110-43"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>42<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Despite the efforts of Eric Gomez, the vice president and matchmaker of Golden Boy Promotions, Ishida\'s opponent was quite undecided.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-65" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-65"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>61<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-66" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-66"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>62<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>According to a YouTube video by Canelo Promotions<sup id="cite&#95;ref-67" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-67"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>Video 3<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> and Ishida\'s blog as of November 2011, although Ishida is most comfortable in the middleweight division, he is willing to move in weight classes, since he thinks he had better prepare the opportunity in possible multiple classes than pick a weight class, until the right offer comes.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-68" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-68"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>63<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Having trained in Los Angeles from July 2011,<sup id="cite&#95;ref-69" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-69"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>64<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> he served as <a href="/wiki/Sa%C3%BAl_%C3%81lvarez" class="mw-redirect" title="Saúl Álvarez">Saúl Álvarez</a>\'s sparring partner at his training camp in Mexico from November of that year.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-70" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-70"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>65<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Ishida won by a technical knockout in the first round against late substitute opponent Edson Espinoza on the undercard of <a href="/wiki/Canelo_%C3%81lvarez_vs._Kermit_Cintr%C3%B3n" title="Canelo Álvarez vs. Kermit Cintrón">Canelo Álvarez vs. Kermit Cintrón</a> on November 26, 2011.\n</p>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Return_to_Super_Welterweight">Return to Super Welterweight</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Nobuhiro_Ishida&amp;action=edit&amp;section=7" title="Edit section: Return to Super Welterweight"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading4"><h4 id="Ishida_vs._Williams">Ishida vs. Williams</h4><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Nobuhiro_Ishida&amp;action=edit&amp;section=8" title="Edit section: Ishida vs. Williams"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<p>Ishida fought against Paul Williams in a twelve-round super welterweight bout held as the main event on <i><a href="/wiki/Showtime_Championship_Boxing" title="Showtime Championship Boxing">Showtime Championship Boxing</a></i> at the <a href="/wiki/American_Bank_Center" class="mw-redirect" title="American Bank Center">American Bank Center</a> in <a href="/wiki/Corpus_Christi,_Texas" title="Corpus Christi, Texas">Corpus Christi</a>, <a href="/wiki/Texas" title="Texas">Texas</a>, on February 18, 2012.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-71" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-71"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>Video 4<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> For that fight, he sparred with <a href="/wiki/Hugo_Centeno,_Jr." class="mw-redirect" title="Hugo Centeno, Jr.">Hugo Centeno, Jr.</a>, Ray Rivera and others, in Maywood, <a href="/wiki/Bell,_California" title="Bell, California">Bell</a>, <a href="/wiki/Carson,_California" title="Carson, California">Carson</a> and <a href="/wiki/East_Los_Angeles,_California" title="East Los Angeles, California">East Los Angeles, California</a>.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-72" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-72"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>66<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Ishida made it an inside fight where power punches accounted for a larger proportion than jabs. Williams\' bodywork skills and holding tactics<sup id="cite&#95;ref-boxon20120221&#95;73-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-boxon20120221-73"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>67<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> did not allow Ishida to throw accurate punches,<sup id="cite&#95;ref-74" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-74"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>68<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> compared with the five fights against Kirkland, Álvarez, Valdéz and Avendaño twice.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-75" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-75"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>69<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Ishida\'s single shots and not many combinations,<sup id="cite&#95;ref-boxon20120221&#95;73-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-boxon20120221-73"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>67<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> although they were sometimes shorter and sharper<sup id="cite&#95;ref-76" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-76"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>70<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> than those of his opponent as were his characteristic ways<sup id="cite&#95;ref-miyata&#95;5-7" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-miyata-5"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>5<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> and made Williams\' face swollen,<sup id="cite&#95;ref-77" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-77"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>71<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> were not enough to make up for the lack of power and physical strength which has often been pointed out.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-78" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-78"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>72<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> He lost the fight via a unanimous decision by the identical scores of 108–120,<sup id="cite&#95;ref-79" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-79"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>73<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> but managed to put himself in position to earn another decent opportunity.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-80" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-80"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>74<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Ishida\'s rankings dropped slightly to number three and number nine in the WBA super welterweight and <a href="/wiki/World_Boxing_Organization" title="World Boxing Organization">WBO</a> middleweight, respectively.\n</p>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Return_to_Middleweight">Return to Middleweight</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Nobuhiro_Ishida&amp;action=edit&amp;section=9" title="Edit section: Return to Middleweight"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading4"><h4 id="Ishida_vs._Pirog">Ishida vs. Pirog</h4><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Nobuhiro_Ishida&amp;action=edit&amp;section=10" title="Edit section: Ishida vs. Pirog"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<p>Subsequently, Ishida lost to <a href="/wiki/Dmitry_Pirog" title="Dmitry Pirog">Dmitry Pirog</a> via a unanimous decision in the WBO middleweight title bout at the Sport Complex Krylatskoe in <a href="/wiki/Moscow" title="Moscow">Moscow</a>, <a href="/wiki/Russia" title="Russia">Russia</a> on May 1 of that year.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-81" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-81"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>75<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-82" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-82"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>Video 5<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> As the JBC had been hesitant to allow that fight,<sup id="cite&#95;ref-83" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-83"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>76<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Ishida resigned his JBC license on April 27, 2012.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-84" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-84"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>77<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Hence, Ishida had not been permitted to fight in Japan from that time forward in principle.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-85" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-85"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>78<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> He has been licensed in California and Texas.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-86" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-86"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>79<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> In June 2012, Ishida underwent surgery to remove <a href="/wiki/Osteochondritis_dissecans" title="Osteochondritis dissecans">bone chips</a> in his left elbow that had plagued him for years.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-87" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-87"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>80<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading4"><h4 id="Ishida_vs._Golovkin">Ishida vs. Golovkin</h4><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Nobuhiro_Ishida&amp;action=edit&amp;section=11" title="Edit section: Ishida vs. Golovkin"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<p>On March 15, 2013, just before the JBC joined the WBO and the <a href="/wiki/International_Boxing_Federation" title="International Boxing Federation">IBF</a>, they gave Ishida permission to fight under the JBC license. Thus, he is allowed to fight anywhere in the world.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-88" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-88"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>81<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>Ishida fought for the WBA and <a href="/wiki/International_Boxing_Organization" title="International Boxing Organization">IBO</a> middleweight titles against <a href="/wiki/Gennady_Golovkin" title="Gennady Golovkin">Gennady Golovkin</a> at the Salle des Étoiles in <a href="/wiki/Monte_Carlo" title="Monte Carlo">Monte Carlo</a>, <a href="/wiki/Monaco" title="Monaco">Monaco</a> on March 30, 2013. The bout was co-featured to the "Monte Carlo Million Dollar Super Four", a <a href="/wiki/Light_heavyweight" title="Light heavyweight">light heavyweight</a> elimination tournament.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-89" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-89"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>82<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> He was knocked out for the first time in his career by Golovkin\'s overhand right in the third round.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-90" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-90"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>83<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-91" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-91"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>84<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-92" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-92"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>85<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-93" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-93"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>Video 6<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>Ishida made a return to the ring in Japan in August 2013.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-94" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-94"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>86<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Professional_boxing_record">Professional boxing record</h2><span 2026-02-26 13:10:11 | DEBUG    | Scraped content: ScrapedContent(url='https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kali_Reis', title='Kali Reis - Wikipedia', text='From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia American boxer and actress (born 1986) Kali Reis Reis in 2024 Personal information Nickname K.O. Mequinonoag [ 3 ] Born ( 1986-08-24 ) August 24, 1986 (age\xa039) [ 1 ] [ 2 ] Providence, Rhode Island , U.S. Height 5\xa0ft 8\xa0in (173\xa0cm) Weight Light welterweight Welterweight Light middleweight Middleweight Boxing career Stance Orthodox Boxing record Total\xa0fights 27 Wins 19 Win\xa0by\xa0KO 5 Losses 7 Draws 1 Kali Reis (born August 24, 1986) is an American professional boxer and actress. She is a former world champion in two weight classes , having held the WBC female middleweight title in 2016 and the WBA , WBO , and IBO female light welterweight titles between 2020 and 2022. She also challenged Cecilia Brækhus for the undisputed female welterweight title in 2018. Reis is a member of the International Women\'s Boxing Hall of Fame . In 2021, Reis made her acting debut as the star of the American thriller film Catch the Fair One . For her performance as a boxer endeavoring to rescue her missing sister, she was nominated for the Independent Spirit Award for Best Female Lead . [ 4 ] [ 5 ] She has since starred in the mystery series True Detective: Night Country (2024), [ 6 ] for which she received nominations for a Primetime Emmy Award , a Golden Globe Award , and a Critics Choice Award . Early life, family and education [ edit ] Reis was born in Providence, Rhode Island , on August 24, 1986, [ 3 ] [ 1 ] [ 2 ] [ 7 ] [ 8 ] the youngest of five children. [ 9 ] She and her siblings were raised by their mother in East Providence . [ 9 ] [ 10 ] Her father, Frank Reis, was a musician who at one point played keyboards for Marky Mark and the Funky Bunch . [ 11 ] Reis has Cape Verdean heritage, [ 12 ] [ 13 ] [ 14 ] and is a member of the Seaconke Wampanoag Tribe , a cultural organization for people who claim Wompanoag ancestry. [ 9 ] [ 15 ] [ 16 ] She has incorporated the name Mequinonoag , given to her by her mother, which she translates as "many feathers" or "many talents", into her boxing nickname, " K.O. Mequinonoag". [ 9 ] [ 17 ] Reis was an athletic child and often played rougher sports with the neighborhood boys. [ 9 ] She participated in her junior high and high school\'s marching bands and color guards and competed in high school volleyball, basketball, and softball. [ 9 ] Reis started boxing at age 14 at Manfredo\'s Gym in Pawtucket, Rhode Island . She was also coached at home by a local Native American boxer who was a friend of her mother. [ 9 ] [ 18 ] Reis later attended school for criminology, aiming to be a corrections officer for juveniles. [ 19 ] [ 20 ] She also learned how to repair motorcycles at MTTI. [ 10 ] She continued her training at Manfredos Gym and Big Six Boxing Academy in Providence. [ 9 ] Before going pro, Reis had a successful amateur career, securing the 2007 Rocky Marciano Championship, the 2007 NYC Golden Gloves, and the 2006 New England 154 Championship. [ 9 ] While beginning her boxing career, she also worked in nightclub security. During this time, she sued the city after being attacked by a police officer. [ 12 ] Professional boxing career [ edit ] In 2012, Reis was involved in a serious motorcycle accident that sidelined her for the remainder of the boxing season. [ 18 ] However, she returned in 2014 and fought for the WIBA title in November of that year. [ 3 ] Reis gained further attention in the sport after the match. [ 18 ] On November 12, 2014, Reis won the IBA crown defeating Teresa Perozzi in Bermuda . [ 3 ] [ 10 ] Reis also coaches boxing for youth and works as a trainer. [ 18 ] In April 2016, Reis won her first major world title in New Zealand against Maricela Cornejo for the vacant WBC World Middleweight title. HBO broadcast its first women\'s bout, between Cecilia Brækhus and Reis, on May 5, 2018, which Brækhus won. [ 21 ] [ 22 ] Reis won a total of 19 fights during her career, 5 by knockout. [ 23 ] Acting career [ edit ] Reis became involved in the movie Catch the Fair One after filmmaker Josef Kubota Wladyka discovered Reis\'s advocacy for the MMIWG movement and asked if she would collaborate as a co-writer and lead actress on a film about that subject. [ 24 ] Catch the Fair One premiered in June 2021 at the Tribeca Film Festival . [ 25 ] The film and Reis\'s debut performance received critical acclaim. Reis was cast in Jean-Stéphane Sauvaire \'s 2023 film Asphalt City (originally titled Black Flies , adapted from the 2008 novel of the same name by Shannon Burke ), starring Sean Penn , Tye Sheridan , and Katherine Waterston . [ 26 ] [ 27 ] In June 2022, Reis was announced as the co-lead of True Detective: Night Country , the fourth season of HBO \'s anthology crime series. Reis starred alongside Jodie Foster as a detective investigating the disappearance of eight men from an Alaskan research station and that event\'s possible connection to the earlier murder of a young woman, an Iñupiaq activist. [ 26 ] [ 28 ] [ 17 ] Accolades [ edit ] For her role in Catch the Fair One , Reis won the Jury Award for Best Actress at the 2021 Newport Beach Film Festival . [ 29 ] She was also nominated for Best Female Lead at the 37th Independent Spirit Awards . [ 30 ] In 2024, Reis became the first Native American woman nominated for a Primetime Emmy for acting; Reis was nominated for a Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Supporting Actress in a Limited or Anthology Series or Movie for her work in True Detective . [ 31 ] [ 32 ] [ 33 ] In February 2022, Reis was honored for her achievements as an athlete and for mentoring local youth by being inducted into the North American Indigenous Athletic Hall of Fame. [ 34 ] That same year, she also received the "Misty Upham Award" at the Red National International Film Festival and was honored with a key to the City of East Providence. [ 35 ] [ 36 ] On March 28, 2024, a panel of Rhode Island House of Representatives recognized Reis with the Community Hero Award for her advocacy and support of Murdered and Missing Indigenous Women and Girls. [ 36 ] [ 37 ] The award was inscribed: "She needed a hero, so she became one." [ 38 ] In October 2025, she was named among the inductees for the 2026 International Women\'s Boxing Hall of Fame class. [ 39 ] Personal life [ edit ] Reis identifies as two-spirit , and has been in relationships with both women and men. [ 12 ] She is married to Brian Cohen , a retired professional boxer. [ 40 ] [ 41 ] She is an active supporter of the Missing and Murdered Indigenous Women and Girls (MMIWG) movement. [ 42 ] [ 43 ] [ 17 ] Disputed ancestry [ edit ] A report from the website Tribal Alliance Against Frauds claims Reis has no Native American ancestry. The website claims to have researched five generations of her genealogy. color:black;">Boxing career</th></tr><tr><td colspan="2" class="infobox-full-data"><link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1316064257" /></td></tr><tr><th scope="row" class="infobox-label">Stance</th><td class="infobox-data"><a href="/wiki/Orthodox_stance" title="Orthodox stance">Orthodox</a></td></tr><tr><th colspan="2" class="infobox-header" style="background:#CCCC99;color:black;">Boxing record</th></tr><tr><th scope="row" class="infobox-label">Total&#160;fights</th><td class="infobox-data">27</td></tr><tr><th scope="row" class="infobox-label">Wins</th><td class="infobox-data">19</td></tr><tr><th scope="row" class="infobox-label">Win&#160;by&#160;KO</th><td class="infobox-data">5</td></tr><tr><th scope="row" class="infobox-label">Losses</th><td class="infobox-data">7</td></tr><tr><th scope="row" class="infobox-label">Draws</th><td class="infobox-data">1</td></tr><tr style="display:none"><td colspan="2">\n</td></tr></tbody></table>\n<p><b>Kali Reis</b> (born August 24, 1986) is an American <a href="/wiki/Professional_boxer" class="mw-redirect" title="Professional boxer">professional boxer</a> and actress. She is a former world champion in two <a href="/wiki/Weight_class_(boxing)" title="Weight class (boxing)">weight classes</a>, having held the <a href="/wiki/World_Boxing_Council" title="World Boxing Council">WBC</a> female <a href="/wiki/Middleweight" title="Middleweight">middleweight</a> title in 2016 and the <a href="/wiki/World_Boxing_Association" title="World Boxing Association">WBA</a>, <a href="/wiki/WBO" class="mw-redirect" title="WBO">WBO</a>, and <a href="/wiki/International_Boxing_Organization" title="International Boxing Organization">IBO</a> female <a href="/wiki/Light_welterweight" title="Light welterweight">light welterweight</a> titles between 2020 and 2022. She also challenged <a href="/wiki/Cecilia_Br%C3%A6khus" title="Cecilia Brækhus">Cecilia Brækhus</a> for the <a href="/wiki/Undisputed_championship_(boxing)" title="Undisputed championship (boxing)">undisputed</a> female <a href="/wiki/Welterweight" title="Welterweight">welterweight</a> title in 2018. Reis is a member of the <a href="/wiki/International_Women%27s_Boxing_Hall_of_Fame" title="International Women&#39;s Boxing Hall of Fame">International Women\'s Boxing Hall of Fame</a>.\n</p><p>In 2021, Reis made her acting debut as the star of the American thriller film <i><a href="/wiki/Catch_the_Fair_One" title="Catch the Fair One">Catch the Fair One</a></i>. For her performance as a boxer endeavoring to rescue her missing sister, she was nominated for the <a href="/wiki/Independent_Spirit_Award_for_Best_Female_Lead" title="Independent Spirit Award for Best Female Lead">Independent Spirit Award for Best Female Lead</a>.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-4" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-4"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>4<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-5" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-5"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>5<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> She has since starred in the mystery series <i><a href="/wiki/True_Detective_(season_4)" class="mw-redirect" title="True Detective (season 4)">True Detective: Night Country</a></i> (2024),<sup id="cite&#95;ref-6" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-6"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>6<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> for which she received nominations for a <a href="/wiki/Primetime_Emmy_Award" class="mw-redirect" title="Primetime Emmy Award">Primetime Emmy Award</a>, a <a href="/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award" class="mw-redirect" title="Golden Globe Award">Golden Globe Award</a>, and a <a href="/wiki/Critics_Choice_Award" class="mw-redirect" title="Critics Choice Award">Critics Choice Award</a>.\n</p>\n<meta property="mw:PageProp/toc" />\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Early_life,_family_and_education"><span id="Early_life.2C_family_and_education"></span>Early life, family and education</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Kali_Reis&amp;action=edit&amp;section=1" title="Edit section: Early life, family and education"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<p>Reis was born in <a href="/wiki/Providence,_Rhode_Island" title="Providence, Rhode Island">Providence, Rhode Island</a>, on August 24, 1986,<sup id="cite&#95;ref-idnc&#95;3-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-idnc-3"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>3<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-roundbyroundboxing.com&#95;1-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-roundbyroundboxing.com-1"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-realcombatmedia.com&#95;2-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-realcombatmedia.com-2"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-bdd&#95;7-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-bdd-7"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>7<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-komeq&#95;8-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-komeq-8"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>8<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> the youngest of five children.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-WomenBoxing&#95;9-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-WomenBoxing-9"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>9<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> She and her siblings were raised by their mother in <a href="/wiki/East_Providence,_Rhode_Island" title="East Providence, Rhode Island">East Providence</a>.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-WomenBoxing&#95;9-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-WomenBoxing-9"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>9<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-ksc&#95;10-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-ksc-10"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>10<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Her father, Frank Reis, was a musician who at one point played keyboards for <a href="/wiki/Marky_Mark_and_the_Funky_Bunch" title="Marky Mark and the Funky Bunch">Marky Mark and the Funky Bunch</a>.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-11" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-11"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>11<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>Reis has <a href="/wiki/Cape_Verde" title="Cape Verde">Cape Verdean</a> heritage,<sup id="cite&#95;ref-Vulture&#95;12-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Vulture-12"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>12<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-13" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-13"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>13<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-14" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-14"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>14<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> and is a member of the <a href="/wiki/Seaconke_Wampanoag_Tribe" title="Seaconke Wampanoag Tribe">Seaconke Wampanoag Tribe</a>, a cultural organization for people who claim <a href="/wiki/Wampanoag_people" class="mw-redirect" title="Wampanoag people">Wompanoag</a> ancestry.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-WomenBoxing&#95;9-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-WomenBoxing-9"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>9<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-15" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-15"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>15<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-16" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-16"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>16<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> She has incorporated the name <i>Mequinonoag</i>, given to her by her mother, which she translates as "many feathers" or "many talents", into her boxing nickname, "<a href="/wiki/Knockout" title="Knockout">K.O.</a> Mequinonoag".<sup id="cite&#95;ref-WomenBoxing&#95;9-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-WomenBoxing-9"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>9<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-:0&#95;17-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:0-17"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>17<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>Reis was an athletic child and often played rougher sports with the neighborhood boys.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-WomenBoxing&#95;9-4" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-WomenBoxing-9"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>9<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> She participated in her junior high and high school\'s <a href="/wiki/Marching_band" title="Marching band">marching bands</a> and <a href="/wiki/Color_guard" class="mw-redirect" title="Color guard">color guards</a> and competed in high school volleyball, basketball, and softball.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-WomenBoxing&#95;9-5" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-WomenBoxing-9"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>9<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Reis started boxing at age 14 at Manfredo\'s Gym in <a href="/wiki/Pawtucket,_Rhode_Island" title="Pawtucket, Rhode Island">Pawtucket, Rhode Island</a>. She was also coached at home by a local Native American boxer who was a friend of her mother.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-WomenBoxing&#95;9-6" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-WomenBoxing-9"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>9<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-fig&#95;18-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-fig-18"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>18<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> \n</p><p>Reis later attended school for criminology, aiming to be a corrections officer for juveniles.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-19" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-19"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>19<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-20" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-20"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>20<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> She also learned how to repair motorcycles at MTTI.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-ksc&#95;10-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-ksc-10"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>10<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> She continued her training at Manfredos Gym and Big Six Boxing Academy in Providence.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-WomenBoxing&#95;9-7" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-WomenBoxing-9"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>9<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>Before going pro, Reis had a successful amateur career, securing the 2007 Rocky Marciano Championship, the 2007 NYC Golden Gloves, and the 2006 New England 154 Championship.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-WomenBoxing&#95;9-8" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-WomenBoxing-9"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>9<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> While beginning her boxing career, she also worked in nightclub security. During this time, she sued the city after being attacked by a police officer.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-Vulture&#95;12-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Vulture-12"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>12<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Professional_boxing_career">Professional boxing career</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Kali_Reis&amp;action=edit&amp;section=2" title="Edit section: Professional boxing career"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<p>In 2012, Reis was involved in a serious motorcycle accident that sidelined her for the remainder of the boxing season.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-fig&#95;18-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-fig-18"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>18<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> However, she returned in 2014 and fought for the WIBA title in November of that year.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-idnc&#95;3-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-idnc-3"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>3<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Reis gained further attention in the sport after the match.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-fig&#95;18-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-fig-18"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>18<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>  On November 12, 2014, Reis won the IBA crown defeating <a href="/wiki/Teresa_Perozzi" title="Teresa Perozzi">Teresa Perozzi</a> in <a href="/wiki/Bermuda" title="Bermuda">Bermuda</a>.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-idnc&#95;3-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-idnc-3"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>3<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-ksc&#95;10-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-ksc-10"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>10<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Reis also coaches boxing for youth and works as a trainer.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-fig&#95;18-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-fig-18"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>18<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> In April 2016, Reis won her first major world title in <a href="/wiki/New_Zealand" title="New Zealand">New Zealand</a> against <a href="/wiki/Maricela_Cornejo" title="Maricela Cornejo">Maricela Cornejo</a> for the vacant WBC World Middleweight title.\n</p><p><a href="/wiki/HBO" title="HBO">HBO</a> broadcast its first women\'s bout, between <a href="/wiki/Cecilia_Br%C3%A6khus" title="Cecilia Brækhus">Cecilia Brækhus</a> and Reis, on May 5, 2018, which Brækhus won.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-21" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-21"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>21<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-22" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-22"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>22<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>Reis won a total of 19 fights during her career, 5 by knockout.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-23" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-23"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>23<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Acting_career">Acting career</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Kali_Reis&amp;action=edit&amp;section=3" title="Edit section: Acting career"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<p>Reis became involved in the movie <i>Catch the Fair One</i> after filmmaker Josef Kubota Wladyka discovered Reis\'s advocacy for the <a href="/wiki/Missing_and_Murdered_Indigenous_Women" title="Missing and Murdered Indigenous Women">MMIWG</a> movement and asked if she would collaborate as a co-writer and lead actress on a film about that subject.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-24" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-24"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>24<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> <i>Catch the Fair One</i> premiered in June 2021 at the <a href="/wiki/Tribeca_Film_Festival" class="mw-redirect" title="Tribeca Film Festival">Tribeca Film Festival</a>.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-25" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-25"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>25<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> The film and Reis\'s debut performance received critical acclaim.\n</p><p>Reis was cast in <a href="/wiki/Jean-St%C3%A9phane_Sauvaire" title="Jean-Stéphane Sauvaire">Jean-Stéphane Sauvaire</a>\'s 2023 film <i><a href="/wiki/Asphalt_City" title="Asphalt City">Asphalt City</a></i> (originally titled <i>Black Flies</i>, adapted from the 2008 novel of the same name by <a href="/wiki/Shannon_Burke_(writer)" title="Shannon Burke (writer)">Shannon Burke</a>), starring <a href="/wiki/Sean_Penn" title="Sean Penn">Sean Penn</a>, <a href="/wiki/Tye_Sheridan" title="Tye Sheridan">Tye Sheridan</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Katherine_Waterston" title="Katherine Waterston">Katherine Waterston</a>.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-Deadline&#95;26-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Deadline-26"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>26<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-27" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-27"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>27<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>In June 2022, Reis was announced as the co-lead of <i><a href="/wiki/True_Detective_(season_4)" class="mw-redirect" title="True Detective (season 4)">True Detective: Night Country</a></i>, the fourth season of <a href="/wiki/HBO" title="HBO">HBO</a>\'s anthology crime series. Reis starred alongside <a href="/wiki/Jodie_Foster" title="Jodie Foster">Jodie Foster</a> as a detective investigating the disappearance of eight men from an Alaskan research station and that event\'s possible connection to the earlier murder of a young woman, an <a href="/wiki/I%C3%B1upiaq" class="mw-redirect" title="Iñupiaq">Iñupiaq</a> activist.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-Deadline&#95;26-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Deadline-26"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>26<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-28" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-28"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>28<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-:0&#95;17-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:0-17"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>17<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Accolades">Accolades</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Kali_Reis&amp;action=edit&amp;section=4" title="Edit section: Accolades"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<p>For her role in <i>Catch the Fair One</i>, Reis won the Jury Award for Best Actress at the 2021 <a href="/wiki/Newport_Beach_Film_Festival" title="Newport Beach Film Festival">Newport Beach Film Festival</a>.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-29" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-29"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>29<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> She was also nominated for <a href="/wiki/Independent_Spirit_Award_for_Best_Female_Lead" title="Independent Spirit Award for Best Female Lead">Best Female Lead</a> at the <a href="/wiki/37th_Independent_Spirit_Awards" title="37th Independent Spirit Awards">37th Independent Spirit Awards</a>.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-30" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-30"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>30<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> In 2024, Reis became the first Native American woman nominated for a Primetime Emmy for acting; Reis was nominated for a <a href="/wiki/Primetime_Emmy_Award_for_Outstanding_Supporting_Actress_in_a_Limited_or_Anthology_Series_or_Movie" title="Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Supporting Actress in a Limited or Anthology Series or Movie">Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Supporting Actress in a Limited or Anthology Series or Movie</a> for her work in <i><a href="/wiki/True_Detective" title="True Detective">True Detective</a></i>.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-31" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-31"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>31<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-32" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-32"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>32<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-33" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-33"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>33<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>In February 2022, Reis was honored for her achievements as an athlete and for mentoring local youth by being inducted into the North American Indigenous Athletic Hall of Fame.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-34" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-34"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>34<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> That same year, she also received the "Misty Upham Award" at the Red National International Film Festival and was honored with a key to the City of East Providence.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-35" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-35"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>35<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-:1&#95;36-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:1-36"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>36<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> On March 28, 2024, a panel of <a href="/wiki/Rhode_Island_House_of_Representatives" title="Rhode Island House of Representatives">Rhode Island House of Representatives</a> recognized Reis with the Community Hero Award for her advocacy and support of Murdered and Missing Indigenous Women and Girls.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-:1&#95;36-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:1-36"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>36<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-37" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-37"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>37<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> The award was inscribed: "She needed a hero, so she became one."<sup id="cite&#95;ref-38" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-38"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>38<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>In October 2025, she was named among the inductees for the 2026 <a href="/wiki/International_Women%27s_Boxing_Hall_of_Fame" title="International Women&#39;s Boxing Hall of Fame">International Women\'s Boxing Hall of Fame</a> class.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-39" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-39"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>39<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Personal_life">Personal life</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Kali_Reis&amp;action=edit&amp;section=5" title="Edit section: Personal life"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<p>Reis identifies as <a href="/wiki/Two-spirit" title="Two-spirit">two-spirit</a>, and has been in relationships with both women and men.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-Vulture&#95;12-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Vulture-12"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>12<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> She is married to <a href="/wiki/Brian_Cohen_(boxer)" title="Brian Cohen (boxer)">Brian Cohen</a>, a retired professional boxer.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-40" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-40"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>40<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-41" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-41"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>41<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>She is an active supporter of the <a href="/wiki/Missing_and_Murdered_Indigenous_Women_and_Girls" class="mw-redirect" title="Missing and Murdered Indigenous Women and Girls">Missing and Murdered Indigenous Women and Girls</a> (MMIWG) movement.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-boxing-social.com&#95;42-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-boxing-social.com-42"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>42<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-43" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-43"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>43<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-:0&#95;17-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:0-17"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>17<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Disputed_ancestry">Disputed ancestry</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Kali_Reis&amp;action=edit&amp;section=6" title="Edit section: Disputed ancestry"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<p>A report from the website <a href="/wiki/Tribal_Alliance_Against_Frauds" title="Tribal Alliance Against Frauds">Tribal Alliance Against Frauds</a> claims Reis has no Native American ancestry. The website claims to have researched five generations of her genealogy.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-44" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-44"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>44<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> \n</p>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Professional_boxing_record">Professional boxing record</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span
