2026-02-26 13:10:12 | DEBUG    | Scraped content: ScrapedContent(url='https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalton_Smith_(boxer)', title='Dalton Smith (boxer) - Wikipedia', text='From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia British boxer (born 1997) For the Canadian ice hockey player, see Dalton Smith . Dalton Smith Personal information Nickname Thunder Born ( 1997-02-08 ) 8 February 1997 (age\xa029) Sheffield , Yorkshire , England Height 5\xa0ft 9 + 1 ⁄ 2 in (177\xa0cm) Weight Light welterweight Boxing career Reach 69 + 1 ⁄ 2 in (177\xa0cm) Stance Orthodox Boxing record Total\xa0fights 19 Wins 19 Win\xa0by\xa0KO 14 Medal record Men\'s Amateur boxing Representing England Commonwealth Youth Games 2015 Apia Lightweight European Youth Championships 2014 Zagreb Lightweight ABA Championships 2018 London Light-welterweight Dalton Smith (born 8 February 1997) is a British professional boxer . He has held the World Boxing Council (WBC) super-lightweight title since January 2026. Previously, he held the European super-lightweight title in 2025, the British title between 2022 and 2024, and the Commonwealth title in 2023. As an amateur , he won a silver medal at the 2014 European Youth Championships and bronze at the 2015 Commonwealth Youth Games , both in the lightweight division, and won the 2018 ABA Championships at light-welterweight . Amateur career [ edit ] As an amateur Smith won multiple national titles at the junior and senior level, [ 1 ] including the 2018 ABA Championships at light-welterweight . [ 2 ] At the international level he won a silver medal at the 2014 European Youth Championships and bronze at the 2015 Commonwealth Youth Games , both in the lightweight division. [ 1 ] He also competed at the 2013 World Junior Championships , reaching the quarter-finals; [ 3 ] the 2014 World Youth Championships , losing in the round of 8; [ 4 ] and the 2016 , [ 5 ] 2017 [ 6 ] and 2018 World Series of Boxing as part of the British Lionhearts . [ 7 ] Professional career [ edit ] After deciding to forgo the 2020 Olympics – due to rule changes regarding weight categories, along with several injuries suffered throughout his amateur career – Smith signed a promotional contract with Eddie Hearn \'s Matchroom Boxing in May 2019, [ 8 ] making his professional debut two months later on 10 May, scoring a four-round points decision (PTS) victory over Luka Leskovic at the Motorpoint Arena in Nottingham . [ 9 ] In his next fight he defeated Ibrar Riyaz with a second-round stoppage via corner retirement (RTD) on 21 July as part of the undercard for Dillian Whyte vs. Oscar Rivas . [ 10 ] Smith became only the fourth man to stop Riyaz, [ 11 ] a career journeyman who at the time had a record of 6–165–4. [ 12 ] Three months later he travelled to Italy , defeating Marko Radenovic via third-round technical knockout (TKO) [ 13 ] before ending the year with a third-round TKO win against Michael Carrero in November. [ 14 ] On 7 March 2020 at the Manchester Arena , Smith fought Benson Nyilawila, winning by fourth-round TKO in a bout that was streamed live on Facebook . [ 15 ] On 6 August 2022, Smith defeated Sam O\'maison via 6th round TKO to win the British super lightweight championship. [ 16 ] On 1 July 2023, Smith knocked out Sam Maxwell in round 7 and won the Commonwealth super lightweight championship. [ 17 ] Smith vacated the title one month later. [ citation needed ] On 23 March 2024 in Sheffield , England, Smith was scheduled to face Jose Zepeda . [ 18 ] [ 19 ] He won the fight by knockout in the fifth round with body shot, winning the vacant WBC Silver super lightweight title. [ 20 ] Smith was originally scheduled to face Jon Fernandez for the vacant European super lightweight title in Sheffield, England on 28 September 2024, However, the bout was cancelled on September 6 due to unclear reasons. [ 21 ] On 25 January 2025 in Nottingham, England, Smith defeated Walid Ouizza by knockout in the first round to defend his WBC Silver super lightweight title and win the vacant EBU European super lightweight title. [ 22 ] [ 23 ] [ 24 ] Smith faced Mathieu Germain at Canon Medical Arena in Sheffield on 19 April 2025. [ 25 ] [ 26 ] He won the fight by unanimous decision. [ 27 ] [ 28 ] [ 29 ] He challenged WBC super-lightweight champion, Subriel Matías , at Barclays Center in Brooklyn , New York, USA, on 10 January 2026. [ 30 ] [ 31 ] Smith won by technical knockout in the fifth round. src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d5/Gold_medal_icon_%28G_initial%29.svg/20px-Gold_medal_icon_%28G_initial%29.svg.png" decoding="async" width="16" height="16" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d5/Gold_medal_icon_%28G_initial%29.svg/40px-Gold_medal_icon_%28G_initial%29.svg.png 1.5x" data-file-width="16" data-file-height="16" /></span></span></td>\n<td style="text-align:center;vertical-align:middle;"><span class="nowrap">2018 London</span></td>\n<td style="text-align:center;vertical-align:middle;"><a href="/wiki/England_Boxing_National_Amateur_Championships_Light-Welterweight_Champions" title="England Boxing National Amateur Championships Light-Welterweight Champions">Light-welterweight</a>\n</td></tr></tbody></table>\n</div></div></th></tr></tbody></table>\n<p><b>Dalton Smith</b> (born 8 February 1997) is a British <a href="/wiki/Professional_boxer" class="mw-redirect" title="Professional boxer">professional boxer</a>. He has held the <a href="/wiki/World_Boxing_Council" title="World Boxing Council">World Boxing Council</a> (WBC) <a href="/wiki/Super-lightweight" class="mw-redirect" title="Super-lightweight">super-lightweight</a> title since January 2026. Previously, he held the <a href="/wiki/European_Boxing_Union" title="European Boxing Union">European</a> super-lightweight title in 2025, the <a href="/wiki/British_Boxing_Board_of_Control" title="British Boxing Board of Control">British</a> title between 2022 and 2024, and the <a href="/wiki/Commonwealth_Boxing_Council" title="Commonwealth Boxing Council">Commonwealth</a> title in 2023. As an <a href="/wiki/Amateur_boxing" title="Amateur boxing">amateur</a>, he won a silver medal at the 2014 <a href="/wiki/European_Amateur_Boxing_Championships#EUBC_events" title="European Amateur Boxing Championships">European Youth Championships</a> and bronze at the <a href="/wiki/Boxing_at_the_2015_Commonwealth_Youth_Games" title="Boxing at the 2015 Commonwealth Youth Games">2015 Commonwealth Youth Games</a>, both in the <a href="/wiki/Lightweight" title="Lightweight">lightweight</a> division, and won the 2018 <a href="/wiki/ABA_Championships" class="mw-redirect" title="ABA Championships">ABA Championships</a> at <a href="/wiki/Light-welterweight" class="mw-redirect" title="Light-welterweight">light-welterweight</a>.\n</p>\n<meta property="mw:PageProp/toc" />\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Amateur_career">Amateur career</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Dalton_Smith_(boxer)&amp;action=edit&amp;section=1" title="Edit section: Amateur career"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<p>As an amateur Smith won multiple national titles at the junior and senior level,<sup id="cite&#95;ref-TheStar1&#95;1-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-TheStar1-1"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> including the <a href="/wiki/England_Boxing_National_Amateur_Championships_Light-Welterweight_Champions" title="England Boxing National Amateur Championships Light-Welterweight Champions">2018 ABA Championships</a> at <a href="/wiki/Light-welterweight" class="mw-redirect" title="Light-welterweight">light-welterweight</a>.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-2"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> At the international level he won a silver medal at the 2014 <a href="/wiki/European_Amateur_Boxing_Championships#EUBC_events" title="European Amateur Boxing Championships">European Youth Championships</a> and bronze at the <a href="/wiki/Boxing_at_the_2015_Commonwealth_Youth_Games" title="Boxing at the 2015 Commonwealth Youth Games">2015 Commonwealth Youth Games</a>, both in the <a href="/wiki/Lightweight" title="Lightweight">lightweight</a> division.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-TheStar1&#95;1-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-TheStar1-1"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> He also competed at the 2013 <a href="/wiki/Youth_and_Junior_World_Boxing_Championships#Men&#39;s_editions" class="mw-redirect" title="Youth and Junior World Boxing Championships">World Junior Championships</a>, reaching the quarter-finals;<sup id="cite&#95;ref-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-3"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>3<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> the <a href="/wiki/2014_AIBA_Youth_World_Boxing_Championships" title="2014 AIBA Youth World Boxing Championships">2014 World Youth Championships</a>, losing in the round of 8;<sup id="cite&#95;ref-4" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-4"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>4<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> and the <a href="/wiki/2016_World_Series_of_Boxing" title="2016 World Series of Boxing">2016</a>,<sup id="cite&#95;ref-5" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-5"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>5<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> <a href="/wiki/2017_World_Series_of_Boxing" title="2017 World Series of Boxing">2017</a><sup id="cite&#95;ref-6" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-6"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>6<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> and 2018 <a href="/wiki/World_Series_of_Boxing" title="World Series of Boxing">World Series of Boxing</a> as part of the <a href="/wiki/British_Lionhearts" title="British Lionhearts">British Lionhearts</a>.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-7" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-7"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>7<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Professional_career">Professional career</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Dalton_Smith_(boxer)&amp;action=edit&amp;section=2" title="Edit section: Professional career"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<p>After deciding to forgo the <a href="/wiki/2020_Olympics" class="mw-redirect" title="2020 Olympics">2020 Olympics</a> – due to rule changes regarding weight categories, along with several injuries suffered throughout his amateur career – Smith signed a promotional contract with <a href="/wiki/Eddie_Hearn" title="Eddie Hearn">Eddie Hearn</a>\'s <a href="/wiki/Matchroom_Boxing" class="mw-redirect" title="Matchroom Boxing">Matchroom Boxing</a> in May 2019,<sup id="cite&#95;ref-8" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-8"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>8<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> making his professional debut two months later on 10 May, scoring a four-round <a href="/wiki/Points_decision" title="Points decision">points decision</a> (PTS) victory over Luka Leskovic at the <a href="/wiki/Motorpoint_Arena_Nottingham" class="mw-redirect" title="Motorpoint Arena Nottingham">Motorpoint Arena</a> in <a href="/wiki/Nottingham" title="Nottingham">Nottingham</a>.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-9" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-9"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>9<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>In his next fight he defeated Ibrar Riyaz with a second-round stoppage via <a href="/wiki/Corner_retirement" title="Corner retirement">corner retirement</a> (RTD) on 21 July as part of the undercard for <a href="/wiki/Dillian_Whyte_vs._Oscar_Rivas" class="mw-redirect" title="Dillian Whyte vs. Oscar Rivas">Dillian Whyte vs. Oscar Rivas</a>.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-10" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-10"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>10<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Smith became only the fourth man to stop Riyaz,<sup id="cite&#95;ref-11" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-11"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>11<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> a career <a href="/wiki/Journeyman_(boxing)" class="mw-redirect" title="Journeyman (boxing)">journeyman</a> who at the time had a record of 6–165–4.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-12" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-12"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>12<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Three months later he travelled to <a href="/wiki/Italy" title="Italy">Italy</a>, defeating Marko Radenovic via third-round <a href="/wiki/Technical_knockout" class="mw-redirect" title="Technical knockout">technical knockout</a> (TKO)<sup id="cite&#95;ref-13" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-13"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>13<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> before ending the year with a third-round TKO win against Michael Carrero in November.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-14" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-14"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>14<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>On 7 March 2020 at the <a href="/wiki/Manchester_Arena" title="Manchester Arena">Manchester Arena</a>, Smith fought Benson Nyilawila, winning by fourth-round TKO in a bout that was <a href="/wiki/Streaming_television" title="Streaming television">streamed</a> live on <a href="/wiki/Facebook" title="Facebook">Facebook</a>.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-15" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-15"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>15<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>On 6 August 2022, Smith defeated Sam O\'maison via 6th round TKO to win the British super lightweight championship.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-16" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-16"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>16<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>On 1 July 2023, Smith knocked out Sam Maxwell in round 7 and won the Commonwealth super lightweight championship.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-17" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-17"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>17<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Smith vacated the title one month later.<sup class="noprint Inline-Template Template-Fact" style="white-space:nowrap;">&#91;<i><a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed" title="Wikipedia:Citation needed"><span title="This claim needs references to reliable sources. (March 2025)">citation needed</span></a></i>&#93;</sup>\n</p><p>On 23 March 2024 in <a href="/wiki/Sheffield" title="Sheffield">Sheffield</a>, England, Smith was scheduled to face <a href="/wiki/Jose_Zepeda" title="Jose Zepeda">Jose Zepeda</a>.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-18" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-18"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>18<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-19" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-19"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>19<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> He won the fight by knockout in the fifth round with body shot, winning the vacant WBC Silver super lightweight title.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-20" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-20"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>20<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>Smith was originally scheduled to face Jon Fernandez for the vacant European super lightweight title in Sheffield, England on 28 September 2024, However, the bout was cancelled on September 6 due to unclear reasons.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-21" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-21"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>21<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>On 25 January 2025 in Nottingham, England, Smith defeated Walid Ouizza by knockout in the first round to defend his WBC Silver super lightweight title and win the vacant EBU European super lightweight title.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-22" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-22"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>22<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-23" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-23"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>23<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-24" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-24"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>24<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>Smith faced Mathieu Germain at <a href="/wiki/Canon_Medical_Arena" class="mw-redirect" title="Canon Medical Arena">Canon Medical Arena</a> in Sheffield on 19 April 2025.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-25" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-25"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>25<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-26" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-26"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>26<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> He won the fight by unanimous decision.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-27" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-27"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>27<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-28" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-28"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>28<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-29" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-29"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>29<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>He challenged <a href="/wiki/World_Boxing_Council" title="World Boxing Council">WBC</a> super-lightweight champion, <a href="/wiki/Subriel_Mat%C3%ADas" title="Subriel Matías">Subriel Matías</a>, at <a href="/wiki/Barclays_Center" title="Barclays Center">Barclays Center</a> in <a href="/wiki/Brooklyn" title="Brooklyn">Brooklyn</a>, New York, USA, on 10 January 2026.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-30" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-30"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>30<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-31" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-31"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>31<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Smith won by technical knockout in the fifth round.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-32" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-32"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>32<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-33" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-33"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>33<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Professional_boxing_record">Professional boxing record</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span 2026-02-26 13:10:13 | DEBUG    | Scraped content: ScrapedContent(url='https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Light_welterweight', title='Light welterweight - Wikipedia', text='From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia Weight class in boxing and kickboxing Light welterweight , also known as junior welterweight [ 1 ] or super lightweight , [ 2 ] is a weight class in combat sports . Boxing [ edit ] Professional boxing [ edit ] In professional boxing , light welterweight is contested between the lightweight and welterweight divisions, in which boxers weigh above 61.2kg or 135 pounds and up to 63.5\xa0kg or 140 Ibs. The first champion of this weight class was Pinky Mitchell in 1922, though he was only awarded his championship by a vote of the readers of the Boxing Blade magazine. There was not widespread acceptance of this new weight division in its early years, and the New York State Athletic Commission withdrew recognition of it in 1930. The National Boxing Association continued to recognize it until its champion, Barney Ross relinquished the title in 1935 to concentrate on regaining the welterweight championship. A few commissions recognized bouts in the 1940s as being for the light welterweight title, but the modern beginnings of this championship date from 1959 when Carlos Ortiz won the vacant title with a victory over Kenny Lane . Both the World Boxing Association (WBA) and the World Boxing Council (WBC) recognized the same champions until 1967, when the WBC stripped Paul Fuji of the title and matched Pedro Adigue and Adolph Pruitt for their version of the championship. Adigue won a fifteen-round decision. The International Boxing Federation (IBF) recognized Aaron Pryor as its first champion in 1984. Hector Camacho became the first World Boxing Organization (WBO) champion with his victory against Ray Mancini in 1989. [ 5 ] Rank Name Record Title(s) 1 Shakur Stevenson 25–0 (11 KO) WBO & The Ring 2 Dalton Smith 19–0 (14 KO) WBC 3 Keyshawn Davis 14–0 (10 KO) 4 Teofimo Lopez 22–2 (13 KO) 5 Richardson Hitchins 20–0 (8 KO) IBF 6 Adam Azim 14–0 (11 KO) 7 Arnold Barboza Jr. 32–1 (11 KO) 8 Arthur Biyarslanov 20–0 (16 KO) 9 Ernesto Mercado 18–0 (17 KO) 10 Khariton Agrba 17–1 (9 KO) Amateur boxing [ edit ] In amateur boxing , light welterweight is a weight class for fighters weighing up to 64 kilograms . For the 1952 Summer Olympics , the division was created when the span from 54 to 67\xa0kg was changed from three weight classes ( featherweight , lightweight , and welterweight ) to four. Perhaps the most famous amateur light welterweight champion is Sugar Ray Leonard , who went on to an impressive professional career. Lethwei [ edit ] The World Lethwei Championship recognizes the light welterweight division with an upper limit of 63.5\xa0kg (140\xa0lb). In World Lethwei Championship Antonio Faria is the Light welterweight Champion. References [ edit ] ^ "Ring Ratings" Archived 2015-11-15 at the Wayback Machine . The Ring . class="vector-body" aria-labelledby="firstHeading" data-mw-ve-target-container>\n\t\t\t\t\t<div class="vector-body-before-content">\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t<div class="mw-indicators">\n\t\t</div>\n\n\t\t\t\t\t\t<div id="siteSub" class="noprint">From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia</div>\n\t\t\t\t\t</div>\n\t\t\t\t\t<div id="contentSub"><div id="mw-content-subtitle"></div></div>\n\t\t\t\t\t\n\t\t\t\t\t\n\t\t\t\t\t<div id="mw-content-text" class="mw-body-content"><div class="mw-subjectpageheader">\n</div><div class="mw-content-ltr mw-parser-output" lang="en" dir="ltr"><div class="shortdescription nomobile noexcerpt noprint searchaux" style="display:none">Weight class in boxing and kickboxing</div>\n<p><b>Light welterweight</b>, also known as <b>junior welterweight</b><sup id="cite&#95;ref-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-1"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> or <b>super lightweight</b>,<sup id="cite&#95;ref-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-2"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> is a <a href="/wiki/Weight_class" title="Weight class">weight class</a> in <a href="/wiki/Combat_sport" title="Combat sport">combat sports</a>.\n</p>\n<meta property="mw:PageProp/toc" />\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Boxing">Boxing</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Light_welterweight&amp;action=edit&amp;section=1" title="Edit section: Boxing"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Professional_boxing">Professional boxing</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Light_welterweight&amp;action=edit&amp;section=2" title="Edit section: Professional boxing"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<p>In <a href="/wiki/Professional_boxing" title="Professional boxing">professional boxing</a>, light welterweight is contested between the <a href="/wiki/Lightweight" title="Lightweight">lightweight</a> and <a href="/wiki/Welterweight" title="Welterweight">welterweight</a> divisions, in which boxers weigh above 61.2kg or 135 pounds and up to 63.5&#160;kg or 140 Ibs. The first champion of this weight class was <a href="/wiki/Pinky_Mitchell" title="Pinky Mitchell">Pinky Mitchell</a> in 1922, though he was only awarded his championship by a vote of the readers of the <i>Boxing Blade</i> magazine.\n</p><p>There was not widespread acceptance of this new weight division in its early years, and the <a href="/wiki/New_York_State_Athletic_Commission" title="New York State Athletic Commission">New York State Athletic Commission</a> withdrew recognition of it in 1930. The <a href="/wiki/National_Boxing_Association" class="mw-redirect" title="National Boxing Association">National Boxing Association</a> continued to recognize it until its champion, <a href="/wiki/Barney_Ross" title="Barney Ross">Barney Ross</a> relinquished the title in 1935 to concentrate on regaining the <a href="/wiki/Welterweight" title="Welterweight">welterweight</a> championship.\n</p><p>A few commissions recognized bouts in the 1940s as being for the light welterweight title, but the modern beginnings of this championship date from 1959 when <a href="/wiki/Carlos_Ortiz_(boxer)" title="Carlos Ortiz (boxer)">Carlos Ortiz</a> won the vacant title with a victory over <a href="/wiki/Kenny_Lane" title="Kenny Lane">Kenny Lane</a>. Both the World Boxing Association (WBA) and the World Boxing Council (WBC) recognized the same champions until 1967, when the WBC stripped <a href="/wiki/Paul_Fuji" class="mw-redirect" title="Paul Fuji">Paul Fuji</a> of the title and matched <a href="/wiki/Pedro_Adigue" title="Pedro Adigue">Pedro Adigue</a> and Adolph Pruitt for their version of the championship. Adigue won a fifteen-round decision. The <a href="/wiki/International_Boxing_Federation" title="International Boxing Federation">International Boxing Federation</a> (IBF) recognized <a href="/wiki/Aaron_Pryor" title="Aaron Pryor">Aaron Pryor</a> as its first champion in 1984. <a href="/wiki/Hector_Camacho" class="mw-redirect" title="Hector Camacho">Hector Camacho</a> became the first <a href="/wiki/World_Boxing_Organization" title="World Boxing Organization">World Boxing Organization</a> (WBO) champion with his victory against <a href="/wiki/Ray_Mancini" title="Ray Mancini">Ray Mancini</a> in 1989.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-3"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>3<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> \n</p>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading4"><h4 class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Amateur_boxing">Amateur boxing</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Light_welterweight&amp;action=edit&amp;section=7" title="Edit section: Amateur boxing"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<p>In <a href="/wiki/Amateur_boxing" title="Amateur boxing">amateur boxing</a>, light welterweight is a weight class for fighters weighing up to 64 <a href="/wiki/Kilograms" class="mw-redirect" title="Kilograms">kilograms</a>. For the <a href="/wiki/1952_Summer_Olympics" title="1952 Summer Olympics">1952 Summer Olympics</a>, the division was created when the span from 54 to 67&#160;kg was changed from three weight classes (<a href="/wiki/Featherweight" title="Featherweight">featherweight</a>, <a href="/wiki/Lightweight" title="Lightweight">lightweight</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Welterweight" title="Welterweight">welterweight</a>) to four. Perhaps the most famous amateur light welterweight champion is <a href="/wiki/Sugar_Ray_Leonard" title="Sugar Ray Leonard">Sugar Ray Leonard</a>, who went on to an impressive professional career.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-6" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-6"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>6<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading4"><h4 id="Olympic_Champions">Olympic Champions</h4><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Light_welterweight&amp;action=edit&amp;section=8" 2026-02-26 13:10:13 | INFO     | Scraping: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vernon_Forrest
2026-02-26 13:10:14 | DEBUG    | Scraped content: ScrapedContent(url='https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vernon_Forrest', title='Vernon Forrest - Wikipedia', text='From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia American boxer Vernon Forrest Personal information Nickname The Viper Born ( 1971-02-12 ) February 12, 1971 Augusta, Georgia , U.S. Died July 25, 2009 (2009-07-25) (aged\xa038) Atlanta, Georgia , U.S. Height 6\xa0ft (183\xa0cm) [ 1 ] Weight Light welterweight Welterweight Light middleweight Boxing career Reach 72 + 1 ⁄ 2 in (184\xa0cm) [ 1 ] Stance Orthodox Boxing record Total\xa0fights 45 Wins 41 Win\xa0by\xa0KO 29 Losses 3 No\xa0contests 1 Medal record Men\'s amateur boxing Representing United States World Championships 1991 Sydney Light welterweight Vernon Forrest (February 12, 1971 – July 25, 2009) was an American professional boxer who competed from 1992 to 2008. He held multiple world championships in two weight classes , including the WBC , IBF , Ring magazine and lineal welterweight between 2002 and 2003, and the WBC super welterweight title twice between 2007 and 2009. In 2002, Forrest was named Fighter of the Year by The Ring and the Boxing Writers Association of America . In 2009, Forrest was murdered after he was robbed at a gas station in the Mechanicsville neighborhood of Atlanta, Georgia . Early years and amateur career [ edit ] A native of Augusta, Georgia , Forrest began boxing at the age of 9. After compiling an impressive 225–16 record as an amateur, he became the 1992 US junior welterweight champion, and won silver at the 1991 World Amateur Boxing Championships , losing in the finals to Kostya Tszyu . [ 2 ] Forrest was the first in his family to graduate from high school receiving his diploma from Marquette Senior High School in Marquette, Michigan .  Staying in Marquette, Forrest was on scholarship to Northern Michigan University where he majored in business administration through the U.S. Olympic Education Center. Forrest continued to train with the US National Team under head coach Al Mitchell . [ 2 ] He was a member of the 1992 US Olympic Team during the Summer Olympics in Barcelona, Spain . [ 2 ] He earned his Olympic position by beating Shane Mosley in the trials. After that fight, Forrest was the gold medal favorite heading into the tournament. He would have to fight Cuban fighter Hector Vinent , a gold medallist, before reaching that goal. However, he was stricken with food poisoning a day before his first round bout and was beaten by Peter Richardson , who he\'d previously defeated in a fight at the 1991 World Amateur Boxing Championships en route to winning the silver medal. He returned home to Augusta, then moved to Las Vegas , and made his professional debut on November 25, 1992. Professional career [ edit ] In his professional debut in November 1992, Forrest defeated Charles Hawkins. Through 1996, Forrest stopped 13 out of 15 opponents. Five were stopped in the first round. Welterweight [ edit ] As the years went by Forrest won a few minor title belts. In the year 2000 Forrest finally got his chance to fight for a major title belt against Raul Frank (for the IBF welterweight title). Unfortunately for Forrest however, a cut caused by an accidental head butt ended the bout in round three and the fight was ruled a no contest. IBF welterweight champion [ edit ] Main article: Raul Frank vs. Vernon Forrest II Forrest met Frank again in a rematch at Madison Square Garden on May 12, 2001, on a Félix Trinidad undercard . Forrest dominated his opponent and won the fight by a unanimous decision to claim his first major professional boxing title. Forrest vs Mosley I [ edit ] Main article: Shane Mosley vs. Vernon Forrest In 2001, Forrest fought the WBC and lineal welterweight champion, Shane Mosley . [ 3 ] Many considered Mosley to be the best fighter in the world, and he was the betting favorite to win the fight.  Despite being the favorite, Mosley was dominated in this bout. Both fighters initially started strong, landing hard blows, but in the second round Forrest had Mosley hurt early and knocked him down for the first time in his career.  A series of strong punches would put him down yet again later in the round.  With his dominant performance, Forrest was also awarded the Ring Magazine welterweight title. Forrest vs Mosley II [ edit ] Main article: Vernon Forrest vs. Shane Mosley II Six months later, Forrest once again squared off against Mosley in a rematch. Despite a stronger performance from Mosley, Forrest won a clear cut decision, using his jab more effectively and through superior ring generalship. Forrest was now considered by many to be one of the top fighters in the world. Forrest vs. Mayorga I [ edit ] Main article: Vernon Forrest vs. Ricardo Mayorga In January 2003, Forrest fought the WBA welterweight champion, Ricardo Mayorga .  Mayorga was a mostly unknown fringe contender from Nicaragua and few gave him a chance to win against the significantly bigger and stronger Forrest.  Mayorga shocked the world when he easily dominated Forrest, dropping him once in the first round and again in the third round.  The referee would call off the fight after the second knockdown, as Forrest was visibly dazed and unable to get his footing. Forrest vs. Mayorga II [ edit ] Main article: Ricardo Mayorga vs. Vernon Forrest II Forrest would rematch Mayorga six months later, losing again, this time by a majority decision.  The bout was close and competitive, with Mayorga mostly chasing Forrest around the ring while Forrest was content to fight from the outside. Light middleweight [ edit ] Comeback trail [ edit ] Forrest took two years off from fighting because of injuries; Forrest had complete reconstructive surgery on his left arm. He had three surgeries two on his shoulder to repair a torn rotator cuff and one on his left elbow to repair torn cartilage and nerve damages. In his first fight since losing twice to Mayorga, Forrest knocked out Sergio Rios in two rounds. After the fight against Rios, Forrest stopped Elco Garcia in the tenth round. Forrest won a controversial ten round unanimous decision over Ike Quartey on August 5, 2006, at Madison Square Theatre, New York City. The judges at ringside scored the fight, 95–94, 95–94, and 96–93. [ 4 ] WBC Light middleweight champion [ edit ] On July 28, 2007, Forrest won a unanimous decision against Carlos Baldomir in Tacoma, Washington , frequently firing off heavy right blows at Baldomir. After twelve rounds, Forrest won a lopsided 118–109, 116–111, 118–109 decision to take the vacant WBC light middleweight title. On December 1, 2007, at Foxwoods Resort Casino , he successfully defended his light middleweight title against Italian Michele Piccirillo , scoring an eleventh-round TKO. Forrest vs. Mora [ edit ] On June 7, 2008, Forrest lost his title to The Contender winner Sergio Mora via a 12-round majority decision. In the build-up to the fight, Forrest referred to Mora as "the pretender" and threatened to send him "out on a stretcher". [ 5 ] However, Mora succeeded in pulling off the upset victory. [ 6 ] The final scores were 114–114, 115–113 and 116–112 in favor of Mora. [ 7 ] [ 8 ] Reclaiming the title [ edit ] Forrest reclaimed his WBC 154-pound title on September 14, 2008, against Sergio Mora via unanimous decision, the judges scores were 118–109, 117–110, and 119–110. [ 9 ] Charity work [ edit ] Forrest was involved directly with the creation of the Not for Profit Destiny\'s Child, a group home that assists people with developmental, emotional, and psychological disabilities and needs. [ 10 ] Forrest was also involved directly with helping the clients by organizing Destiny\'s Child\'s activities. [ 11 ] Murder [ edit ] At about 11:00\xa0pm EDT on July 25, 2009, Forrest stopped at a gas station in the Atlanta neighborhood of Mechanicsville . [ 12 ] With him was his 11-year-old godson. As the boy went inside the gas station, Forrest went to the back of his car to add air to a low tire. As this occurred, a man robbed him at gunpoint and fled. Forrest, who was armed, went after the man and shots were exchanged. After a short distance, Forrest gave up the chase and began talking to a second man. It was this man that shot Forrest seven to eight times in the back. According to police, the shooter and a second person left the scene in a red Pontiac. [ 13 ] Forrest died at the scene and the death was ruled a homicide. Atlanta Police would arrest and later charge 25-year-old Jquante Crews, 20-year-old Demario Ware and 30-year-old Charman Sinkfield for his murder. It is believed that Sinkfield was the shooter, Ware was the robber, and Crews was the driver. [ 14 ] Crews and Ware are serving life sentences. (Georgia Department of Corrections). On October 28, 2016, Charman Sinkfield was sentenced to life without parole. class="country-name"><span class="flagicon"><span class="mw-image-border" typeof="mw:File"><span><img alt="" welterweight\n</td></tr></tbody></table>\n</div></div></th></tr></tbody></table>\n<p><b>Vernon Forrest</b> (February 12, 1971 – July 25, 2009) was an American <a href="/wiki/Professional_boxer" class="mw-redirect" title="Professional boxer">professional boxer</a> who competed from 1992 to 2008. He held multiple world championships in two <a href="/wiki/Weight_class_(boxing)" title="Weight class (boxing)">weight classes</a>, including the <a href="/wiki/World_Boxing_Council" title="World Boxing Council">WBC</a>, <a href="/wiki/International_Boxing_Federation" title="International Boxing Federation">IBF</a>, <i><a href="/wiki/The_Ring_(magazine)" title="The Ring (magazine)">Ring</a></i> magazine and <a href="/wiki/Lineal_championship" title="Lineal championship">lineal</a> <a href="/wiki/Welterweight" title="Welterweight">welterweight</a> between 2002 and 2003, and the WBC <a href="/wiki/Super_welterweight" class="mw-redirect" title="Super welterweight">super welterweight</a> title twice between 2007 and 2009. In 2002, Forrest was named Fighter of the Year by <i><a href="/wiki/The_Ring_magazine_Fighter_of_the_Year" title="The Ring magazine Fighter of the Year">The Ring</a></i> and the <a href="/wiki/Sugar_Ray_Robinson_Award" title="Sugar Ray Robinson Award">Boxing Writers Association of America</a>.\n</p><p>In 2009, Forrest was murdered after he was robbed at a gas station in the <a href="/wiki/Mechanicsville_(Atlanta)" class="mw-redirect" title="Mechanicsville (Atlanta)">Mechanicsville</a> neighborhood of <a href="/wiki/Atlanta,_Georgia" class="mw-redirect" title="Atlanta, Georgia">Atlanta, Georgia</a>.\n</p>\n<meta property="mw:PageProp/toc" />\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Early_years_and_amateur_career">Early years and amateur career</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Vernon_Forrest&amp;action=edit&amp;section=1" title="Edit section: Early years and amateur career"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<p>A native of <a href="/wiki/Augusta,_Georgia" title="Augusta, Georgia">Augusta, Georgia</a>, Forrest began boxing at the age of 9. After compiling an impressive 225–16 record as an amateur, he became the 1992 <a href="/wiki/United_States_national_amateur_boxing_championships" title="United States national amateur boxing championships">US junior welterweight</a> champion, and won silver at the <a href="/wiki/1991_World_Amateur_Boxing_Championships" title="1991 World Amateur Boxing Championships">1991 World Amateur Boxing Championships</a>, losing in the finals to <a href="/wiki/Kostya_Tszyu" title="Kostya Tszyu">Kostya Tszyu</a>.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-HBO&#95;2-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-HBO-2"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Forrest was the first in his family to graduate from high school receiving his diploma from <a href="/wiki/Marquette_Senior_High_School" title="Marquette Senior High School">Marquette Senior High School</a> in <a href="/wiki/Marquette,_Michigan" title="Marquette, Michigan">Marquette, Michigan</a>.  Staying in Marquette, Forrest was on scholarship to <a href="/wiki/Northern_Michigan_University" title="Northern Michigan University">Northern Michigan University</a> where he majored in <a href="/wiki/Business_administration" title="Business administration">business administration</a> through the U.S. Olympic Education Center. Forrest continued to train with the US National Team under head coach <a href="/wiki/Al_Mitchell" title="Al Mitchell">Al Mitchell</a>.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-HBO&#95;2-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-HBO-2"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>He was a member of the <a href="/wiki/Boxing_at_the_1992_Summer_Olympics" title="Boxing at the 1992 Summer Olympics">1992 US Olympic Team</a> during the Summer Olympics in <a href="/wiki/Barcelona,_Spain" class="mw-redirect" title="Barcelona, Spain">Barcelona, Spain</a>.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-HBO&#95;2-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-HBO-2"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> He earned his Olympic position by beating <a href="/wiki/Shane_Mosley" title="Shane Mosley">Shane Mosley</a> in the trials. After that fight, Forrest was the <a href="/wiki/Gold_medal" title="Gold medal">gold medal</a> favorite heading into the tournament. He would have to fight Cuban fighter <a href="/wiki/Hector_Vinent" class="mw-redirect" title="Hector Vinent">Hector Vinent</a>, a gold medallist, before reaching that goal. However, he was stricken with <a href="/wiki/Food_poisoning" class="mw-redirect" title="Food poisoning">food poisoning</a> a day before his first round bout and was beaten by <a href="/wiki/Peter_Richardson_(boxer)" title="Peter Richardson (boxer)">Peter Richardson</a>, who he\'d previously defeated in a fight at the <a href="/wiki/1991_World_Amateur_Boxing_Championships" title="1991 World Amateur Boxing Championships">1991 World Amateur Boxing Championships</a> en route to winning the silver medal. He returned home to Augusta, then moved to <a href="/wiki/Las_Vegas_Valley" title="Las Vegas Valley">Las Vegas</a>, and made his professional debut on November 25, 1992.\n</p>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Professional_career">Professional career</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Vernon_Forrest&amp;action=edit&amp;section=2" title="Edit section: Professional career"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<p>In his professional debut in November 1992, Forrest defeated Charles Hawkins. Through 1996, Forrest stopped 13 out of 15 opponents. Five were stopped in the first round.\n</p>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Welterweight">Welterweight</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Vernon_Forrest&amp;action=edit&amp;section=3" title="Edit section: Welterweight"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<p>As the years went by Forrest won a few minor title belts. In the year 2000 Forrest finally got his chance to fight for a major title belt against Raul Frank (for the <a href="/wiki/International_Boxing_Federation" title="International Boxing Federation">IBF</a> welterweight title). Unfortunately for Forrest however, a cut caused by an accidental head butt ended the bout in round three and the fight was ruled a no contest.\n</p>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading4"><h4 id="IBF_welterweight_champion">IBF welterweight champion</h4><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Vernon_Forrest&amp;action=edit&amp;section=4" title="Edit section: IBF welterweight champion"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<style data-mw-deduplicate="TemplateStyles:r1320445320">.mw-parser-output .hatnote{font-style:italic}.mw-parser-output div.hatnote{padding-left:1.6em;margin-bottom:0.5em}.mw-parser-output .hatnote i{font-style:normal}.mw-parser-output .hatnote+link+.hatnote{margin-top:-0.5em}@media print{body.ns-0 .mw-parser-output .hatnote{display:none!important}}</style><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Raul_Frank_vs._Vernon_Forrest_II" class="mw-redirect" title="Raul Frank vs. Vernon Forrest II">Raul Frank vs. Vernon Forrest II</a></div>\n<p>Forrest met Frank again in a rematch at <a href="/wiki/Madison_Square_Garden" title="Madison Square Garden">Madison Square Garden</a> on May 12, 2001, on a <a href="/wiki/F%C3%A9lix_Trinidad" title="Félix Trinidad">Félix Trinidad</a> <a href="/wiki/William_Joppy_vs._F%C3%A9lix_Trinidad" title="William Joppy vs. Félix Trinidad">undercard</a>. Forrest dominated his opponent and won the fight by a <a href="/wiki/Unanimous_decision" title="Unanimous decision">unanimous decision</a> to claim his first major professional boxing title.\n</p>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading4"><h4 id="Forrest_vs_Mosley_I">Forrest vs Mosley I</h4><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Vernon_Forrest&amp;action=edit&amp;section=5" title="Edit section: Forrest vs Mosley I"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1320445320" /><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Shane_Mosley_vs._Vernon_Forrest" title="Shane Mosley vs. Vernon Forrest">Shane Mosley vs. Vernon Forrest</a></div>\n<p>In 2001, Forrest fought the <a href="/wiki/World_Boxing_Council" title="World Boxing Council">WBC</a> and lineal welterweight champion, <a href="/wiki/Shane_Mosley" title="Shane Mosley">Shane Mosley</a>.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-3"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>3<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Many considered Mosley to be the best fighter in the world, and he was the betting favorite to win the fight.  Despite being the favorite, Mosley was dominated in this bout. Both fighters initially started strong, landing hard blows, but in the second round Forrest had Mosley hurt early and knocked him down for the first time in his career.  A series of strong punches would put him down yet again later in the round.  With his dominant performance, Forrest was also awarded the Ring Magazine welterweight title.\n</p>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading4"><h4 id="Forrest_vs_Mosley_II">Forrest vs Mosley II</h4><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Vernon_Forrest&amp;action=edit&amp;section=6" title="Edit section: Forrest vs Mosley II"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1320445320" /><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Vernon_Forrest_vs._Shane_Mosley_II" title="Vernon Forrest vs. Shane Mosley II">Vernon Forrest vs. Shane Mosley II</a></div>\n<p>Six months later, Forrest once again squared off against Mosley in a rematch. Despite a stronger performance from Mosley, Forrest won a clear cut decision, using his jab more effectively and through superior ring generalship. Forrest was now considered by many to be one of the top fighters in the world.\n</p>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading4"><h4 id="Forrest_vs._Mayorga_I">Forrest vs. Mayorga I</h4><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Vernon_Forrest&amp;action=edit&amp;section=7" title="Edit section: Forrest vs. Mayorga I"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1320445320" /><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Vernon_Forrest_vs._Ricardo_Mayorga" title="Vernon Forrest vs. Ricardo Mayorga">Vernon Forrest vs. Ricardo Mayorga</a></div>\n<p>In January 2003, Forrest fought the <a href="/wiki/World_Boxing_Association" title="World Boxing Association">WBA</a> welterweight champion, <a href="/wiki/Ricardo_Mayorga" title="Ricardo Mayorga">Ricardo Mayorga</a>.  Mayorga was a mostly unknown fringe contender from Nicaragua and few gave him a chance to win against the significantly bigger and stronger Forrest.  Mayorga shocked the world when he easily dominated Forrest, dropping him once in the first round and again in the third round.  The referee would call off the fight after the second knockdown, as Forrest was visibly dazed and unable to get his footing.\n</p>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading4"><h4 id="Forrest_vs._Mayorga_II">Forrest vs. Mayorga II</h4><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Vernon_Forrest&amp;action=edit&amp;section=8" title="Edit section: Forrest vs. Mayorga II"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1320445320" /><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Ricardo_Mayorga_vs._Vernon_Forrest_II" title="Ricardo Mayorga vs. Vernon Forrest II">Ricardo Mayorga vs. Vernon Forrest II</a></div>\n<p>Forrest would rematch Mayorga six months later, losing again, this time by a majority decision.  The bout was close and competitive, with Mayorga mostly chasing Forrest around the ring while Forrest was content to fight from the outside.\n</p>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Light_middleweight">Light middleweight</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Vernon_Forrest&amp;action=edit&amp;section=9" title="Edit section: Light middleweight"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading4"><h4 id="Comeback_trail">Comeback trail</h4><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Vernon_Forrest&amp;action=edit&amp;section=10" title="Edit section: Comeback trail"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<p>Forrest took two years off from fighting because of injuries; Forrest had complete <a href="/wiki/Reconstructive_surgery" title="Reconstructive surgery">reconstructive surgery</a> on his left arm. He had three surgeries two on his shoulder to repair a <a href="/wiki/Rotator_cuff_tear" title="Rotator cuff tear">torn rotator cuff</a> and one on his left elbow to repair torn cartilage and nerve damages.\n</p><p>In his first fight since losing twice to Mayorga, Forrest knocked out Sergio Rios in two rounds. After the fight against Rios, Forrest stopped Elco Garcia in the tenth round.\n</p><p>Forrest won a controversial ten round unanimous decision over <a href="/wiki/Ike_Quartey" title="Ike Quartey">Ike Quartey</a> on August 5, 2006, at Madison Square Theatre, New York City. The judges at ringside scored the fight, 95–94, 95–94, and 96–93.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-4" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-4"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>4<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading4"><h4 id="WBC_Light_middleweight_champion">WBC Light middleweight champion</h4><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Vernon_Forrest&amp;action=edit&amp;section=11" title="Edit section: WBC Light middleweight champion"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<p>On July 28, 2007, Forrest won a unanimous decision against <a href="/wiki/Carlos_Baldomir" title="Carlos Baldomir">Carlos Baldomir</a> in <a href="/wiki/Tacoma,_Washington" title="Tacoma, Washington">Tacoma, Washington</a>, frequently firing off heavy right blows at Baldomir. After twelve rounds, Forrest won a lopsided 118–109, 116–111, 118–109 decision to take the vacant WBC light middleweight title.\n</p><p>On December 1, 2007, at <a href="/wiki/Foxwoods_Resort_Casino" title="Foxwoods Resort Casino">Foxwoods Resort Casino</a>, he successfully defended his light middleweight title against Italian <a href="/wiki/Michele_Piccirillo" title="Michele Piccirillo">Michele Piccirillo</a>, scoring an eleventh-round TKO.\n</p>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading4"><h4 id="Forrest_vs._Mora">Forrest vs. Mora</h4><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Vernon_Forrest&amp;action=edit&amp;section=12" title="Edit section: Forrest vs. Mora"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<p>On June 7, 2008, Forrest lost his title to <i><a href="/wiki/The_Contender_(TV_series)" title="The Contender (TV series)">The Contender</a></i> winner <a href="/wiki/Sergio_Mora" title="Sergio Mora">Sergio Mora</a> via a 12-round majority decision. In the build-up to the fight, Forrest referred to Mora as "the pretender" and threatened to send him "out on a stretcher".<sup id="cite&#95;ref-5" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-5"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>5<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> However, Mora succeeded in pulling off the upset victory.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-6" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-6"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>6<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> The final scores were 114–114, 115–113 and 116–112 in favor of Mora.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-7" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-7"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>7<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-8" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-8"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>8<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading4"><h4 id="Reclaiming_the_title">Reclaiming the title</h4><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Vernon_Forrest&amp;action=edit&amp;section=13" title="Edit section: Reclaiming the title"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<p>Forrest reclaimed his WBC 154-pound title on September 14, 2008, against <a href="/wiki/Sergio_Mora" title="Sergio Mora">Sergio Mora</a> via unanimous decision, the judges scores were 118–109, 117–110, and 119–110.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-9" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-9"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>9<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Charity_work">Charity work</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Vernon_Forrest&amp;action=edit&amp;section=14" title="Edit section: Charity work"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<p>Forrest was involved directly with the creation of the <a href="/wiki/Not_for_Profit" class="mw-redirect" title="Not for Profit">Not for Profit</a> Destiny\'s Child, a group home that assists people with developmental, emotional, and psychological disabilities and needs.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-dc&#95;10-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-dc-10"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>10<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Forrest was also involved directly with helping the clients by organizing Destiny\'s Child\'s activities.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-cnn&#95;11-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-cnn-11"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>11<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Murder">Murder</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Vernon_Forrest&amp;action=edit&amp;section=15" title="Edit section: Murder"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<p>At about 11:00&#160;pm <a href="/wiki/Eastern_Time_Zone" title="Eastern Time Zone">EDT</a> on July 25, 2009, Forrest stopped at a gas station in the <a href="/wiki/Atlanta" title="Atlanta">Atlanta</a> neighborhood of <a href="/wiki/Mechanicsville_(Atlanta)" class="mw-redirect" title="Mechanicsville (Atlanta)">Mechanicsville</a>.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-12" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-12"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>12<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> With him was his 11-year-old godson. As the boy went inside the gas station, Forrest went to the back of his car to add air to a low tire. As this occurred, a man robbed him at gunpoint and fled. Forrest, who was armed, went after the man and shots were exchanged. After a short distance, Forrest gave up the chase and began talking to a second man. It was this man that shot Forrest seven to eight times in the back. According to police, the shooter and a second person left the scene in a red Pontiac.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-13" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-13"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>13<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Forrest died at the scene and the death was ruled a homicide. Atlanta Police would arrest and later charge 25-year-old Jquante Crews, 20-year-old Demario Ware and 30-year-old Charman Sinkfield for his murder. It is believed that Sinkfield was the shooter, Ware was the robber, and Crews was the driver.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-14" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-14"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>14<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Crews and Ware are serving life sentences. (Georgia Department of Corrections). On October 28, 2016, Charman Sinkfield was sentenced to life without parole.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-15" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-15"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>15<span 2026-02-26 13:10:15 | DEBUG    | Scraped content: ScrapedContent(url='https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josh_Kelly_(boxer)', title='Josh Kelly (boxer) - Wikipedia', text='From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia British boxer (born 1994) For other people named Josh Kelly, see Josh Kelly (disambiguation) . Josh Kelly Personal information Nickname Pretty Boy [ 2 ] Born Joshua Kelly ( 1994-03-07 ) 7 March 1994 (age\xa031) Sunderland , England Height 5\xa0ft 10\xa0in (178\xa0cm) [ 1 ] Weight Welterweight Light middleweight Boxing career Reach 72\xa0in (183\xa0cm) [ 1 ] Stance Orthodox Boxing record Total\xa0fights 20 Wins 18 Win\xa0by\xa0KO 9 Losses 1 Draws 1 Medal record Men\'s Amateur boxing Representing United Kingdom European Games 2015 Baku Welterweight Joshua "Josh" Kelly (born 7 March 1994) is an English professional boxer who has held the IBF light-middleweight title since January 2026. He is a former British light-middleweight and Commonwealth welterweight title holder. As an amateur he competed in the men\'s welterweight event at the 2016 Summer Olympics and the 2015 European Games , in which he won a bronze medal. Amateur career [ edit ] Representing Great Britain, Kelly won a bronze medal in the 69kg category at the 2015 European Games in Azerbaijan, losing in the semi-finals to the host nation\'s eventual champion Parviz Baghirov . [ 3 ] The following year he was selected for the Rio Olympics , where he lost in the round-of-16 to Kazakhstan\'s Daniyar Yeleussinov who went on to win the gold medal. [ 4 ] Professional career [ edit ] Kelly\'s first fight as a professional was a six rounds points victory (59–55) against Jay Byrne (4–1) of Dublin in April 2017 at the SSE Hydro in Glasgow on the undercard of Ricky Burns vs. Julius Indongo . [ 5 ] Kelly won his next two fights in the next two months, defeating Spain\'s Jony Vila (6–1) and Gateshead \'s Tom Whitfield (4–1) by fourth-round stoppage and first-round knockout respectively. [ 6 ] [ 7 ] The Vila fight took place at the Barclaycard Arena , Birmingham in May whilst the Whitfield fight took place at the Walker Activity Dome, Newcastle in June, with his fight being the main event. [ 8 ] [ 9 ] Kelly finished the year with a record of 5–0 after victories over Mexico\'s Jose Luis Zuniga (13–2–1) and France\'s Jean Michel Hamilcaro (25–8–3), winning by second-round stoppage and sixth-round stoppage respectively in October and December. Those fights took place at the SSE Arena, Belfast and the York Hall , London . [ citation needed ] Kelly vs. Robinson [ edit ] On June 1, 2019, Kelly fought Ray Robinson, who was ranked #13 by the WBC and #15 by the WBO at welterweight. Kelly was ranked #9 by the WBA at welterweight. The contest was even and ended up in a majority draw, with one scorecard going in favour of Kelly, 96–94, while the other two read 95–95 twice. [ 10 ] Kelly vs. Campos [ edit ] In his next fight, Kelly fought Wiston Campos. Kelly won the bout via unanimous decision. The scorecards read 99–90, 99–90 and 98–91. [ 11 ] Kelly vs. Avanesyan [ edit ] In his next fight, Kelly fought highly ranked welterweight and reigning European Champion David Avanesyan , who was ranked #6 by the IBF , #7 by the WBC, #9 by the WBA and #10 by the WBO at the time. Avanesyan showed to be the better man on the night and finished Kelly within six rounds. [ 12 ] [ 13 ] Kelly vs. Williamson [ edit ] Kelly won the British light-middleweight title by beating defending champion Troy Williamson by unanimous decision at Newcastle Arena on 2 December 2022. [ 14 ] Kelly vs. Davis [ edit ] Kelly was scheduled to face Liam Smith at Wembley Stadium in London, England on 21 September 2024. [ 15 ] On September 13, 2024 it was reported that the latter withdrew due to illness. [ 16 ] On 16 September 2024 it was announced that Smith was replaced by Ishmael Davis . [ 17 ] Kelly won by majority decision winning the two judges awarding the fight to him and the third scoring it as a draw. [ 18 ] Kelly vs. Biea [ edit ] At Newcastle Arena on 6 June 2025, he defeated Flavius Biea by first-round stoppage. Kelly knocked his opponent to the canvas and, although Biea got back to his feet, the referee decided he was not fit to continue and waved off the contest. [ 19 ] Kelly vs. Murtazaliev [ edit ] Kelly challenged IBF light-middleweight champion Bakhram Murtazaliev at Newcastle Arena on 31 January 2026. [ 20 ] [ 21 ] Throughout the fight, Kelly fought off of the backfoot, scoring countershots as Murtazaliev attempted to pressure him and force him against the ropes with hard shots. In the fourth round, Kelly scored a knockdown, while Murtazaliev returned the favor in the ninth. After 12 rounds, Kelly won the world title via majority decision, with judges scorecards of 115–111, 114–113, and the third scoring it a 113–113 draw, thus becoming the first boxer from Sunderland to become a world champion. style="text-align:center;vertical-align:middle;color:inherit;"><span typeof="mw:File"><span title="Bronze medal – third place"><img alt="Bronze medal – third place" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/60/Bronze_medal_icon_%28B_initial%29.svg/40px-Bronze_medal_icon_%28B_initial%29.svg.png 1.5x" data-file-width="16" Baku</a></span></td>\n<td style="text-align:center;vertical-align:middle;"><a href="/wiki/Boxing_at_the_2015_European_Games_%E2%80%93_Men%27s_69_kg" title="Boxing at the 2015 European Games – Men&#39;s 69 kg">Welterweight</a>\n</td></tr></tbody></table>\n</div></div></th></tr></tbody></table>\n<p><b>Joshua "Josh" Kelly</b> (born 7 March 1994) is an English <a href="/wiki/Professional_boxer" class="mw-redirect" title="Professional boxer">professional boxer</a> who has held the <a href="/wiki/International_Boxing_Federation" title="International Boxing Federation">IBF</a> <a href="/wiki/Light-middleweight" class="mw-redirect" title="Light-middleweight">light-middleweight</a> title since January 2026. He is a former <a href="/wiki/British_Boxing_Board_of_Control" title="British Boxing Board of Control">British</a> <a href="/wiki/Light-middleweight" class="mw-redirect" title="Light-middleweight">light-middleweight</a> and <a href="/wiki/Commonwealth_Boxing_Council" title="Commonwealth Boxing Council">Commonwealth</a> <a href="/wiki/Welterweight" title="Welterweight">welterweight</a> title holder. As an amateur he competed in the <a href="/wiki/Boxing_at_the_2016_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Men%27s_welterweight" title="Boxing at the 2016 Summer Olympics – Men&#39;s welterweight">men\'s welterweight</a> event at the <a href="/wiki/2016_Summer_Olympics" title="2016 Summer Olympics">2016 Summer Olympics</a> and the <a href="/wiki/2015_European_Games" title="2015 European Games">2015 European Games</a>, in which he won a bronze medal.\n</p>\n<meta property="mw:PageProp/toc" />\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Amateur_career">Amateur career</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Josh_Kelly_(boxer)&amp;action=edit&amp;section=1" title="Edit section: Amateur career"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<p>Representing Great Britain, Kelly won a bronze medal in the 69kg category at the <a href="/wiki/Boxing_at_the_2015_European_Games_%E2%80%93_Men%27s_69_kg" title="Boxing at the 2015 European Games – Men&#39;s 69 kg">2015 European Games</a> in Azerbaijan, losing in the semi-finals to the host nation\'s eventual champion <a href="/wiki/Parviz_Baghirov" title="Parviz Baghirov">Parviz Baghirov</a>.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-3"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>3<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>The following year he was selected for the <a href="/wiki/Boxing_at_the_2016_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Men%27s_welterweight" title="Boxing at the 2016 Summer Olympics – Men&#39;s welterweight">Rio Olympics</a>, where he lost in the round-of-16 to Kazakhstan\'s <a href="/wiki/Daniyar_Yeleussinov" title="Daniyar Yeleussinov">Daniyar Yeleussinov</a> who went on to win the gold medal.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-4" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-4"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>4<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Professional_career">Professional career</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Josh_Kelly_(boxer)&amp;action=edit&amp;section=2" title="Edit section: Professional career"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<p>Kelly\'s first fight as a professional was a six rounds points victory (59–55) against Jay Byrne (4–1) of <a href="/wiki/Dublin" title="Dublin">Dublin</a> in April 2017 at the <a href="/wiki/SSE_Hydro" class="mw-redirect" title="SSE Hydro">SSE Hydro</a> in <a href="/wiki/Glasgow" title="Glasgow">Glasgow</a> on the undercard of <a href="/wiki/Ricky_Burns" title="Ricky Burns">Ricky Burns</a> vs. <a href="/wiki/Julius_Indongo" title="Julius Indongo">Julius Indongo</a>.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-5" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-5"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>5<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>Kelly won his next two fights in the next two months, defeating Spain\'s Jony Vila (6–1) and <a href="/wiki/Gateshead" title="Gateshead">Gateshead</a>\'s Tom Whitfield (4–1) by fourth-round stoppage and first-round knockout respectively.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-6" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-6"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>6<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-7" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-7"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>7<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> The Vila fight took place at the <a href="/wiki/Barclaycard_Arena" class="mw-redirect" title="Barclaycard Arena">Barclaycard Arena</a>, <a href="/wiki/Birmingham" title="Birmingham">Birmingham</a> in May whilst the Whitfield fight took place at the Walker Activity Dome, <a href="/wiki/Newcastle_United_F.C." title="Newcastle United F.C.">Newcastle</a> in June, with his fight being the main event.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-8" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-8"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>8<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-9" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-9"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>9<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>Kelly finished the year with a record of 5–0 after victories over Mexico\'s Jose Luis Zuniga (13–2–1) and France\'s Jean Michel Hamilcaro (25–8–3), winning by second-round stoppage and sixth-round stoppage respectively in October and December. Those fights took place at the <a href="/wiki/SSE_Arena,_Belfast" class="mw-redirect" title="SSE Arena, Belfast">SSE Arena, Belfast</a> and the <a href="/wiki/York_Hall" title="York Hall">York Hall</a>, <a href="/wiki/London" title="London">London</a>.<sup class="noprint Inline-Template Template-Fact" style="white-space:nowrap;">&#91;<i><a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed" title="Wikipedia:Citation needed"><span title="This claim needs references to reliable sources. (September 2025)">citation needed</span></a></i>&#93;</sup>\n</p>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Kelly_vs._Robinson">Kelly vs. Robinson</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Josh_Kelly_(boxer)&amp;action=edit&amp;section=3" title="Edit section: Kelly vs. Robinson"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<p>On June 1, 2019, Kelly fought Ray Robinson, who was ranked #13 by the <a href="/wiki/World_Boxing_Council" title="World Boxing Council">WBC</a> and #15 by the <a href="/wiki/World_Boxing_Organization" title="World Boxing Organization">WBO</a> at welterweight. Kelly was ranked #9 by the <a href="/wiki/World_Boxing_Association" title="World Boxing Association">WBA</a> at welterweight. The contest was even and ended up in a majority draw, with one scorecard going in favour of Kelly, 96–94, while the other two read 95–95 twice.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-10" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-10"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>10<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Kelly_vs._Campos">Kelly vs. Campos</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Josh_Kelly_(boxer)&amp;action=edit&amp;section=4" title="Edit section: Kelly vs. Campos"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<p>In his next fight, Kelly fought Wiston Campos. Kelly won the bout via unanimous decision. The scorecards read 99–90, 99–90 and 98–91.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-11" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-11"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>11<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Kelly_vs._Avanesyan">Kelly vs. Avanesyan</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Josh_Kelly_(boxer)&amp;action=edit&amp;section=5" title="Edit section: Kelly vs. Avanesyan"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<p>In his next fight, Kelly fought highly ranked welterweight and reigning European Champion <a href="/wiki/David_Avanesyan" title="David Avanesyan">David Avanesyan</a>, who was ranked #6 by the <a href="/wiki/International_Boxing_Federation" title="International Boxing Federation">IBF</a>, #7 by the WBC, #9 by the WBA and #10 by the WBO at the time. Avanesyan showed to be the better man on the night and finished Kelly within six rounds.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-12" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-12"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>12<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-13" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-13"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>13<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Kelly_vs._Williamson">Kelly vs. Williamson</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Josh_Kelly_(boxer)&amp;action=edit&amp;section=6" title="Edit section: Kelly vs. Williamson"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<p>Kelly won the <a href="/wiki/British_Boxing_Board_of_Control" title="British Boxing Board of Control">British</a> <a href="/wiki/Light-middleweight" class="mw-redirect" title="Light-middleweight">light-middleweight</a> title by beating defending champion <a href="/wiki/Troy_Williamson_(boxer)" title="Troy Williamson (boxer)">Troy Williamson</a> by unanimous decision at <a href="/wiki/Newcastle_Arena" title="Newcastle Arena">Newcastle Arena</a> on 2 December 2022.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-14" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-14"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>14<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Kelly_vs._Davis">Kelly vs. Davis</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Josh_Kelly_(boxer)&amp;action=edit&amp;section=7" title="Edit section: Kelly vs. Davis"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<p>Kelly was scheduled to face <a href="/wiki/Liam_Smith_(boxer)" title="Liam Smith (boxer)">Liam Smith</a> at <a href="/wiki/Wembley_Stadium" title="Wembley Stadium">Wembley Stadium</a> in London, England on 21 September 2024.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-15" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-15"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>15<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> On September 13, 2024 it was reported that the latter withdrew due to illness.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-16" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-16"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>16<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> On 16 September 2024 it was announced that Smith was replaced by <a href="/wiki/Ishmael_Davis" title="Ishmael Davis">Ishmael Davis</a>.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-17" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-17"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>17<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Kelly won by majority decision winning the two judges awarding the fight to him and the third scoring it as a draw.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-18" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-18"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>18<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Kelly_vs._Biea">Kelly vs. Biea</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Josh_Kelly_(boxer)&amp;action=edit&amp;section=8" title="Edit section: Kelly vs. Biea"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<p>At Newcastle Arena on 6 June 2025, he defeated Flavius Biea by first-round stoppage. Kelly knocked his opponent to the canvas and, although Biea got back to his feet, the referee decided he was not fit to continue and waved off the contest.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-19" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-19"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>19<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Kelly_vs._Murtazaliev">Kelly vs. Murtazaliev</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Josh_Kelly_(boxer)&amp;action=edit&amp;section=9" title="Edit section: Kelly vs. Murtazaliev"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<p>Kelly challenged <a href="/wiki/International_Boxing_Federation" title="International Boxing Federation">IBF</a> <a href="/wiki/Light-middleweight" class="mw-redirect" title="Light-middleweight">light-middleweight</a> champion <a href="/wiki/Bakhram_Murtazaliev" title="Bakhram Murtazaliev">Bakhram Murtazaliev</a> at Newcastle Arena on 31 January 2026.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-20" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-20"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>20<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id="cite&#95;ref-21" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-21"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>21<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Throughout the fight, Kelly fought off of the backfoot, scoring countershots as Murtazaliev attempted to pressure him and force him against the ropes with hard shots. In the fourth round, Kelly scored a knockdown, while Murtazaliev returned the favor in the ninth. After 12 rounds, Kelly won the world title via majority decision, with judges scorecards of 115–111, 114–113, and the third scoring it a 113–113 draw, thus becoming the first boxer from <a href="/wiki/Sunderland" title="Sunderland">Sunderland</a> to become a world champion.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-22" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-22"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>22<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Professional_boxing_record">Professional boxing record</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span
