class="infobox-label">Structural system</th><td class="infobox-data category"><a href="/wiki/Concrete" title="Concrete">Concrete</a></td></tr><tr><th scope="row" class="infobox-label">Floor count</th><td class="infobox-data">52</td></tr><tr><th scope="row" class="infobox-label">Floor area</th><td class="infobox-data">135,000&#160;m<sup>2</sup> (1,450,000&#160;sq&#160;ft)</td></tr><tr><th colspan="2" class="infobox-header" style="background-color:#ededed;color:#000;">Design and construction</th></tr><tr><th scope="row" class="infobox-label">Architect</th><td class="infobox-data">Philippe Chiambaretta</td></tr><tr><th scope="row" class="infobox-label">Developer</th><td class="infobox-data">Redman</td></tr><tr><th scope="row" class="infobox-label">Main contractor</th><td class="infobox-data"><a href="/wiki/Vinci_SA" title="Vinci SA">Vinci SA</a></td></tr><tr><th colspan="2" class="infobox-header" style="background-color:#ededed;color:#000;">Website</th></tr><tr><td colspan="2" class="infobox-full-data"><span class="url"><a rel="nofollow" class="external text" href="http://thelink-ladefense.com">thelink-ladefense<wbr />.com</a></span></td></tr></tbody></table>\n<p><b>The Link</b> is a <a href="/wiki/Mixed-use" class="mw-redirect" title="Mixed-use">mixed-use</a> <a href="/wiki/Skyscraper" title="Skyscraper">skyscraper</a> <a href="/wiki/Tower_block" title="Tower block">building development</a> under construction in <a href="/wiki/Puteaux" title="Puteaux">Puteaux</a>, <a href="/wiki/France" title="France">France</a>. It will be part of the <a href="/wiki/La_D%C3%A9fense" title="La Défense">La Défense</a> business district. Completed in 2025, the tallest tower stands at 242&#160;m (794&#160;ft) tall with 52 floors, making it the tallest skyscraper in the Paris metropolitan area and in France, and the second tallest structure overall, after the <a href="/wiki/Eiffel_Tower" title="Eiffel Tower">Eiffel Tower</a>.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-2"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>The tower will house the new headquarters of French energy company <a href="/wiki/TotalEnergies" title="TotalEnergies">TotalEnergies</a>, which is currently located in <a href="/wiki/Tour_Total" title="Tour Total">Tour Total</a>.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-3"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>3<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p>\n<meta property="mw:PageProp/toc" />\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="History">History</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=The_Link_(building)&amp;action=edit&amp;section=1" title="Edit section: History"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<p>In July 2017, Total has chosen the Link tower to house its next headquarters. Between 5,500 and 6,000 employees, previously located in the Coupole and Michelet towers, will be grouped together in this new skyscraper.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-4" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-4"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>4<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> Its construction cost was estimated at one billion euros in October 2021.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-5" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-5"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>5<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>On June 11, 2020, <a href="/wiki/Groupama" title="Groupama">Groupama</a> announced the groundbreaking of The Link with the start of the demolition work on the existing building, which would be followed in 2021 by foundation work on the new towers.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-6" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-6"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>6<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Architecture">Architecture</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=The_Link_(building)&amp;action=edit&amp;section=2" title="Edit section: Architecture"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<p>The complex consists of two office towers called Arche and Seine, standing at 242 and 178 meters high respectively, connected by 35 platforms called "links", a term derived from the English "link" and meaning "connection". The tallest tower will house the new headquarters of <a href="/wiki/TotalEnergies" title="TotalEnergies">TotalEnergies</a>, currently located in the Coupole Tower.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-7" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-7"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>7<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>The Link project comprises approximately 130,000 m² of office space. It is located near a green space. The building includes duplex floors of approximately 6,000 m² and high ceilings, to allow internal pedestrian movement and limit the use of elevators.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-8" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-8"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>8<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>The tower, by its height and position, is designed to visually rebalance the historic <a href="/wiki/Axe_historique" title="Axe historique">Axe historique</a>.\n</p><p>The building features a double-skin insulating façade incorporating photovoltaic panels and aims to reduce energy consumption by 50% compared to the towers previously occupied by the company. Accessibility to the district from Puteaux is to be improved through the renovation of Cours Michelet.\n</p>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Gallery">Gallery</h2><span 2026-02-26 13:10:24 | DEBUG    | Scraped content: ScrapedContent(url='https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_tallest_buildings_and_structures_in_the_Paris_region', title='List of tallest buildings and structures in the Paris region - Wikipedia', text='From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia See also: List of tallest buildings in France , List of tallest buildings in Europe , and List of tallest structures in Europe The tallest structure in the city of Paris and the Île-de-France remains the Eiffel Tower in the 7th arrondissement , 330 meters high, completed in 1889 as the gateway to the 1889 Paris Universal Exposition. The tallest building in the Paris region is The Link , at 242 meters, located in La Défense . It is tied for eighth place among the tallest buildings in the European Union. The tallest building within the city limits of Paris is the Tour Montparnasse , 210 meters high. Tallest buildings and structures [ edit ] The Paris region has four of the tallest twenty-five buildings in the European Union: the tour Link, the Tour First, the Tour Hekla, and the Tour Montparnasse. As of 2025, there are 24 skyscrapers that reach a roof height of at least 150 metres (490\xa0ft). Most of the Paris region\'s high-rise buildings are located in three distinct areas: La Défense , located just west of the City of Paris in the département of the Hauts-de-Seine . Eight of the ten tallest buildings and structures in the region are located in La Defense. Italie 13 , located in the southern half of the 13th arrondissement : The 13th arrondissement towers are mostly residential, located in the south of the arrondissement , in what is today le Quartier chinois (Chinatown). Front de Seine , located in the 15th arrondissement : Most of the buildings of the Front de Seine , which is in close proximity to the Eiffel Tower , were built in the 1970s and 1980s and are of mixed commercial and residential use. The tallest building is the Tour Montparnasse . Other high-rise buildings are scattered throughout the Paris area, mainly in close proximity to the Périphérique freeway. These include Les Mercuriales in Bagnolet , the Tour Pleyel in Saint-Denis , and the Hôtel Hyatt Regency Paris Étoile in the city proper (near the Porte Maillot). However the tallest tower is built within central Paris: the iconic Eiffel Tower standing alongside the Seine River at the heart of the 7th arrondissement . Built in 1889, it was the first man-made structure in the world to exceed 1,000 feet. Paris , with the skyscrapers of La Défense in the background Towers in the 13th arrondissement The Front de Seine project in the 15th arrondissement This list ranks the Paris area buildings and structures that stand at least 100 meters tall. Structures proposed, approved, or under construction [ edit ] This is a list of structures that are either under construction or due to start construction soon. Structures are sorted by planned height.\nThe Authority managing La Défense , the EPAD, has launched several contests for new towers in a large scale operation of renovation of the business district. Other proposed projects are currently being talked about in other municipalities of the inner suburbs such as Issy-les-Moulineaux , Boulogne-Billancourt or Saint-Denis . class="vector-body" aria-labelledby="firstHeading" data-mw-ve-target-container>\n\t\t\t\t\t<div class="vector-body-before-content">\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t<div class="mw-indicators">\n\t\t</div>\n\n\t\t\t\t\t\t<div id="siteSub" class="noprint">From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia</div>\n\t\t\t\t\t</div>\n\t\t\t\t\t<div id="contentSub"><div id="mw-content-subtitle"></div></div>\n\t\t\t\t\t\n\t\t\t\t\t\n\t\t\t\t\t<div id="mw-content-text" class="mw-body-content"><div class="mw-subjectpageheader">\n</div><div class="mw-content-ltr mw-parser-output" lang="en" dir="ltr"><p class="mw-empty-elt">\n</p>\n<style data-mw-deduplicate="TemplateStyles:r1320445320">.mw-parser-output .hatnote{font-style:italic}.mw-parser-output div.hatnote{padding-left:1.6em;margin-bottom:0.5em}.mw-parser-output .hatnote i{font-style:normal}.mw-parser-output .hatnote+link+.hatnote{margin-top:-0.5em}@media print{body.ns-0 .mw-parser-output .hatnote{display:none!important}}</style><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">See also: <a href="/wiki/List_of_tallest_buildings_in_France" title="List of tallest buildings in France">List of tallest buildings in France</a>, <a href="/wiki/List_of_tallest_buildings_in_Europe" title="List of tallest buildings in Europe">List of tallest buildings in Europe</a>, and <a href="/wiki/List_of_tallest_structures_in_Europe" title="List of tallest structures in Europe">List of tallest structures in Europe</a></div>\n<p>The tallest structure in the city of <a href="/wiki/Paris" title="Paris">Paris</a> and the <a href="/wiki/%C3%8Ele-de-France" title="Île-de-France">Île-de-France</a> remains the <a href="/wiki/Eiffel_Tower" title="Eiffel Tower">Eiffel Tower</a> in the <a href="/wiki/7th_arrondissement_of_Paris" title="7th arrondissement of Paris">7th arrondissement</a>, 330 meters high, completed in 1889 as the gateway to the 1889 Paris Universal Exposition. The tallest building in the Paris region is <a href="/wiki/The_Link_(building)" title="The Link (building)">The Link</a>, at 242 meters, located in <a href="/wiki/La_D%C3%A9fense" title="La Défense">La Défense</a>. It is tied for eighth place among the tallest buildings in the European Union. The tallest building within the city limits of Paris is the <a href="/wiki/Tour_Montparnasse" title="Tour Montparnasse">Tour Montparnasse</a>, 210 meters high.\n</p>\n<meta property="mw:PageProp/toc" />\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Tallest_buildings_and_structures">Tallest buildings and structures</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=List_of_tallest_buildings_and_structures_in_the_Paris_region&amp;action=edit&amp;section=1" title="Edit section: Tallest buildings and structures"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<p>The Paris region has four of the tallest twenty-five buildings in the European Union: the tour Link, the Tour First, the Tour Hekla, and the Tour Montparnasse. As of 2025, there are 24 skyscrapers that reach a roof height of at least 150 metres (490&#160;ft).\n</p><p>Most of the Paris region\'s high-rise buildings are located in three distinct areas:\n</p>\n<dl><dd><ul><li><b><a href="/wiki/La_D%C3%A9fense" title="La Défense">La Défense</a></b>, located just west of the City of Paris in the <a href="/wiki/Departments_of_France" title="Departments of France">département</a> of the <i><a href="/wiki/Hauts-de-Seine" title="Hauts-de-Seine">Hauts-de-Seine</a></i>. Eight of the ten tallest buildings and structures in the region are located in La Defense.</li>\n<li><b><a href="/wiki/Italie_13" title="Italie 13">Italie 13</a></b>, located in the southern half of the <a href="/wiki/13th_arrondissement_of_Paris" title="13th arrondissement of Paris">13th arrondissement</a>: The 13th arrondissement towers are mostly residential, located in the south of the <a href="/wiki/Arrondissements_of_Paris" title="Arrondissements of Paris">arrondissement</a>, in what is today le <i>Quartier chinois</i> (Chinatown).</li>\n<li><b><a href="/wiki/Front_de_Seine" title="Front de Seine">Front de Seine</a></b>, located in the <a href="/wiki/15th_arrondissement_of_Paris" title="15th arrondissement of Paris">15th arrondissement</a>: Most of the buildings of the <a href="/wiki/Front_de_Seine" title="Front de Seine">Front de Seine</a>, which is in close proximity to the <a href="/wiki/Eiffel_Tower" title="Eiffel Tower">Eiffel Tower</a>, were built in the 1970s and 1980s and are of mixed commercial and residential use. The tallest building is the <a href="/wiki/Tour_Montparnasse" title="Tour Montparnasse">Tour Montparnasse</a>.</li></ul></dd></dl>\n<p>Other high-rise buildings are scattered throughout the Paris area, mainly in close proximity to the <i><a href="/wiki/Boulevard_P%C3%A9riph%C3%A9rique" title="Boulevard Périphérique">Périphérique</a></i> freeway. These include <a href="/wiki/Les_Mercuriales" title="Les Mercuriales">Les Mercuriales</a> in <a href="/wiki/Bagnolet" title="Bagnolet">Bagnolet</a>, the <a href="/wiki/Tour_Pleyel" title="Tour Pleyel">Tour Pleyel</a> in <a href="/wiki/Saint-Denis,_Seine-Saint-Denis" title="Saint-Denis, Seine-Saint-Denis">Saint-Denis</a>, and the <a href="/wiki/Hyatt_Regency_Paris_%C3%89toile" title="Hyatt Regency Paris Étoile">Hôtel Hyatt Regency Paris Étoile</a> in the city proper (near the Porte Maillot).\n</p><p>However the tallest tower is built within central Paris: the iconic <a href="/wiki/Eiffel_Tower" title="Eiffel Tower">Eiffel Tower</a> standing alongside the Seine River at the heart of the <a href="/wiki/7th_arrondissement_of_Paris" title="7th arrondissement of Paris">7th arrondissement</a>. Built in 1889, it was the first man-made structure in the world to exceed 1,000 feet.\n</p>\n<ul class="gallery mw-gallery-packed">\n\t\t<li class="gallerybox" style="width: 2026-02-26 13:10:24 | INFO     | Scraping: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_the_world's_tallest_buildings
2026-02-26 13:10:25 | DEBUG    | Scraped content: ScrapedContent(url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_the_world's_tallest_buildings", title="History of the world's tallest buildings - Wikipedia", text='From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia The tallest building in the world, as of 2026, [update] is the Burj Khalifa in Dubai , United Arab Emirates. The title of " world\'s tallest building " has been held  by various buildings in modern times, including Lincoln Cathedral in Lincoln, England , and the Empire State Building and the original World Trade Center , both in New York City . Before the modern skyscraper era emerged, between c. 1311 and 1884 the tallest buildings and structures were mostly Christian churches and cathedrals. Prior to then, the tallest buildings in the world cannot be conclusively determined. For instance, the Lighthouse of Alexandria , which was completed in approximately 280 BC, has been estimated to have been 100\xa0m (330\xa0ft) tall, [ 1 ] but its true height is not known. For thousands of years, the Great Pyramid in Egypt was the tallest structure in the world until Lincoln Cathedral of 1311 , but the Great Pyramid is not considered a building since it is not habitable. Similarly, the Eiffel Tower was the world\'s tallest structure from 1889, when it was built, but not the tallest building. The skyscraper was invented in Chicago in 1884 when Home Insurance Building was constructed using a steel frame with curtain walls instead of load-bearing walls . For the next century, the world\'s tallest building was always in the United States , with New York City housing the tallest building for  86 years and Chicago housing it for 30 years. After a century (1894–1998), the distinction of the world\'s tallest building moved to Malaysia , which was the first country to break the United States\' record of constructing the tallest buildings in the world when Petronas Towers was completed in 1998. Taiwan \'s Taipei 101 was the next to hold the record; the building\'s status as the world\'s tallest building lasted from 2004 to 2009, when it was transferred to the Burj Khalifa , the current record-holder of 828 meters tall, upon its completion in the United Arab Emirates. Definition of terms [ edit ] The world\'s tallest buildings as of 2015 Meaning of "building" [ edit ] The earliest structures now known to be the tallest in the world were the Egyptian pyramids : the Great Pyramid of Giza , at an original height of 146.5\xa0m (481\xa0ft), was the tallest structure in the world for over 3,800 years, until the construction of Lincoln Cathedral in 1311. From then until the completion of the Washington Monument (capped in 1884) the world\'s tallest structures were churches or cathedrals. Later, the Eiffel Tower and, still later, some radio masts and television towers, were the world\'s tallest structures. However, though all of these are structures , some are not buildings in the sense of being regularly inhabited or occupied. It is in this sense of being regularly inhabited or occupied that the term "building" is generally applied when determining the world\'s tallest building. The non-profit international organization Council on Tall Buildings and Urban Habitat (CTBUH), which maintains a set of criteria for determining the height of tall buildings, defines a "building" as "(A) structure that is designed for residential, business or manufacturing purposes" and that "has floors". [ 2 ] Tall churches and cathedrals occupy a middle ground: their lower areas are regularly occupied, but much of their height is in bell towers and spires which are not. Whether a church or cathedral is a "building" or merely a "structure" for the purposes of determining the title of "world\'s tallest building" is a subjective matter of definition (this article treats churches and cathedrals as buildings). Determination of height [ edit ] The Council on Tall Buildings and Urban Habitat (CTBUH) has been generally recognized as the arbiter on the building height of skyscrapers since the mid-20th century. In the early 1970\'s they promulgated the criteria that height is measured "from the sidewalk of the main entrance to the structural top of the building including penthouse and tower." In 1996, during the controversy over whether the Petronas Twin Towers or the Sears Tower should be considered the world\'s tallest building, the CTBUH adopted three new height criteria. When determining the height of a tall building, each of the three criteria may give a different result. "Height of the highest floor" is one criterion, and "height to the top of any part of the building" is another, but the default criterion used by the CTBUH is "height of the architectural top of the building", which includes spires but not antennas, masts or flag poles. [ 2 ] Before the 20th century [ edit ] Further information: List of tallest structures built before the 20th century Before the 13th century [ edit ] La Danta in El Mirador , Guatemala, a 72\xa0m (236\xa0ft) tall temple built in 300 BC. Vimana of Brihadisvara Temple, Thanjavur , Tamilnadu at 66\xa0m (217\xa0ft) Kutubiyya Mosque at 77\xa0m (253\xa0ft) Early tall buildings were similar to the record-setting Egyptian pyramid structures. In 1400 BC the 70\xa0m (230\xa0ft) ziggurat of Dur-Kurigalzu was constructed in Mesopotamia , and in 601 BC the Etemenanki ziggurat of Babylon (91\xa0m (299\xa0ft)) followed. The 70\xa0m (230\xa0ft) La Danta of El Mirador ( Guatemala ) and the 73\xa0m (240\xa0ft) Amaravati Stupa of Amaravati ( India ) were constructed in around 300 BC. The Lighthouse of Alexandria in Egypt had a height of between 103 and 118\xa0m (338 and 387\xa0ft) [ citation needed ] and existed between the 3rd century BC and 14th century AD. The Pantheon in Rome, finished in the early 2nd century AD, has an ancient Roman height record from floor to top of 43.45\xa0m (142.6\xa0ft), [ 3 ] which exactly corresponds to the diameter of its interior space and was only slightly surpassed by the Pont du Gard structure . The Hagia Sophia , built in AD 537 in Constantinople , reaches a height of 55\xa0m (180\xa0ft). The ancient Kushan stupa of Kanishka , located in the present-day Pakistan , near Peshawar , completed around AD 200, had a height of between 120 and 170\xa0m (390 and 560\xa0ft). The Chinese explorer Xuanzhang described it as the tallest building in the world in his book Records of the western Region . The Sri Lankan Jetavanaramaya stupa, constructed in the 3rd century, measured 122\xa0m (400\xa0ft) from its construction until the 11th century. Its current height is 71\xa0m (233\xa0ft). Another short-lived structure was the 6th-century wooden Yongning Pagoda with a height of about 137\xa0m (449\xa0ft) to 155\xa0m (509\xa0ft) in Luoyang , China. Hwangnyongsa , or Hwangnyong Temple, and sometimes spelled Hwangryongsa, is a former Buddhist temple in the city of Gyeongju , South Korea. Completed in the 7th century, the enormous nine-storey structure was built entirely of interlocking timbers with no iron nails. It had a standing total height of 68 to 80\xa0m (223 to 262\xa0ft), [ 4 ] making it the tallest structure in East Asia and the tallest wooden structure in the world at the time of its construction. It was destroyed by invading Mongol forces in 1238. In the 8th century, two seven-storied pagodas with a height of 100\xa0m (330\xa0ft) were constructed at Todaiｰji (東大寺) in Nara , Japan . They were one of the tallest wooden buildings in the world at the time. By the 14th century, both were burned down by fires caused by war or lightning strikes. In 1057, the 100\xa0m (330\xa0ft) wooden Shwesandaw Pagoda of Bagan , Myanmar , was constructed. The Vimana of the Brihadisvara Temple, Thanjavur , Tamil Nadu , completed in 1010 is 66\xa0m (217\xa0ft) tall, slightly taller and older than Angkor Wat , Cambodia . The entire complex is built of granite . The 77\xa0m (253\xa0ft) minaret of Koutoubia Mosque in Marrakesh , Morocco , includes a spire and orbs.  It was completed under the reign of the Berber Almohad Caliph Yaqub al-Mansur around 1195. The minaret of Isa in the Umayyad Mosque was most likely originally built in the 9th century and also had a height of 77 m (253 ft). The eastern spires of the Romanesque Speyer Cathedral , completed in 1106, reach a height of 71.3\xa0m (234\xa0ft). The still-standing Torre Asinelli , completed some time before 1185, was originally 70\xa0m (230\xa0ft) tall, later raised to 92\xa0m (302\xa0ft). Malmesbury Abbey was built in 1180 and reached a height of 131\xa0m (430\xa0ft). Churches and cathedrals: tallest buildings between the 13th and 20th centuries [ edit ] Main article: List of tallest church buildings An 1850 comparison of the height of 30 notable world structures The world\'s tallest structures were churches or cathedrals from the 13th/14th century until 1884, and buildings until the beginning of the 20th century. The Old St Paul\'s Cathedral (149\xa0m (489\xa0ft)) in London and Lincoln Cathedral (160\xa0m (520\xa0ft)) both surpassed not only any older tallest building, but also the tallest structures until then, the Pyramids. They were constructed from the 12th century, reaching completion and their maximum height in the 1310s (1314 and 1311 respectively). Lincoln Cathedral\'s spire collapsed in 1549, and its previous height was not surpassed elsewhere for a long time. St. Mary\'s Church in Stralsund became the world\'s tallest building after the collapse of the Lincoln spire. The 153\xa0m (502\xa0ft) central tower of St. Pierre\'s Cathedral in Beauvais was tallest from 1569 until it collapsed in 1573, making St. Mary\'s the tallest once again. In 1647, the bell tower of St. Mary\'s burned down, making the shorter Strasbourg Cathedral the world\'s tallest building. It was not until the completion of the Ulm Minster in 1890 that the world\'s tallest building was again also the tallest building ever constructed, surpassing the original configuration of Lincoln Cathedral. [ 6 ] [ 7 ] [ 8 ] [ 9 ] [ 10 ] [ 11 ] The completion date for the spire is given as 1311 rather than 1300 by some sources. [ 12 ] Also the 149\xa0m (489\xa0ft) height of the spire of Old St Paul\'s Cathedral , destroyed by lightning in 1561, is disputed, for example by Christopher Wren (1632–1723), who suggested a height of 140\xa0m (460\xa0ft). [ 13 ] Turn of the century [ edit ] In 1890, Ulm Minster became the tallest church ever built, but it was the last church to claim the position of tallest building, which eventually went to the Philadelphia City Hall in 1894, the first skyscraper taller than 150\xa0m (490\xa0ft) (or, depending on definition, the Mole Antonelliana in 1889). [ 14 ] Among all structures, in 1884 the 169\xa0m (554\xa0ft) Washington Monument had already overtaken the long-standing record held by churches. But five years later in 1889 it was significantly surpassed by the Eiffel Tower , which reached completely new heights at 300\xa0m (980\xa0ft) (its 24\xa0m (79\xa0ft) antennas were added after 1957), [ 15 ] leaving heights of skyscrapers behind and opening up the supertall era, whose heights were only reached by the pinnacle of the Chrysler Building (319\xa0m (1,047\xa0ft)) in 1930 and fully overtaken by the Empire State Building in 1931. Tallest structures since the 20th century [ edit ] Main article: History of the world\'s tallest structures A history of the world\'s tallest buildings Since the completion of the Washington Monument in Washington, D.C. in 1884, the world\'s tallest structure has generally not simultaneously been the world\'s tallest building. The exception is 1930 through 1954 when the Eiffel Tower in Paris was surpassed by the Chrysler Building in 1930, and in 1931 the Chrysler Building was surpassed by the Empire State Building , which was later surpassed by a succession of structures, starting with the Griffin Television Tower in Oklahoma. The CN Tower in Toronto held the record for the world\'s tallest free-standing structure for 32 years from 1975 until 2007 when it was surpassed by Burj Khalifa , and was the world\'s tallest tower until 2009 when it was surpassed by Canton Tower . Since the completion of the Burj Khalifa in 2010, it is the world\'s tallest building and world\'s tallest structure of any kind. Skyscrapers: tallest buildings since 1908 [ edit ] See also: List of tallest buildings Since the completion of the first skyscraper taller than 150\xa0m (490\xa0ft) (depending on the definition of skyscraper, 1894 with the Philadelphia City Hall or 1908 with the Singer Building ), skyscrapers have consistently been the tallest buildings . High-rise blocks and early skyscrapers [ edit ] Main article: Early skyscrapers Before skyscrapers, tower blocks reached at various times and locations heights of 30\xa0m (98\xa0ft) (as in the city of Shibam ) or even up to 100\xa0m (330\xa0ft) among the Towers of Bologna . Buildings that have been specifically called the first skyscrapers include: E. V. Haughwout Building , 24\xa0m (79\xa0ft) tall, 5 floors, first use of a passenger elevator, built in 1857 Equitable Life Building , [ 16 ] at least 40\xa0m (130\xa0ft) tall, 9 floors, built in 1870 New York Tribune Building , [ 16 ] 79\xa0m (259\xa0ft) tall, 9 floors, built in 1875, expanded in 1907 to 19 floors Montauk Building , [ 17 ] 40\xa0m (130\xa0ft) tall, 10 floors, built in 1883 Home Insurance Building , [ 18 ] 42\xa0m (138\xa0ft) tall, 12 floors, built in 1885 Lancashire Insurance Building , [ 16 ] [ 19 ] 10 floors, built in 1890 Manhattan Building in Chicago , [ 16 ] 68.3\xa0m (224\xa0ft) tall, 16 floors, built in 1891 Monadnock Building , [ 17 ] 66\xa0m (217\xa0ft) tall, 17 floors, built in 1891 Later record-setting early skyscrapers include: New York World Building , 94\xa0m (308\xa0ft), 1890 Manhattan Life Insurance Building , 106\xa0m (348\xa0ft), 1894 The height of skyscrapers [ edit ] Comparison of the vanity height as defined as the difference between the pinnacle height and the height to the floor of the highest occupied top floor of some buildings that have at one point registered as the world\'s tallest After the construction of the first skyscraper taller than 150\xa0m (490\xa0ft), depending on definition the Philadelphia City Hall in 1894 or the Singer Building in 1908, the incrementation in the height category of supertall skyscrapers began with the construction of the Chrysler Building , followed by the Empire State Building , in New York City. The Chrysler Building was the first building in the world to break the 300\xa0m (980\xa0ft) barrier, and the Empire State Building was the first building to have more than 100 floors. It stands at 381\xa0m (1,250\xa0ft) and has 102 floors. The next tallest skyscraper was the World Trade Center , which was completed in 1971. The North Tower was 417\xa0m (1,368\xa0ft) and the South Tower 415\xa0m (1,362\xa0ft) tall. It surpassed the height of the Empire State Building by 36\xa0m (118\xa0ft). Two years later the Sears Tower was built in Chicago, standing at 442\xa0m (1,450\xa0ft) with 110 floors, surpassing the height of the World Trade Center by 25\xa0m (82\xa0ft). Counting the Petronas Towers \' antenna spires yet discounting the Sears Tower\'s antennae, the former rose 10 meters above the latter, standing at a height of 452\xa0m (1,483\xa0ft) and each having 88 floors. In 2004, the construction of Taipei 101 brought the height of skyscrapers to a new level, standing at 508\xa0m (1,667\xa0ft) with 101 floors. It is 59\xa0m (194\xa0ft) taller than the previous record-holders, the Petronas Towers. Burj Khalifa surpassed the height of Taipei 101 by 319\xa0m (1,047\xa0ft) in 2009, making it 60% taller. [ 20 ] It has broken several skyscraper records, and it is almost twice as tall as the Empire State Building. Burj Khalifa, however has not broken the record of world\'s tallest structure . In 2009, Guinness World Records recognised the Magnolia oil platform as the tallest structure. It has a record-breaking height of 1,432 metres (4,698 feet). [ 21 ] However the majority of the Burj Khalifa\'s height difference (29%) is gained from vanity height , the Burj Khalifa\'s highest occupiable floor is only 585\xa0m (1,919\xa0ft) above ground. This would still make it the tallest building in the world but only by 2 meters over the Shanghai Tower , [ 22 ] a substantially smaller margin than before. Note: The CTBUH defines a building as a supertall if it is 300\xa0m (980\xa0ft) or taller. [ 23 ] The CTBUH defines a building as a megatall if it is 600\xa0m (1970\xa0ft) or taller. Supertall and megatall skyscrapers by location [ edit ] Since the early skyscraper boom that took place in North America , the significant number of skyscrapers in North America dominated the 100 tallest buildings in the world. In 1930, 99 of the 100 tallest buildings in the world were in North America. In the future, this percentage is expected to decline to only 22 percent. [ 20 ] The predominance of skyscrapers in North America is decreasing because of skyscraper construction in other parts of the world, especially in Asia. In Asia, there has been an increase in the number of supertall skyscrapers beginning with the completion of the Bank of China Tower in Hong Kong in 1990. Currently, sixty of the world\'s 100 tallest buildings are in Asia (including the Middle East), while all six megatall skyscrapers reside in Asia. All proposed future megatall skyscrapers are also in Asia with the exception of the Lakhta Center 2 in St. Petersburg. Skyscrapers [ edit ] Since the skyscraper era began, the great majority of skyscrapers were used predominantly as office space. From 1930 to 2000, the percentage of office towers never fell below 86 percent, but in the future it is expected to be as low as 46 percent. [ 20 ] By 2010, fewer than half of the 100 tallest buildings in the world were office towers, the majority being for residential and mixed use. [ 20 ] Only four of the ten tallest buildings in the world, and twenty-eight of the top fifty, were used primarily as offices. [ 24 ] A mixed-use tall building is defined as having two or more functions that occupy a significant proportion of the tower\'s total space. [A] Support areas such as car parks and mechanical plant space do not contribute towards mixed-use status. [ 23 ] Skyscrapers used primarily or exclusively as hotels or residential space are generally shorter than office and mixed-use buildings, with only a few supertall buildings of the residential or hotel types among the 100 tallest skyscrapers. The tallest completed residential buildings (minimum 85% residential) are Central Park Tower , 111 West 57th Street , and 432 Park Avenue , all on Billionaire\'s Row in New York City. [ 25 ] The tallest completed hotels (primarily hotel space) are the Gevora Hotel , the JW Marriott Marquis Dubai twin towers, the Rose Tower , and the Burj Al Arab , all in Dubai. [ 26 ] List of historically tallest skyscrapers [ edit ] Main article: Skyscraper §\xa0History of the tallest skyscrapers The following list of tallest buildings is based on the default metric of CTBUH, [ 18 ] that of measuring to the highest architectural element. Other criteria would generate a different list. Shanghai World Financial Center is not on the above list, but it surpassed Taipei 101 in 2008 to become the building with the highest occupied floor. Using the criterion of highest tip (including antennae), the World Trade Center in New York City was the world\'s tallest building from 1971 to 1973, until the Willis Tower in Chicago (which already had a higher occupied floor than the World Trade Center) had its antenna extended to give that building the world\'s tallest tip, a title it held until the 2010 completion of Burj Khalifa. Petronas Towers and Taipei 101 were never the world\'s tallest buildings by the highest–tip criterion. class="vector-body" aria-labelledby="firstHeading" data-mw-ve-target-container>\n\t\t\t\t\t<div class="vector-body-before-content">\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t<div class="mw-indicators">\n\t\t</div>\n\n\t\t\t\t\t\t<div id="siteSub" class="noprint">From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia</div>\n\t\t\t\t\t</div>\n\t\t\t\t\t<div id="contentSub"><div id="mw-content-subtitle"></div></div>\n\t\t\t\t\t\n\t\t\t\t\t\n\t\t\t\t\t<div id="mw-content-text" class="mw-body-content"><div class="mw-subjectpageheader">\n</div><div class="mw-content-ltr mw-parser-output" lang="en" dir="ltr"><p>\n\nThe tallest building in the world, as of 2026,<sup class="plainlinks noexcerpt noprint asof-tag update" style="display:none;"><a class="external text" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=History_of_the_world%27s_tallest_buildings&amp;action=edit">&#91;update&#93;</a></sup> is the <a href="/wiki/Burj_Khalifa" title="Burj Khalifa">Burj Khalifa</a> in <a href="/wiki/Dubai" title="Dubai">Dubai</a>, United Arab Emirates. The title of "<a href="/wiki/List_of_tallest_buildings" title="List of tallest buildings">world\'s tallest building</a>" has been held  by various buildings in modern times, including <a href="/wiki/Lincoln_Cathedral" title="Lincoln Cathedral">Lincoln Cathedral</a> in <a href="/wiki/Lincoln,_England" title="Lincoln, England">Lincoln, England</a>, and the <a href="/wiki/Empire_State_Building" title="Empire State Building">Empire State Building</a> and the <a href="/wiki/World_Trade_Center_(1973%E2%80%932001)" title="World Trade Center (1973–2001)">original World Trade Center</a>, both in <a href="/wiki/New_York_City" title="New York City">New York City</a>.\n</p><p>Before the modern <a href="/wiki/Skyscraper" title="Skyscraper">skyscraper</a> era emerged, between <abbr title="circa">c.</abbr> 1311 and 1884 the tallest buildings and structures were mostly <a href="/wiki/Christianity" title="Christianity">Christian</a> churches and cathedrals. Prior to then, the tallest buildings in the world cannot be conclusively determined. For instance, the <a href="/wiki/Lighthouse_of_Alexandria" title="Lighthouse of Alexandria">Lighthouse of Alexandria</a>, which was completed in approximately 280 BC, has been estimated to have been 100&#160;m (330&#160;ft) tall,<sup id="cite&#95;ref-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-1"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> but its true height is not known. For thousands of years, the <a href="/wiki/Great_Pyramid_of_Giza" title="Great Pyramid of Giza">Great Pyramid</a> in <a href="/wiki/Egypt" title="Egypt">Egypt</a> was the tallest <i>structure</i> in the world until <a href="/wiki/Lincoln_Cathedral" title="Lincoln Cathedral">Lincoln Cathedral of 1311</a>, but the Great Pyramid is not considered a building since it is not habitable. Similarly, the <a href="/wiki/Eiffel_Tower" title="Eiffel Tower">Eiffel Tower</a> was the world\'s tallest structure from 1889, when it was built, but not the tallest building.\n</p><p>The skyscraper was invented in <a href="/wiki/Chicago" title="Chicago">Chicago</a> in 1884 when <a href="/wiki/Home_Insurance_Building" title="Home Insurance Building">Home Insurance Building</a> was constructed using a <a href="/wiki/Steel_frame" title="Steel frame">steel frame</a> with <a href="/wiki/Curtain_wall_(architecture)" title="Curtain wall (architecture)">curtain walls</a> instead of <a href="/wiki/Load-bearing_wall" title="Load-bearing wall">load-bearing walls</a>. For the next century, the world\'s tallest building was always in the <a href="/wiki/United_States" title="United States">United States</a>, with <a href="/wiki/New_York_City" title="New York City">New York City</a> housing the tallest building for  86 years and Chicago housing it for 30 years. After a century (1894–1998), the distinction of the world\'s tallest building moved to <a href="/wiki/Malaysia" title="Malaysia">Malaysia</a>, which was the first country to break the United States\' record of constructing the tallest buildings in the world when <a href="/wiki/Petronas_Towers" title="Petronas Towers">Petronas Towers</a> was completed in 1998. <a href="/wiki/Taiwan" title="Taiwan">Taiwan</a>\'s <a href="/wiki/Taipei_101" title="Taipei 101">Taipei 101</a> was the next to hold the record; the building\'s status as the world\'s tallest building lasted from 2004 to 2009, when it was transferred to the <a href="/wiki/Burj_Khalifa" title="Burj Khalifa">Burj Khalifa</a>, the current record-holder of 828 meters tall, upon its completion in the United Arab Emirates.\n</p>\n<meta property="mw:PageProp/toc" />\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Definition_of_terms">Definition of terms</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=History_of_the_world%27s_tallest_buildings&amp;action=edit&amp;section=1" title="Edit section: Definition of terms"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Tallest_buildings_in_the_world.png" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7e/Tallest_buildings_in_the_world.png/330px-Tallest_buildings_in_the_world.png" decoding="async" width="280" height="111" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7e/Tallest_buildings_in_the_world.png/500px-Tallest_buildings_in_the_world.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7e/Tallest_buildings_in_the_world.png/960px-Tallest_buildings_in_the_world.png 2x" data-file-width="4961" data-file-height="1969" /></a><figcaption>The world\'s tallest buildings as of 2015</figcaption></figure>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Meaning_of_&quot;building&quot;"><span id="Meaning_of_.22building.22"></span>Meaning of "building"</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=History_of_the_world%27s_tallest_buildings&amp;action=edit&amp;section=2" title="Edit section: Meaning of &quot;building&quot;"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<p>The earliest structures now known to be the tallest in the world were the <a href="/wiki/Egyptian_pyramids" title="Egyptian pyramids">Egyptian pyramids</a>: the <a href="/wiki/Great_Pyramid_of_Giza" title="Great Pyramid of Giza">Great Pyramid of Giza</a>, at an original height of 146.5&#160;m (481&#160;ft), was the tallest structure in the world for over 3,800 years, until the construction of <a href="/wiki/Lincoln_Cathedral" title="Lincoln Cathedral">Lincoln Cathedral</a> in 1311. From then until the completion of the <a href="/wiki/Washington_Monument" title="Washington Monument">Washington Monument</a> (capped in 1884) the world\'s tallest structures were churches or cathedrals. Later, the <a href="/wiki/Eiffel_Tower" title="Eiffel Tower">Eiffel Tower</a> and, still later, some radio masts and television towers, were the world\'s tallest structures.\n</p><p>However, though all of these are <i>structures</i>, some are not <i><a href="/wiki/Building" title="Building">buildings</a></i> in the sense of being regularly inhabited or occupied. It is in this sense of being regularly inhabited or occupied that the term "building" is generally applied when determining the world\'s tallest building. The non-profit international organization <a href="/wiki/Council_on_Tall_Buildings_and_Urban_Habitat" class="mw-redirect" title="Council on Tall Buildings and Urban Habitat">Council on Tall Buildings and Urban Habitat</a> (CTBUH), which maintains a set of criteria for determining the height of tall buildings, defines a "building" as "(A) structure that is designed for residential, business or manufacturing purposes" and that "has floors".<sup id="cite&#95;ref-CTBUH&#95;criteria&#95;2-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-CTBUH_criteria-2"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>Tall churches and cathedrals occupy a middle ground: their lower areas are regularly occupied, but much of their height is in bell towers and spires which are not. Whether a church or cathedral is a "building" or merely a "structure" for the purposes of determining the title of "world\'s tallest building" is a subjective matter of definition (this article treats churches and cathedrals as buildings).\n</p>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Determination_of_height">Determination of height</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=History_of_the_world%27s_tallest_buildings&amp;action=edit&amp;section=3" title="Edit section: Determination of height"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<p>The Council on Tall Buildings and Urban Habitat (CTBUH) has been generally recognized as the arbiter on the building height of skyscrapers since the mid-20th century. In the early 1970\'s they promulgated the criteria that height is measured "from the sidewalk of the main entrance to the structural top of the building including penthouse and tower." In 1996, during the controversy over whether the <a href="/wiki/Petronas_Twin_Towers" class="mw-redirect" title="Petronas Twin Towers">Petronas Twin Towers</a> or the <a href="/wiki/Sears_Tower" class="mw-redirect" title="Sears Tower">Sears Tower</a> should be considered the world\'s tallest building, the CTBUH adopted three new height criteria. When determining the height of a tall building, each of the three criteria may give a different result. "Height of the highest floor" is one criterion, and "height to the top of any part of the building" is another, but the default criterion used by the CTBUH is "height of the architectural top of the building", which includes spires but not antennas, masts or flag poles.<sup id="cite&#95;ref-CTBUH&#95;criteria&#95;2-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-CTBUH_criteria-2"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Before_the_20th_century">Before the 20th century</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=History_of_the_world%27s_tallest_buildings&amp;action=edit&amp;section=4" title="Edit section: Before the 20th century"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<style data-mw-deduplicate="TemplateStyles:r1320445320">.mw-parser-output .hatnote{font-style:italic}.mw-parser-output div.hatnote{padding-left:1.6em;margin-bottom:0.5em}.mw-parser-output .hatnote i{font-style:normal}.mw-parser-output .hatnote+link+.hatnote{margin-top:-0.5em}@media print{body.ns-0 .mw-parser-output .hatnote{display:none!important}}</style><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Further information: <a href="/wiki/List_of_tallest_structures_built_before_the_20th_century" title="List of tallest structures built before the 20th century">List of tallest structures built before the 20th century</a></div>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Before_the_13th_century">Before the 13th century</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=History_of_the_world%27s_tallest_buildings&amp;action=edit&amp;section=5" title="Edit section: Before the 13th century"><span>edit</span></a><span src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0a/Thanjavur%2C_Brihadishwara_Temple_%287013915633%29.jpg/330px-Thanjavur%2C_Brihadishwara_Temple_%287013915633%29.jpg" decoding="async" width="280" height="420" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0a/Thanjavur%2C_Brihadishwara_Temple_%287013915633%29.jpg/500px-Thanjavur%2C_Brihadishwara_Temple_%287013915633%29.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0a/Thanjavur%2C_Brihadishwara_Temple_%287013915633%29.jpg/960px-Thanjavur%2C_Brihadishwara_Temple_%287013915633%29.jpg 2x" data-file-width="2848" data-file-height="4272" /></a><figcaption>Vimana of <a href="/wiki/Brihadisvara_Temple,_Thanjavur" class="mw-redirect" title="Brihadisvara Temple, Thanjavur">Brihadisvara Temple, Thanjavur</a>, <a href="/wiki/Tamilnadu" class="mw-redirect" title="Tamilnadu">Tamilnadu</a> at 66&#160;m (217&#160;ft)</figcaption></figure>\n<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Marokko0112_(retouched).jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/49/Marokko0112_%28retouched%29.jpg/330px-Marokko0112_%28retouched%29.jpg" decoding="async" width="280" height="373" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/49/Marokko0112_%28retouched%29.jpg/500px-Marokko0112_%28retouched%29.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/49/Marokko0112_%28retouched%29.jpg/960px-Marokko0112_%28retouched%29.jpg 2x" data-file-width="2304" data-file-height="3072" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Kutubiyya_Mosque" title="Kutubiyya Mosque">Kutubiyya Mosque</a> at 77&#160;m (253&#160;ft)</figcaption></figure>\n<p>Early tall buildings were similar to the record-setting Egyptian pyramid structures. In 1400 BC the 70&#160;m (230&#160;ft) <a href="/wiki/Ziggurat" title="Ziggurat">ziggurat</a> of <a href="/wiki/Dur-Kurigalzu" title="Dur-Kurigalzu">Dur-Kurigalzu</a> was constructed in <a href="/wiki/Mesopotamia" title="Mesopotamia">Mesopotamia</a>, and in 601 BC the <a href="/wiki/Etemenanki" title="Etemenanki">Etemenanki</a> ziggurat of <a href="/wiki/Babylon" title="Babylon">Babylon</a> (91&#160;m (299&#160;ft)) followed. The 70&#160;m (230&#160;ft) <a href="/wiki/La_Danta" class="mw-redirect" title="La Danta">La Danta</a> of <a href="/wiki/El_Mirador" title="El Mirador">El Mirador</a> (<a href="/wiki/Guatemala" title="Guatemala">Guatemala</a>) and the 73&#160;m (240&#160;ft) <a href="/wiki/Amaravati_Stupa" title="Amaravati Stupa">Amaravati Stupa</a> of <a href="/wiki/Amaravati" title="Amaravati">Amaravati</a> (<a href="/wiki/India" title="India">India</a>) were constructed in around 300 BC.\n</p><p>The <a href="/wiki/Lighthouse_of_Alexandria" title="Lighthouse of Alexandria">Lighthouse of Alexandria</a> in <a href="/wiki/Egypt" title="Egypt">Egypt</a> had a height of between 103 and 118&#160;m (338 and 387&#160;ft)<sup class="noprint Inline-Template Template-Fact" style="white-space:nowrap;">&#91;<i><a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed" title="Wikipedia:Citation needed"><span title="This claim needs references to reliable sources. (May 2024)">citation needed</span></a></i>&#93;</sup> and existed between the 3rd century BC and 14th century AD.\n</p><p>The <a href="/wiki/Pantheon,_Rome" title="Pantheon, Rome">Pantheon</a> in Rome, finished in the early 2nd century AD, has an <a href="/wiki/List_of_Greek_and_Roman_architectural_records" title="List of Greek and Roman architectural records">ancient Roman height record</a> from floor to top of 43.45&#160;m (142.6&#160;ft),<sup id="cite&#95;ref-Rasch&#95;1985,&#95;119&#95;3-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Rasch_1985,_119-3"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>3<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> which exactly corresponds to the diameter of its interior space and was only slightly surpassed by the <a href="/wiki/Pont_du_Gard" title="Pont du Gard">Pont du Gard</a> <i>structure</i>. The <a href="/wiki/Hagia_Sophia" title="Hagia Sophia">Hagia Sophia</a>, built in AD 537 in <a href="/wiki/Constantinople" title="Constantinople">Constantinople</a>, reaches a height of 55&#160;m (180&#160;ft).\n</p><p>The ancient <a href="/wiki/Kushan_Empire" title="Kushan Empire">Kushan</a> <a href="/wiki/Kanishka_Stupa" title="Kanishka Stupa">stupa of Kanishka</a>, located in the present-day <a href="/wiki/Pakistan" title="Pakistan">Pakistan</a>, near <a href="/wiki/Peshawar" title="Peshawar">Peshawar</a>, completed around AD 200, had a height of between 120 and 170&#160;m (390 and 560&#160;ft). The Chinese explorer <a href="/wiki/Xuanzhang" class="mw-redirect" title="Xuanzhang">Xuanzhang</a> described it as the tallest building in the world in his book <i>Records of the western Region</i>. The <a href="/wiki/Sri_Lanka" title="Sri Lanka">Sri Lankan</a> <a href="/wiki/Jetavanaramaya" title="Jetavanaramaya">Jetavanaramaya</a> stupa, constructed in the 3rd century, measured 122&#160;m (400&#160;ft) from its construction until the 11th century. Its current height is 71&#160;m (233&#160;ft).\n</p><p>Another short-lived structure was the 6th-century wooden <a href="/wiki/Yongning_Pagoda" title="Yongning Pagoda">Yongning Pagoda</a> with a height of about 137&#160;m (449&#160;ft) to 155&#160;m (509&#160;ft) in <a href="/wiki/Luoyang" title="Luoyang">Luoyang</a>, China.\n</p><p><a href="/wiki/Hwangnyongsa" title="Hwangnyongsa">Hwangnyongsa</a>, or Hwangnyong Temple, and sometimes spelled Hwangryongsa, is a former <a href="/wiki/Buddhist_temple" title="Buddhist temple">Buddhist temple</a> in the city of <a href="/wiki/Gyeongju" title="Gyeongju">Gyeongju</a>, South Korea. Completed in the 7th century, the enormous nine-storey structure was built entirely of interlocking timbers with no iron nails. It had a standing total height of 68 to 80&#160;m (223 to 262&#160;ft),<sup id="cite&#95;ref-Silla1&#95;4-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Silla1-4"><span class="cite-bracket">&#91;</span>4<span class="cite-bracket">&#93;</span></a></sup> making it the tallest structure in East Asia and the <a href="/wiki/List_of_tallest_wooden_buildings" class="mw-redirect" title="List of tallest wooden buildings">tallest wooden structure</a> in the world at the time of its construction. It was destroyed by invading Mongol forces in 1238.\n</p><p>In the 8th century, two seven-storied pagodas with a height of 100&#160;m (330&#160;ft) were constructed at <a href="/wiki/T%C5%8Ddai-ji" title="Tōdai-ji">Todaiｰji (東大寺)</a> in <a href="/wiki/Nara,_Nara" class="mw-redirect" title="Nara, Nara">Nara</a>, <a href="/wiki/Japan" title="Japan">Japan</a>. They were one of the tallest wooden buildings in the world at the time. By the 14th century, both were burned down by fires caused by war or lightning strikes.\n</p><p>In 1057, the 100&#160;m (330&#160;ft) wooden <a href="/wiki/Shwesandaw_Pagoda_(Bagan)" title="Shwesandaw Pagoda (Bagan)">Shwesandaw Pagoda</a> of <a href="/wiki/Bagan" title="Bagan">Bagan</a>, <a href="/wiki/Myanmar" title="Myanmar">Myanmar</a>, was constructed.\n</p><p>The Vimana of the <a href="/wiki/Brihadisvara_Temple,_Thanjavur" class="mw-redirect" title="Brihadisvara Temple, Thanjavur">Brihadisvara Temple, Thanjavur</a>, <a href="/wiki/Tamil_Nadu" title="Tamil Nadu">Tamil Nadu</a>, completed in 1010 is 66&#160;m (217&#160;ft) tall, slightly taller and older than <a href="/wiki/Angkor_Wat" title="Angkor Wat">Angkor Wat</a>, <a href="/wiki/Cambodia" title="Cambodia">Cambodia</a>. The entire complex is built of <a href="/wiki/Granite" title="Granite">granite</a>.\n</p><p>The 77&#160;m (253&#160;ft) <a href="/wiki/Minaret" title="Minaret">minaret</a> of <a href="/wiki/Koutoubia_Mosque" class="mw-redirect" title="Koutoubia Mosque">Koutoubia Mosque</a> in <a href="/wiki/Marrakesh" title="Marrakesh">Marrakesh</a>, <a href="/wiki/Morocco" title="Morocco">Morocco</a>, includes a spire and orbs.  It was completed under the reign of the Berber <a href="/wiki/Almohad" class="mw-redirect" title="Almohad">Almohad</a> <a href="/wiki/Caliph" class="mw-redirect" title="Caliph">Caliph</a> <a href="/wiki/Yaqub_al-Mansur" title="Yaqub al-Mansur">Yaqub al-Mansur</a> around 1195. The minaret of Isa in the <a href="/wiki/Umayyad_Mosque" title="Umayyad Mosque">Umayyad Mosque</a> was most likely originally built in the 9th century and also had a height of 77 m (253 ft).\n</p><p>The eastern spires of the Romanesque <a href="/wiki/Speyer_Cathedral" title="Speyer Cathedral">Speyer Cathedral</a>, completed in 1106, reach a height of 71.3&#160;m (234&#160;ft). The still-standing <a href="/wiki/Torre_Asinelli" class="mw-redirect" title="Torre Asinelli">Torre Asinelli</a>, completed some time before 1185, was originally 70&#160;m (230&#160;ft) tall, later raised to 92&#160;m (302&#160;ft). <a href="/wiki/Malmesbury_Abbey" title="Malmesbury Abbey">Malmesbury Abbey</a> was built in 1180 and reached a height of 131&#160;m (430&#160;ft).\n</p>\n<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Churches_and_cathedrals:_tallest_buildings_between_the_13th_and_20th_centuries">Churches and cathedrals: tallest buildings between the 13th and 20th centuries</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=History_of_the_world%27s_tallest_buildings&amp;action=edit&amp;section=6" title="Edit section: Churches and cathedrals: tallest buildings between the 13th and 20th centuries"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>\n<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1320445320" /><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/List_of_tallest_church_buildings" title="List of tallest church buildings">List of tallest church buildings</a></div>\n<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:1850_-_James_Reynolds_%26_John_Emslie_-_Buildings.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/65/1850_-_James_Reynolds_%26_John_Emslie_-_Buildings.jpg/330px-1850_-_James_Reynolds_%26_John_Emslie_-_Buildings.jpg" decoding="async" width="280" height="223" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/65/1850_-_James_Reynolds_%26_John_Emslie_-_Buildings.jpg/500px-1850_-_James_Reynolds_%26_John_Emslie_-_Buildings.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/65/1850_-_James_Reynolds_%26_John_Emslie_-_Buildings.jpg/960px-1850_-_James_Reynolds_%26_John_Emslie_-_Buildings.jpg 2x" data-file-width="5350" data-file-height="4270" /></a><figcaption>An 1850 comparison of the height of 30 notable world structures</figcaption></figure>\n<p>The world\'s tallest <i>structures</i> were churches or cathedrals from the 13th/14th century until 1884, and <i>buildings</i> until the beginning of the 20th century. The <a href="/wiki/Old_St_Paul%27s_Cathedral" title="Old St Paul&#39;s Cathedral">Old St Paul\'s Cathedral</a> (149&#160;m (489&#160;ft)) in London and <a href="/wiki/Lincoln_Cathedral" title="Lincoln Cathedral">Lincoln Cathedral</a> (160&#160;m (520&#160;ft)) both surpassed not only any older tallest building, but also the tallest structures until then, the Pyramids. They were constructed from the 12th century, reaching completion and their maximum height in the 1310s (1314 and 1311 respectively). Lincoln Cathedral\'s spire collapsed in 1549, and its previous height was not surpassed elsewhere for a long time. <a href="/wiki/St._Mary%27s_Church,_Stralsund" title="St. Mary&#39;s Church, Stralsund">St. Mary\'s Church</a> in <a href="/wiki/Stralsund" title="Stralsund">Stralsund</a> became the world\'s tallest building after the collapse of the Lincoln spire. The 153&#160;m (502&#160;ft) central tower of <a href="/wiki/Beauvais_Cathedral" title="Beauvais Cathedral">St. Pierre\'s Cathedral</a> in Beauvais was tallest from 1569 until it collapsed in 1573, making St. Mary\'s the tallest once again. In 1647, the bell tower of St. Mary\'s burned down, making the shorter <a href="/wiki/Strasbourg_Cathedral" title="Strasbourg Cathedral">Strasbourg Cathedral</a> the world\'s tallest building.\n</p><p>It was not until the completion of the <a href="/wiki/Ulm_Minster" title="Ulm Minster">Ulm Minster</a> in 1890 that the world\'s tallest building was again also the tallest building ever constructed, surpassing the original configuration of Lincoln Cathedral.\n</p>\n<table class="sortable wikitable">\n\n<tbody><tr>\n<th style="width:15%">Years tallest\n</th>\n<th style="width:30%">Name\n</th>\n<th style="width:15%">Location\n</th>\n<th style="width:10%">Height\n</th>\n<th style="width:10%">Increase\n</th>\n<th style="width:20%">Notes\n</th></tr>\n<tr>\n<td>13th century – 1311<sup class="noprint Inline-Template Template-Fact" style="white-space:nowrap;">&#91;<i><a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed" title="Wikipedia:Citation needed"><span title="This claim needs references to reliable sources. (482&#160;ft)\n</td>\n<td>3.5%\n</td>\n<td>\n</td></tr>\n<tr>\n<td>1876–1880\n</td>\n<td><a href="/wiki/Rouen_Cathedral" title="Rouen Cathedral">Rouen Cathedral</a>\n</td>\n<td><a href="/wiki/Rouen"
